article_content: New York City has long struggled with a massive rat population, with millions of rodents making their home in the urban landscape. City officials have experimented with numerous eradication strategies over the years. A relatively recent innovation in pest control involves injecting carbon monoxide gas into rat burrows—a method that has proven highly effective, virtually eliminating all of the affected burrows in designated areas. Matt Deodato, owner of Urban Pest Management, reports that he has eliminated thousands of rats using this technique. Deodato observes that local residents have become so accustomed to rats that people often brush them aside while sitting on park benches. Despite this familiarity, many New Yorkers are still grateful for pest controllers like Deodato, sometimes rewarding their efforts with coffee, pastries, or even beer to show appreciation, as rats impact businesses throughout the city. Deodato also admires the resourcefulness of rats, describing them as resilient creatures that are strong swimmers, quick to breed, agile, inquisitive, and adept at gnawing through various materials. He considers them impressive survivors. Bethany Brookshire, author of 'Pests: How Humans Create Animal Villains,' has likened squirrels to 'rats with better PR,' suggesting that our aversion to rats stems partly from cultural perceptions about animals associated with lower social status. While some of rats' negative reputation is deserved—given their destructive habits, tendency to bite, and contamination of food—they also cost the U.S. economy billions yearly, with one estimate placing annual damage at $19 billion. Public health experts point out that humans are naturally conditioned to avoid animals that can carry disease, such as rats, which are known to spread bacteria and viruses. Nonetheless, rats are also surprisingly intelligent and social creatures, capable of behaviors like being ticklish or even driving miniature cars in experiments. While extermination efforts continue, many people prefer methods that are quick and humane. Carbon monoxide stands out as a relatively painless solution compared to poisons, which not only cause prolonged suffering for rats but can poison other animals that eat the contaminated carcasses. Carbon monoxide, by contrast, does not carry that same risk of secondary poisoning, but it is lethal to humans and pets, so its use is limited to outdoor environments. Some critics are uneasy with the carbon monoxide method, especially when pest controllers must use additional techniques to deal with escaping rats. Nevertheless, Deodato claims that the majority of New Yorkers support these aggressive efforts to reduce the rat population. Urban ecology scholars point out that rats thrive primarily because of human waste and abundance of accessible food, making their prevalence largely an issue of human behavior. Michael Parsons, a researcher, has argued that unless food sources are curbed, rats' phenomenal reproductive ability—up to seven litters and dozens of offspring per year per pair—makes population control nearly impossible. Both Deodato and Parsons agree: improving sanitation to limit food and shelter for rats is the most effective long-term strategy for reducing their numbers.
translated_content: New York har länge kämpat med ett massivt råttproblem, med miljontals gnagare som bosatt sig i staden. Myndigheterna har provat många olika utrotningsmetoder genom åren. En förhållandevis ny teknik är att pumpa in kolmonoxidgas i råttbon—en metod som har visat sig mycket effektiv och nästan helt fått bort råttbon i vissa områden. Matt Deodato, ägare av Urban Pest Management, säger att han har avlivat tusentals råttor med den här metoden. Enligt Deodato har New York-borna vant sig så mycket vid råttor att folk ibland bara sparkar bort dem när de sitter på parkbänkar. Trots det är många ändå tacksamma för skadedjursbekämpare som Deodato och visar uppskattning med kaffe, bakverk eller ibland till och med öl—råttorna påverkar ju stadens företag. Deodato visar också viss beundran för råttornas smarthet och beskriver dem som motståndskraftiga—de är starka simmare, förökar sig snabbt, är smidiga, nyfikna och bra på att gnaga sig genom olika material. Han anser faktiskt att de är imponerande överlevare. Bethany Brookshire, författare till 'Pests: How Humans Create Animal Villains', har kallat ekorrar för 'råttor med bättre PR' och menar att vårt äckel för råttor delvis handlar om hur vi ser på djur med lägre status. Även om råttor har dåligt rykte, inte minst för att de förstör saker, biter och smutsar ner mat, orsakar de också enorma kostnader—uppskattningsvis 19 miljarder dollar årligen i USA. Folkhälsoexperter påpekar att människor är programmerade att undvika djur som kan sprida sjukdomar, och råttor är kända för att bära på bakterier och virus. Trots detta är råttor också smarta och sociala—de kan till exempel vara kittliga eller köra små bilar i experiment. De flesta föredrar effektiva och humana sätt att bekämpa råttor. Kolmonoxid är smidigare och skonsammare än gift, som ofta innebär långsamt lidande och riskerar att förgifta andra djur som kanske äter de döda råttorna. Kolmonoxid saknar dessa sekundära risker, men är farligt för människor och husdjur och får därför bara användas utomhus. Vissa är kritiska till kolmonoxidmetoden, speciellt när råttbekämpare ibland måste ta till andra metoder för råttor som försöker fly. article_content: Two men who were intoxicated broke into a police van for amusement, only to find themselves accidentally locked inside. Jeffrey Olson, 22, and Ryan Letchford, 21, had attended a party on Friday night when they noticed the empty patrol vehicle. Deciding to climb inside, they started to play with the police equipment and took pictures of each other pretending to be arrested. Their misadventure became real when they found themselves unable to get out and, eventually, ended up in handcuffs. The police discovered the pair in South Jersey, Philadelphia, in the early morning hours and arrested them. Olson and Letchford were charged with attempted theft of a motor vehicle, public drunkenness, and criminal mischief. According to Constable Mike Connor, whose van was involved, the men had come from a party at a condominium in Radnor. It is believed they entered through an unlocked door. Once inside, they smoked cigarettes, spat on the ground, and took more photos pretending to be arrested. After realizing they were trapped, the men unsuccessfully tried to break through the metal barrier separating the back of the van from the driver's area, according to police. A concerned friend, unable to find them at the party, discovered them inside the van but could not open the door, which apparently had an automatic locking mechanism. He called the police at 3:57 a.m. and Constable Connor arrived to arrest the pair. Officers found cigarette butts and a large amount of saliva inside the van.

article_content: Summit Ghimire, founder of Outpace, an SEO agency, assists national and enterprise businesses in achieving their revenue goals. Following a series of natural disasters and humanitarian crises in 2023, philanthropy has become increasingly prominent. For small businesses, giving back to their communities is a natural development. According to SCORE, small businesses contribute 250% more to local nonprofits and causes than larger corporations. Despite challenges, 75% of small business owners donate on average 6% of their profits to charity. SMBs often establish their reputation through philanthropy. However, seeing charity solely as a way to manage public image can be a missed opportunity to build a deeper company culture grounded in authentic integrity and durable growth. Understanding Company Culture Defining company culture can appear challenging. Despite the abundance of research and resources, information overload can cause hesitation. Still, company culture is essentially the set of shared values, goals, attitudes, and practices that define an organization. Much like individual personality, it shapes how employees interact and make decisions. Core elements of company culture include: • WHY: The organization's mission and vision, representing its driving purpose. • WHAT: The core values and beliefs forming its ethical framework. • HOW: The norms and expectations guiding employee behavior. Each business is shaped by its industry, location, and size, so every company's culture is unique. In small and midsize organizations, culture tends to be more adaptive and influenced by employees. SMB Advantages in Philanthropy Small and midsize businesses possess characteristics that enable them to approach philanthropy effectively. Their agility and close connections help them respond quickly to local needs. With smaller teams and flexible resources, they can create innovative partnerships and tailor projects. Strong relationships between leaders and staff foster a sense of shared values. These connections promote ownership and engagement in charitable activity. Active community relationships and a robust internal culture lead to better outcomes for those in need. While greater resources help, employee passion for local communities often extends reach the most. Best Practices for SMBs Integrating Philanthropy To incorporate philanthropy into operations, consider both philosophical and practical approaches. Key practices include: 1. Assess community needs to target your support effectively. 2. Focus efforts on areas where your business has the most impact. 3. Involve staff who have relevant experience or expertise. 4. Start with manageable projects and gradually increase your involvement. 5. Partner with like-minded businesses to expand your reach. 6. Track progress and maintain transparency to build trust and accountability. 7. Celebrate and share successes to increase enthusiasm internally and externally. Positive Impacts of Philanthropy Philanthropy benefits the community, organizations, and individuals involved. Key advantages include: • Enhanced reputation for volunteerism, supporting employee recruitment and retention. • Increased employee engagement, strengthening workplace culture and job satisfaction. • Improved community and customer relationships, boosting loyalty and growth. • Personal fulfillment and well-being through service. • Higher morale and job satisfaction, which can improve job performance and professional growth. • Expanded networking through community connections. Strengthening SMBs Combining philanthropy with company culture offers significant potential for small and midsize businesses. Internal benefits, such as a more engaged and motivated workforce, can be substantial. Philanthropy may become a core part of an organization’s identity, shaping its culture beyond goodwill alone. article_content: Greater Manchester Police and two of its officers are now being prosecuted by the Health and Safety Executive following the 2008 death of PC Ian Terry during a police training exercise. Terry was killed when a colleague accidentally shot him during a staged 'cops and robbers' drill. He was acting as a suspect with an unloaded gun when he was fatally struck by a close-range, non-lethal round fired by another officer. A 2010 inquest at Manchester's Coroner’s Court determined the death was unlawful, citing numerous failures in safety, training, and planning. The Crown Prosecution Service decided there was not enough evidence for criminal charges, but the HSE found grounds to prosecute under health and safety laws. Assistant Chief Constable Garry Shewan expressed regret to Terry’s family and said the department has since made important changes to firearm training. He also noted that eight officers still face unresolved misconduct cases, pending further information. The HSE is charging GMP for breaches of Section 2 of the Health and Safety at Work Act 1974, and is prosecuting the officers who organized and oversaw the exercise for breaches of Section 7. This action comes nearly four years after the incident, with GMP stating their ongoing cooperation and continued condolences.

article_content: Huw Allanson always dreamed of becoming a father, but his plans were jeopardized when he was diagnosed with testicular cancer at 18. After fighting the illness twice—losing his left testicle and enduring nine rounds of chemotherapy—doctors told Huw his chances of conceiving naturally were only five percent. This year brought unexpected joy. Just a week before he and his fiancée, Lizi, 32, were scheduled to begin IVF treatment, they learned they had conceived naturally. Their son, Ryan, was born in April. Huw reflected on his journey: 'One of my biggest ambitions in life was to have a family, but I was always concerned it would never happen.' After noticing a lump on his left testicle, he underwent surgery soon after diagnosis. Three months later, the cancer returned and had spread to his stomach, requiring intensive chemotherapy at Charing Cross Hospital. As a precaution against potential infertility from the treatment, he had his sperm frozen at Hammersmith Hospital. The chemotherapy was grueling, causing severe nausea, vomiting, and fatigue, but Huw ultimately responded well and has been in remission since 2004. Now, he only needs annual check-ups. Huw credits part of his treatment’s success to the drug cisplatin, developed with Cancer Research UK, which has transformed outcomes for men with advanced testicular cancer. Four years ago, Huw met Lizi at a friend’s birthday. After nearly a year of unsuccessfully trying for a baby, tests showed the couple had only a five percent chance of natural conception. They decided to pursue fertility treatment and were approved for IVF on the NHS. Amazingly, just nine days before their first IVF session, Lizi discovered she was pregnant. On April 6, Ryan was born healthy, weighing 7 pounds, 4 ounces. Huw described his son’s arrival as 'one of the best days of my life.' He and Lizi hope to grow their family further. According to Cancer Research UK, surveys show that 77 percent of men treated for testicular cancer between 1982 and 1992 were able to father children, with an additional five percent succeeding through fertility treatment. Chemotherapy poses the greatest risk to fertility, though around 70 percent of men can have children post-treatment. Martin Ledwick of Cancer Research UK highlights that fertility can return after treatment and recommends discussing sperm banking before starting therapy. CRUK offers information and support for those affected. Huw is now participating in Cancer Research UK’s campaign emphasizing the importance of research in combating cancer.

In today's fast-evolving organizational landscape, effective leadership is key to ensuring operational success—whether in small teams, large companies, state bodies, or nations. Senior individuals in these environments are often termed 'leaders' due to their roles in guiding their organizations. Leadership is a complex concept, encompassing various philosophies and styles, from democratic to autocratic approaches.

Leadership is universally valued across industries and contexts, forming the foundation of growth and achievement. As global challenges become increasingly diverse and complex, strong leadership becomes ever more vital. Enrolling in a leadership course helps individuals develop essential skills such as strategic thinking, communication, and emotional intelligence, preparing them for impactful roles.

Established in 1961 in collaboration with the Alfred P. Sloan School of Management (MIT), the Government of West Bengal, Indian industry, and the Ford Foundation, the Indian Institute of Management Calcutta (IIM Calcutta) is a renowned institution in management education. Course modules cover leadership theories, strategic thinking, decision-making, effective communication, and managing high-performing teams. article_content: A man claiming he did not receive a fair trial because the presiding judge kept falling asleep will now have an opportunity to appeal his lengthy jail sentence. Paul Duncan was sentenced to 16 years for permanently injuring a man during a 2003 brawl in Wollongong on the New South Wales south coast. His family has succeeded in securing an appeal, arguing that District Court Judge Ian Dodd frequently dozed off during the trial. Duncan's family spent years seeking to appeal his conviction, and their persistence was recently rewarded when NSW Supreme Court Justice Richard Button granted the appeal. Justice Button referred the case to the NSW Court of Criminal Appeal, citing concerns about whether Duncan's trial was properly conducted due to allegations that Judge Dodd was asleep during critical parts of the proceedings. Duncan’s mother, Linda Machman, testified that she heard Judge Dodd snoring during the trial. The case is set to be heard in the NSW Court of Criminal Appeal on July 17. Judge Dodd has faced similar allegations previously. In 2008, the High Court ordered a retrial for two men accused of drug smuggling, after finding that Judge Dodd, who suffered from sleep apnoea, had fallen asleep during their trial. Court officials and lawyers reportedly attempted to wake him by dropping documents loudly. The defendants, Rafael Cesan and Ruben Rivadavia, claimed their right to a fair trial was compromised. Chief Justice Robert French stated, 'Where the judge is noticeably and repeatedly asleep or inattentive during the trial, there can be a miscarriage of justice.' The High Court found a substantial miscarriage and ordered a retrial. Judge Dodd's sleep apnoea resulted in daytime fatigue and inattentiveness. At the retrial, Cesan and Rivadavia were found guilty. Paul Duncan's appeal will be heard in the NSW Court of Criminal Appeal on July 17.

Paul Duncan dömdes till 16 års fängelse för att ha orsakat en man bestående skador under ett slagsmål i Wollongong på New South Wales södra kust 2003. Hans familj har lyckats få ett överklagande beviljat och menar att distriktsdomare Ian Dodd ofta slumrade till under rättegången. Duncans familj har i flera år försökt få till stånd ett överklagande av hans dom, och deras envishet gav nyligen resultat när rättvisa Richard Button i Högsta domstolen i New South Wales godkände överklagandet. Domare Button skickade ärendet vidare till Brottmålsöverklagandedomstolen i New South Wales med hänvisning till oro över om Duncans rättegång hade hanterats korrekt då det påstås att domaren Dodd sov under viktiga delar av förhandlingen. Duncans mamma, Linda Machman, vittnade om att hon hört domaren Dodd snarka under rättegången. Ärendet ska nu behandlas i Brottmålsöverklagandedomstolen i New South Wales den 17 juli. Domare Dodd har tidigare kritiserats för liknande beteende. År 2008 beslutade Högsta domstolen om en ny rättegång för två män misstänkta för narkotikasmuggling, efter att ha funnit att domare Dodd, som led av sömnapné, hade somnat under deras rättegång. Rättstjänstemän och advokater försökte väcka honom genom att släppa dokument högljutt. De åtalade, Rafael Cesan och Ruben Rivadavia, ansåg att de inte hade fått en rättvis rättegång. Överdomare Robert French uttalade: 'Om domaren tydligt och upprepade gånger somnar eller är ouppmärksam under rättegången kan det leda till ett rättsfel.' Högsta domstolen fann att ett betydande rättsfel hade skett och beslutade om en ny rättegång. Domare Dodds sömnapné orsakade trötthet och bristande uppmärksamhet. Vid den nya rättegången fälldes Cesan och Rivadavia på nytt. Paul Duncans överklagande tas upp i Brottmålsöverklagandedomstolen i New South Wales den 17 juli.

article_content: Kate Vincent, a 29-year-old first-time mother from Newcastle, NSW, was diagnosed with incurable bowel cancer just three months after giving birth to her daughter, Charlotte. Despite being told her cancer was advanced, with tumors in her liver and lungs, Kate is determined to fight the disease so she can be there for Charlotte's milestones, especially her first day at kindergarten. Kate initially noticed a lump under her ribs but attributed it to post-pregnancy changes. It wasn’t until she took Charlotte to the doctor for a cold that Kate mentioned the lump to her GP, who suggested further tests. On Boxing Day 2014, after a CT scan, Kate received the devastating diagnosis. Supported by her husband Nathan and a strong network of family and friends, Kate has resolved to tackle her illness head-on. She sees her diagnosis as a challenge to discover new strengths within herself and refuses to let cancer define her future. With no prior symptoms and while on maternity leave from her teaching job, Kate said, 'I just thought it was hormones and my body adjusting after childbirth.' The news that her cancer was not only advanced but also incurable was a shock. However, Kate remains positive, saying she wants to prove her doctors wrong. Throughout her treatment—which includes several rounds of chemotherapy—Kate has relied on the support network around her. She says the love and practical help from her family and friends, as well as Charlotte’s easy-going temperament, make coping easier. Kate is in the process of launching a support group for mothers with life-threatening illnesses. She believes it is vital for women in similar situations to have a space to share their experiences and feelings. A fundraising page titled 'Something For Kate', started by her best friend's husband, has raised over $48,000 for Kate and Bowel Cancer Australia. Kate requested that 60% of the funds go to charity, with the rest supporting her family. She is deeply moved by the outpouring of support, which she says has raised awareness that bowel cancer can affect young people, not just older adults. Messages of encouragement from strangers have provided Kate with comfort and strength during difficult times. For her, Charlotte remains the main motivation to continue fighting, and she is determined to raise awareness and help others in similar situations.

Kate märkte först en knöl under revbenen men trodde att det handlade om förändringar efter graviditeten. Det var först när hon tog Charlotte till läkaren för en förkylning som Kate nämnde knölen för sin husläkare, som rekommenderade vidare undersökning. På annandag jul 2014, efter en datortomografi, fick Kate den förkrossande diagnosen. Med stöd av sin man Nathan och ett starkt nätverk av familj och vänner har Kate beslutat sig för att möta sjukdomen rakt på. Hon ser sin diagnos som en utmaning att upptäcka nya styrkor inom sig själv och vägrar låta cancern definiera hennes framtid. Utan några tidigare symtom och under sin mammaledighet från jobbet som lärare sade Kate: ”Jag trodde bara att det var hormoner och att kroppen återhämtade sig efter förlossningen.” Att få veta att cancern var både avancerad och obotlig var en stor chock, men Kate är ändå positiv och vill bevisa för sina läkare att de har fel. Under hela behandlingen – som inkluderar flera omgångar cellgifter – har Kate förlitat sig på stödet från dem omkring henne. Ukrainian National Guard soldiers participated in combat training with a recoilless cannon at a military training ground in northern Ukraine on Friday, November 3, 2023.

On Saturday, Russia's Defense Ministry reported that a Ukrainian missile strike had damaged a Russian ship at the Zaliv shipyard in Kerch, located in eastern Crimea. According to the ministry, Ukrainian forces launched 15 cruise missiles at the shipyard; Russian air defenses intercepted 13 missiles, but others struck the facility, damaging a vessel. The ministry did not specify which ship was involved or how severe the damage was.

Ukraine's air force commander, Mykola Oleshchuk, stated that at the time of the attack, one of Russia’s most modern Black Sea Fleet ships—capable of carrying Kalibr cruise missiles—was present at the shipyard, but he did not confirm if it was damaged.

Since Russia annexed Crimea from Ukraine in 2014, the peninsula has been central to military operations supporting the wider invasion ordered by President Vladimir Putin 20 months ago. Ukraine has intensified its targeting of naval assets in Crimea. For example, in September, a Ukrainian missile strike in Sevastopol damaged two Russian ships and injured 24 people, followed later by a strike on Russia’s naval headquarters in the city.

Commenting on the latest attack, Andriy Yermak, head of Ukraine’s presidential office, wrote on Telegram that 'life constantly proves that there won’t be (Russia’s) Black Sea fleet in Crimea.'

Meanwhile, Ukrainian officials said that a Russian missile attack in the Zaporizhzhia region on Friday night killed troops and injured civilians. The attack, reportedly involving an Iskander ballistic missile, targeted a group of soldiers during a ceremony, according to a video circulating on social media, but the numbers of casualties have not been confirmed. Defense Minister Rustem Umerov has ordered an investigation.

Previously, a missile attack on a Ukrainian village on October 5 killed 59 civilians attending a wake for a local soldier who had died fighting Russian forces.

Vilseck, Germany (CNN) — The U.S. military released around 77,000 of the roughly 87,000 detainees held during the Iraq war due to insufficient evidence, CNN has learned. Brigadier General David Quantock, who oversees detainee operations in Iraq, commented: "In most cases, if we don't have anything, eventually they'll be released." He explained that many detentions were based mainly on intelligence, which often does not meet the legal standards required in court, whether in Iraq or the United States.

According to the U.S. military, 76,985 detainees have been released out of 87,011 initially captured. A CNN investigation indicates that soldier frustration with the Army’s detainee policy may have contributed to the 2007 killings of four Iraqi men by three highly decorated Army sergeants at a Baghdad canal. Former First Sergeant John Hatley, the mission leader that day, told CNN in a letter that the detainee policy had "extensive flaws," causing ongoing frustration among soldiers. Army interrogation tapes obtained by CNN included additional complaints from soldiers regarding evidence-gathering requirements.

Despite the high rates of release, Quantock asserted that soldiers are capable of collecting basic evidence at crime scenes. "We're asking them to take basic evidence, which they've been trained to do. We've got the greatest soldiers in the world. And I don't accept that they can't take basic evidence off of a crime scene," he said.

When questioned about the large number of releases despite supposed ease of evidence collection, Quantock replied: "It took us a while to realize, it goes back to my point of we were trying to make the fight fit the Army as opposed to have the Army fit the fight. Often we thought the insurgency would dissipate, we were working closely with the government of Iraq, and trying to improve Iraqi security forces, but ultimately it didn’t work out very well. We had to get better at taking evidence off the crime scene."

A memo dated January 9, 2005, set forth detailed standards for evidence soldiers needed to detain suspected insurgents. These standards remained in effect through the end of 2008. The memo specified that evidence should include photos of the physical evidence, the detainee at the crime scene or place of apprehension, and the detainee alongside the evidence. It also required statements from first-hand witnesses. At the start of this year, regulations became stricter, requiring an arrest warrant signed by an Iraqi judge under a new security agreement with Iraq.

Referring to the canal killings, Quantock said to CNN: "There's never an excuse to execute anyone. They become judge, jury and executioner."

Vilseck, Tyskland (CNN) — Den amerikanska militären frigav omkring 77 000 av de cirka 87 000 frihetsberövade under Irakkriget på grund av otillräckliga bevis, uppger CNN. Brigadgeneral David Quantock, som ansvarar för fånghanteringen i Irak, kommenterade: "I de flesta fall, om vi inte har något, kommer de så småningom att släppas." Han förklarade att många frihetsberövanden primärt byggde på underrättelser, vilket ofta inte möter de juridiska kraven i domstol – vare sig i Irak eller i USA.

Enligt den amerikanska militären har 76 985 frihetsberövade släppts av de 87 011 som initialt tillfångatogs. En CNN-undersökning visar att frustration bland soldater över arméns policy för frihetsberövanden kan ha bidragit till dödandet av fyra irakiska män av tre högt dekorerade armésergeanter vid en kanal i Bagdad 2007. Före detta förste sergeant John Hatley, som ledde uppdraget, uppgav i ett brev till CNN att policyn hade "omfattande brister" som ofta frustrerade soldater. Arméförhörsband, som CNN fått tillgång till, innehöll fler klagomål från soldater om reglerna kring bevisinsamling.

Trots det höga antalet frigivna menade Quantock att soldater är tränade för att samla in grundläggande bevis från brottsplatser: "Vi ber dem samla in grundläggande bevis, det har de utbildats för. Vi har världens bästa soldater. Och jag accepterar inte att de inte kan ta grundläggande bevis från en brottsplats," sade han.

På frågan varför så många ändå släppts trots påstådd enkelhet i bevisinsamling svarade Quantock: "Det tog oss tid att inse att vi försökte anpassa striden till armén istället för armén till striden. Ofta trodde vi att upproret skulle avta, vi samarbetade nära med Iraks regering och försökte rusta upp deras säkerhetsstyrkor, men till slut gick det inte särskilt bra. Vi behövde helt enkelt bli bättre på att samla in bevis från brottsplatser."

Ett PM från den 9 januari 2005 fastställde detaljerade beviskrav för att soldater skulle få frihetsberöva misstänkta upprorsmän, krav som gällde till slutet av 2008. I dokumentet står att bevis ska inkludera foton av fysiska bevis, den frihetsberövade på brottsplatsen eller platsen där denne greps samt tillsammans med bevisen, och att uttalanden från direkt vittnen krävs. Vid årets början skärptes reglerna: nu krävs ett gripandeorder undertecknat av en irakisk domare enligt ett nytt säkerhetsavtal med Irak.

Om dödandet vid kanalen sade Quantock till CNN: "Det finns aldrig någon ursäkt för att avrätta någon. Då blir de både domare, jury och bödel."

Just a week after their defeat to Australia in the ODI World Cup final, Team India has already begun preparations for the next major tournament: the T20 World Cup, which will be held in the United States and the West Indies in seven months. Both India and Australia, the two ODI World Cup finalists, have started a five-match T20 series to ready themselves for the upcoming international event.

In the opening T20 hosted in Visakhapatnam, India achieved their highest-ever successful run chase in T20 Internationals in a dramatic last-ball victory over Australia. Emerging Indian players demonstrated their temperament and resolve under pressure: Suryakumar Yadav hit a rapid 80 off 42 balls, Ishan Kishan added 58 off 39 balls, and Rinku Singh finished with a crucial unbeaten 22 to help India secure the win. Although victorious, India’s bowling performance in the middle overs was less convincing, something that head coach VVS Laxman and his staff will need to address. Mukesh Kumar stood out for his work in the death overs, even though he didn't take a wicket.

Arshdeep Singh may have fond memories of the Greenfield Stadium in Thiruvananthapuram, where he previously took three wickets in swinging conditions, helping restrict South Africa to 106. However, the conditions for the current match may not be as favorable to bowlers.

Australia’s Josh Inglis and Steve Smith impressed with the bat, scoring a century and a half-century, respectively, but their inexperienced bowling lineup struggled, which could lead to personnel changes for the next game. Glenn Maxwell, Travis Head, and Adam Zampa are available for selection after missing the first match.

Weather remains a concern following heavy rainfall in parts of Thiruvananthapuram, though the Greenfield Stadium was mostly unaffected. The Australian team practiced on Saturday afternoon in hot and humid conditions as they prepared for the second T20.

article_content: The X-Files: The Official Archives continues as a celebrated sci-fi book series, carrying forward the legacy of the iconic television show. In 2020, io9 spotlighted Paul Terry’s creative vision with the first volume, documenting the detailed case files of Agents Mulder and Scully. Today, on X-Files creator Chris Carter’s birthday, io9 announces the follow-up. The next book in the series, The X-Files: The Official Archives: Volume II: Extraterrestrial Activity and the Syndicate, is an officially licensed, richly illustrated volume exploring Mulder and Scully’s encounters with aliens and the Syndicate. The first volume had covered cryptids, biological anomalies, and psychic phenomena. Featuring archival images and carefully recreated case reports, Volume II revisits iconic episodes like “Deep Throat,” “Jose Chung’s From Outer Space,” “Fight the Future,” and “Musings of a Cigarette Smoking Man.” The book aims to immerse readers in the detailed world of The X-Files. In an io9 interview, author Paul Terry revealed that he envisioned the project as a multi-book series from the start. The initial book aimed at 'monster of the week' cases, with sequels designed to cover the overarching mythology, including UFO and Syndicate conspiracies. Terry emphasized the importance of fan support for the series’ continuation and expressed gratitude for their encouragement. He enjoyed leaving subtle hints about future volumes in the original book. Volume II covers stories from all eleven TV seasons and the movies, combining realistic designs with in-depth narratives. Terry promises unique surprises and a more immersive experience for fans. When asked about favorite characters, Terry praised Scully and Mulder as a great duo and highlighted the complexity of antagonists like Cigarette Smoking Man, as well as performances by James Pickens Jr., Robert Patrick, Annabeth Gish, Steven Williams, Darren McGavin, and Rhys Darby. Terry identified episodes such as “Folie à Deux,” “Chinga,” “Pusher,” and “Irresistible” as some of the series’ scariest, citing the show’s ability to build suspense and emotional horror. The X-Files: The Official Archives: Volume II: Extraterrestrial Activity and the Syndicate is scheduled for release by Abrams Books in fall 2024.

article_content: Caroline Jordan, head of Headington School in Oxford, has expressed deep concern about the influence of 'textspeak'—abbreviated language commonly used in text messages and on social media—on students' proficiency in written English. She contends that widespread use of shorthand like 'gr8' and 'm8' is contributing to weaker spelling, grammar, and more limited vocabularies among students. Jordan highlights the challenge facing teachers: protecting the quality of English instruction as technology and informal language gain prominence. She cites reports from teachers and examiners who increasingly observe abbreviations and slang, such as 'ur' for 'your' and 'I donno huu u r,' appearing in schoolwork and exams. Research supports these concerns. Coventry University found a connection between fewer texting punctuation mistakes and better spelling skills, while a study from Pennsylvania State University observed that frequent use of shortened words in text messages was linked to lower grammar test scores. Jordan questions a government plan to introduce a new maths qualification for sixth-formers not studying A-level maths, suggesting instead that an English assessment would be more beneficial. She emphasizes that strong English skills are crucial for employment in today's competitive environment because errors in spelling or grammar can harm job prospects. She also recommends that the maths syllabus for sixth-form students should have a more practical focus, including essential financial skills and an understanding of concepts like interest rates and mortgages. Jordan advocates for traditional methods in teaching English to help preserve standards in spelling and grammar. She warns that excessive time spent on social media, rather than reading, could limit students' vocabulary growth. A poll of 500 teachers revealed that many students use informal expressions and abbreviations in formal writing, with examples like calling Macbeth 'pure mental' or Romeo a 'numpty.' Educators stress the need for students to learn when informal language is appropriate and when standard English is required.

article_content: A large hostel for refugees has been established in Calais, France, to provide shelter and safety as they await opportunities to cross the Channel to Britain. The hostel, located in a converted dockers' social club, accommodates up to 120 asylum seekers—mainly from Africa and the Middle East. Refugees sleep closely together on mattresses placed on the floor, making it difficult to walk between them. The £70,000 winter shelter is equipped with running water, heating, and a sanitary block. Mayor Natacha Bouchart opened the shelter in response to a significant increase in the number of migrants attempting to cross the Channel. To cope with cold winter conditions, refugees are provided with sleeping bags. Signs posted inside the shelter prohibit drinking, smoking, and fighting. The shelter operates as a temporary refuge during periods of freezing weather, from 6:30pm to 9am. This facility is similar to the former Sangatte asylum center, which closed in 2002. The shelter received over 100 Syrian, Eritrean, and Afghan migrants when it opened last Thursday, many seeking refuge after storms destroyed their tents near the Channel ferry terminal. The opening has sparked protests from some residents, including a group known as 'Save Calais,' who oppose the influx of migrants. The local council has hired a security company to patrol the seafront and prevent migrants from entering beach huts. Many migrants continue to sleep rough in sand dunes and parks. Mayor Bouchart has noted that there are 10 to 15 illegal squats in the town, which are being targeted for eviction. The largest squat, on Boulevard Victor Hugo, is owned by an 80-year-old woman and is home to up to 90 migrants, some supported by the British group No Borders. Sub Prefect Alain Gerard stated that all evictions will be carried out with humanity and respect.

article_content: Only one in six mothers prepares a meal from scratch every day, often due to a lack of confidence and limited time to cook. Food campaigners suggest that grandparents share some responsibility, as many have not passed on their cooking skills to the next generation. Instead, children are frequently served convenience foods such as chicken nuggets, sausages, and pizza, according to research by the Department of Health. Many mothers report choosing these options because they are quick to prepare and popular with their children. The study found that just 16 percent of mothers cooked a meal from scratch daily. More than half of the mothers surveyed said they used basic ingredients to cook four times a week or less. A lack of time was cited by 71 percent of mothers, according to the Change4Life Be Food Smart campaign, as the main reason for serving convenience foods. Only 90 out of the 2,000 mothers surveyed said they never used convenience foods. A quarter of mothers said they either did not know how to cook or lacked ideas and confidence in meal preparation. Over a third of families (36 percent) order takeaway or eat out once a week. The survey highlights that a lack of time and confidence leads to children often being served quick meals like pizza. Child nutrition expert and author Annabel Karmel told the Daily Telegraph that time-saving ingredients, such as pre-chopped vegetables, pre-cooked noodles, and boil-in-the-bag rice, can help parents prepare good meals quickly. She suggested that parents could make marinated chicken under the grill as an alternative to chicken nuggets, emphasizing that a nutritious meal can be made in 15 minutes. Karmel further remarked that cooking from scratch requires some confidence, but many lack cooking skills because their parents did not cook and cooking classes in schools were discontinued. She also noted that parents often give up when their children are fussy eaters. Azmina Govindji of the British Dietetic Association said it is understandable that eating habits evolve and that busy mothers today may not approach cooking family meals as their own mothers did. However, she warned that many takeaways and processed foods contain high levels of salt, sugar, and saturated fat. She encouraged shoppers to choose healthier options and learn how to quickly prepare meals themselves, as this increases awareness of ingredients and helps families avoid 'hidden nasties'.

article_content: The Court of Appeal, Abuja Division, on Thursday affirmed Senator Kaka Shehu Lawan of the All Progressives Congress as the winner of the February 25, 2023, senatorial election for the Borno Central seat. The court stated that the appellants, Barrister Mohammed Kumalia and the Peoples Democratic Party, failed to prove their case to nullify the election. The three-judge panel, led by Hon. Justice Abraham Georgewill and including Folashade Ojo and Peter Obiora, upheld Senator Lawan’s election as Borno Central senator. Earlier, the National Assembly Election Petition Tribunal in Maiduguri dismissed the petitions and confirmed Lawan’s election on September 8, 2023. Lawan received 135,043 votes, while Kumalia got 63,338. Kumalia and his party alleged the Independent National Electoral Commission’s results were affected by irregularities, seeking to have the election nullified. After the verdict, Lawan told journalists in Maiduguri that he was satisfied with the judgement and called on his opponent to withdraw from politics and refrain from filing unsuccessful petitions. Attempts to reach Barrister Kumalia for comment were unsuccessful.

article_content: Portland’s Pearl District has transformed from a warehouse zone into a thriving hub of arts, dining, and entertainment. Visitors will find an array of art galleries, enjoy seasonal sweets like pumpkin pie cupcakes, and spend their evenings at the theater. The Gerding Theater at the Armory is a highlight, having undergone a $36 million eco-conscious renovation. This venue now hosts major shows such as Portland Center Stage’s spotlight on R. Buckminster Fuller. For shoppers seeking artistic gifts at accessible prices, the annual student sale at the Pacific Northwest College of Art features sophisticated works—monotypes, screen-printed cards, jewelry, paintings, and metal sculptures—crafted by emerging artists. Art lovers can also explore the DeSoto Building, which houses four galleries and the Museum of Contemporary Craft. The museum’s Holiday Shoppe opens in early winter with a range of handmade ornaments and distinctive gifts. The Pearl’s dining scene is equally diverse. Ten 01 offers wild rice–smoked duck breast next to the Gerding Theater, Isabel serves flavorful brown rice and tofu bowls with peanut sauce, and 50 Plates delivers creative takes on American favorites. Cupcake Jones, a bakery in the neighborhood, makes a popular pumpkin pie cupcake with pumpkin cream filling—a perfect treat before Thanksgiving. Families can catch productions at Oregon Children’s Theatre, such as the lively staging of Roald Dahl’s ‘James and the Giant Peach,’ featuring special effects and clever humor. Artists Repertory Theatre brings both beloved classics and new works by local writers to its two intimate stages, including comedic productions like ‘Holidazed’ that lampoon holiday traditions. Indie film fans will appreciate the Northwest Film Center’s lineup of curated screenings and the Portland International Film Festival, which presents around 100 films from over 30 countries each February. And for home design enthusiasts, MyHomeIdeas.com hosts a monthly Room Makeover Giveaway.

article_content: A newly formed group called 'Putin's Army,' consisting of female supporters, is urging young, smart, and attractive women in Russia to express their support for Prime Minister Vladimir Putin by submitting homemade video clips. The group's campaign, launched on popular Russian social networking sites VKontakte and LiveJournal, claims to have gathered around 800 supporters ahead of the March 2012 presidential election. The individuals behind the initiative have remained anonymous, but the group's first video features a student named Diana declaring her admiration for Putin. Diana says, 'I'm crazy about the person who has changed our country. He is a prominent politician and an awesome man. His name is Vladimir Putin. Millions of people adore and trust him.' The group is hosting a contest for the most original video of women tearing something—or someone—in the name of Putin, with submissions posted on VKontakte. The creator of the winning video will receive an iPad 2. Diana encourages, 'Tell us what YOU would do for your president.' Putin, Russia's president from 2000 to 2008 and now prime minister, has yet to announce whether he or the current president, Dmitry Medvedev, will run in the 2012 election. Both have said the decision will be made together soon. In her video, set to club music, Diana walks along Moscow streets in high heels and a black outfit, holding an iPhone. The camera occasionally zooms in on her, and later, with friends by the Moscow River, she writes 'I will tear off for Putin' on a white tank top in red lipstick. The video ends with her ripping the tank top, briefly revealing an undergarment. The provocative video has attracted hundreds of thousands of views online since its release and has inspired parodies. 'Putin's Army' announced that the contest, running until August 26, may turn every participant into an Internet star. Public acts of support for Putin are not unprecedented. Recently, supporters sang 'Blueberry Hill'—a song Putin previously performed—outside the main government building in Moscow. Last October, female journalism students from Moscow State University posed for a bikini calendar as a birthday tribute to Putin. Putin has publicly denounced such attempts to glorify his persona or use his likeness in advertising, insisting the attention embarrasses him. He has consistently distanced himself from various tributes dedicated to him. Some Russian analysts suggest these public campaigns are designed to appeal to young voters in advance of pivotal elections: parliamentary polls in December and the presidential election in March 2012.

article_content: This year, Independence Day celebrations in Texas will be noticeably quieter, as severe, ongoing drought has prompted widespread restrictions on fireworks throughout much of the state. Dozens of counties have limited small fireworks such as firecrackers and bottle rockets, and cities including San Antonio, Austin, Amarillo, and Lubbock have canceled their public Fourth of July displays due to high fire risk. According to Chris Angerer, deputy chief of operations at the Lubbock fire department, temperatures remain in the triple digits with little sign of relief. Wildfires have already entered city limits, destroying three homes, and the prolonged absence of rain has left grasslands dry and barren. Deborah Foster, a San Antonio fire department engineer, acknowledged that canceling fireworks is disappointing for many but emphasized that it is necessary to protect the public from the risk of devastating grass fires. Since November, wildfires have burned nearly 3.3 million acres across Texas—an area larger than Connecticut. Currently, outdoor burning is banned in 235 of the state's 254 counties, the highest number on record according to the Texas Forest Service. Texas has been hit hardest among a swath of states suffering from severe drought stretching from Arizona to Florida. More than 90% of Texas is experiencing 'extreme' or 'exceptional' drought, according to the U.S. Drought Monitor at the University of Nebraska-Lincoln, with 72% classified as 'exceptional' as of Thursday. Areas in northeast Texas near Fort Worth have seen some rainfall, but record dry conditions persist elsewhere. On Louis Grissom's farm in Seminole, cotton and peanut crops are stunted, pastures have been scorched, and a single fire in June killed over 300 cows. Grissom reports difficulties even irrigating his peanut crops and says the soil has been too dry to absorb water effectively. The U.S. Department of Agriculture declared disasters in 213 Texas counties on Wednesday, along with seven parishes in adjacent Louisiana, following significant losses in pastures, grain, and forage crops. This disaster declaration makes farmers eligible for federal aid. The Texas agricultural extension service estimates state farmers have lost $62 million, including buildings, crops, livestock, and over 4,100 miles of fencing destroyed by fire, with fencing replacement costs up to $10,000 per mile. Authorities in Arizona and New Mexico are grappling with extensive wildfires as well. Near Los Alamos, New Mexico, a blaze has burned more than 70,000 acres, but firefighters have made some progress in limiting its spread. Water scarcity is also worsening in West Texas oil towns like Midland and Odessa. Reservoirs operated by the Colorado River Municipal Water District are running dangerously low, prompting new water-use restrictions. Midland's water allotment was cut by 20% this year, and its main source, the O.H. Ivie Reservoir, could be depleted by December 2012 if drought persists, according to municipal spokeswoman Tasa Watts. Residents are now limited to watering lawns twice weekly between dusk and midmorning, pool refills are prohibited, and restaurants will serve water only upon request. Violating these rules can result in fines up to $500. Tom Spencer of the Texas Forest Service says 2011 is one of the driest years since 1895. Although rainfall could bring temporary relief, only a major shift in weather patterns or a tropical storm could break the drought, which is unlikely before summer ends. In April, Governor Rick Perry called on Texans to pray for rain. Despite these appeals, conditions remain dire, and Tropical Storm Arlene—recently making landfall in eastern Mexico—will likely provide little help as high-pressure systems steer weather events away from Texas. For farmers like Grissom, cotton yields could fall to one-fifth of previous years, and there is not enough hay for cattle as harvest nears. With little time remaining, many hope for divine intervention to bring much-needed rain.

Dussintals län har infört begränsningar för små fyrverkerier, som smällare och raketer, och städer som San Antonio, Austin, Amarillo och Lubbock har ställt in sina offentliga fyrverkerishower på fjärde juli på grund av den höga brandrisken. Skogsbränder har redan nått in i stadskärnor och förstört tre hem, och den långvariga avsaknaden av regn har gjort gräsmarkerna torra och öde. Deborah Foster, ingenjör vid brandkåren i San Antonio, medger att inställda fyrverkerier är en besvikelse för många men betonar att det är nödvändigt för att skydda allmänheten mot förödande gräsbränder. Just nu råder förbud mot utomhusbränning i 235 av delstatens 254 län, det högsta antalet någonsin enligt Texas Forest Service. Texas har drabbats hårdast av flera delstater som lider av svår torka från Arizona till Florida. Mer än 90 % av Texas upplever "extrem" eller "exceptionell" torka enligt U.S. Drought Monitor vid University of Nebraska-Lincoln, med 72 % klassificerat som "exceptionell" per torsdagen. Områden i nordöstra Texas nära Fort Worth har fått viss nederbörd, men rekordtorrt väder råder på andra håll. På Louis Grissoms gård i Seminole är bomulls- och jordnötsodlingarna förkrympta, betesmarkerna har bränts av, och en enda brand i juni dödade över 300 kor. Grissom berättar att det är svårt att ens vattna jordnötsodlingen, och marken är så torr att vattnet knappt tränger ner. Det amerikanska jordbruksdepartementet utfärdade katastrofförklaring i 213 län i Texas i onsdags, samt i sju församlingar i angränsande Louisiana, efter stora förluster av betesmark, spannmål och fodergrödor. Katastrofförklaringen gör jordbrukarna berättigade till federalt stöd. Texas jordbruksförlängningstjänst uppskattar att delstatens jordbrukare har förlorat 62 miljoner dollar, inklusive byggnader, grödor, boskap och över 4 100 miles stängsel förstört av bränder – där byggandet kan kosta upp till 10 000 dollar per mile. Myndigheter i Arizona och New Mexico kämpar också mot omfattande bränder. I närheten av Los Alamos, New Mexico, har en brand bränt över 70 000 tunnland, men brandmän har gjort vissa framsteg i att begränsa spridningen. Vattenbristen förvärras även i västra Texas oljestäder som Midland och Odessa. Reservoarer som förvaltas av Colorado River Municipal Water District håller på att sina, vilket tvingat fram nya restriktioner för vattenanvändning. Midlands vattenkvot minskades med 20 % i år och huvudkällan, O.H. Ivie-reservoaren, kan vara tömd till december 2012 om torkan fortsätter, enligt kommunens talesperson Tasa Watts. Invånare får nu vattna gräsmattor endast två gånger per vecka mellan skymning och förmiddag, det är förbjudet att fylla pooler, och restauranger serverar endast vatten vid förfrågan. Brott mot reglerna kan leda till böter på upp till 500 dollar. Tom Spencer från Texas Forest Service säger att 2011 är ett av de torraste åren sedan 1895. Även om regn kan ge tillfällig lättnad kan bara en större förändring av vädret eller en tropisk storm bryta torkan, vilket sannolikt inte sker förrän efter sommaren. I april uppmanade guvernör Rick Perry Texasbor att be för regn. Trots dessa böner är läget fortfarande allvarligt, och Tropiska stormen Arlene – som nyligen nådde land i östra Mexiko – väntas inte hjälpa då högtryck styr regnområden bort från Texas. För jordbrukare som Grissom kan bomullsskörden bli bara en femtedel jämfört med tidigare år, och det finns inte tillräckligt med hö till boskapen när skörden närmar sig. Med lite tid kvar hoppas många på gudomligt ingripande för att få regn.

article_content: UK Home Secretary Suella Braverman has sparked controversy by referring to rough sleeping in tents as a 'lifestyle choice' and promising to introduce measures to tackle homeless encampments. She argued that failing to address this issue could see public spaces overtaken by tents, potentially bringing about increased crime, substance abuse, and unsanitary conditions. Braverman also pointed out that many rough sleepers in tents are foreign nationals, though she stressed that the government would still help those facing genuine homelessness. Her remarks have drawn sharp criticism from charities and politicians across the spectrum, who accuse her of blaming the vulnerable for broader government failures. Ex-Conservative MP Ben Howlett condemned the idea of fining charities that provide tents as 'actually evil.' Labour’s Yvette Cooper criticized Braverman for focusing on tents rather than the rising rates of homelessness, while Liberal Democrat Alistair Carmichael described the government’s stance as 'grim politics.' Shelter, the homelessness charity, argued that living on the streets is never a choice and called the government’s approach inhumane. The charity noted an estimated 271,000 people are currently without a home in England, including 123,000 children. Figures show the number of people sleeping rough in England has risen for the first time in years; a snapshot last autumn found 3,069 people sleeping outside—a 26% increase from the previous year and 74% higher than in 2010. The British Red Cross reported a 140% surge in refugees experiencing destitution since August, prompting them to hand out tents and sleeping bags. Charity leaders argue that measures targeting tents would worsen the problem and push vulnerable people further into hardship. They urge the government to boost investment in housing support, not restrict basic shelters. Braverman suggested a new civil offense, where charities could face penalties if those given tents are later seen as causing a public nuisance. The Home Office highlighted the previously announced Antisocial Behaviour Action Plan as part of ongoing efforts to address the issue, although specifics about the King’s Speech were not disclosed. Despite prior government pledges to end rough sleeping by January 2025, officials now admit this goal is unlikely to be achieved.

article_content: A year after Egypt's revolution ousted a longtime dictator, tensions have risen between Egypt and the United States, threatening to disrupt military aid. Egyptian authorities, investigating civil society organizations, recently announced that 43 foreigners—19 of them Americans—working for such groups would face prosecution. Officials claim these NGOs contributed to unrest and cite foreign interference as the cause. Authorities conducted 17 raids on the offices of 10 organizations, including U.S.-based Freedom House, National Democratic Institute, and International Republican Institute. Among those charged is Sam LaHood, son of U.S. Transportation Secretary Ray LaHood. Journalist Ashraf Khalil noted his surprise, suggesting it is unusual to target the relative of a high-ranking official, and expressing worries that the Egyptian government might believe the accused are spies. Many analysts were surprised that Egypt would challenge the U.S. during this sensitive period after the revolution. The case has no straightforward solutions and increases bilateral tensions. Egypt alleges that pro-democracy organizations received illegal foreign financing and operated without proper licenses, although some groups worked informally under former President Hosni Mubarak. U.S. State Department spokeswoman Victoria Nuland stated the targeted groups did not fund candidates or parties, adding that their activities were not new. The U.S. views the prosecutions as a crackdown on democracy and warned that over $1.3 billion in military aid, which is tied to Egypt's progress toward democracy, could be at risk. Top U.S. officials, including Secretary of State Hillary Clinton and Defense Secretary Leon Panetta, criticized the move. Several members of Congress called for aid to be withheld until the NGOs can resume operations. White House spokesman Jay Carney said these actions could seriously affect the relationship and assistance programs with Egypt. Nuland would not comment on potential consequences but acknowledged the difficult situation. The situation escalated when Senator John McCain said an Egyptian military delegation canceled high-level meetings in Washington at short notice and went back to Egypt. Both sides now appear to be entrenched, lacking easy solutions, according to Marina Ottaway from the Carnegie Endowment. Ottaway noted that the U.S. has limited influence since it has no direct relationship with the political leadership of the Muslim Brotherhood, now the dominant party in Egypt's parliament. She suggested that Egypt will need to resolve the legal cases quickly to protect its ties with the U.S. Isobel Coleman of the Council on Foreign Relations commented that nationalism may be motivating the Egyptian government's stance. Recent protests in Cairo's Tahrir Square, fueled partly by deadly soccer riots, show continuing unrest. Coleman emphasized that governments often blame outsiders for domestic problems, a pattern repeated in Egypt. Accusations of activists receiving foreign funds precede the current government, as shown by the earlier case of dissident Saad Eddin Ibrahim. Ashraf Khalil expects Egyptian courts may eventually ease off the prosecution of foreigners, but worries about harsher consequences for local Egyptian democracy groups. CNN's Ted Barrett contributed to this report.

article_content: Exhausted and losing weight, Nicky Rigby believed her symptoms were due to the stress of giving birth just five months earlier. Tragically, she was unaware that these were signs of undiagnosed Type 1 diabetes, which ultimately took her life at age 26. Miss Rigby was found unconscious at home by her fiancé, Mark Wilson, and died shortly after. An inquest later found that she had been suffering from Type 1 diabetes, leading to diabetic ketoacidosis—a life-threatening complication resulting from a lack of insulin. Her family later discovered that Nicky had displayed many symptoms of undiagnosed Type 1 diabetes, such as fatigue and weight loss, but these were mistaken for the normal exhaustion and weight changes experienced by new mothers. When Mr. Wilson took her to the doctor, Nicky was prescribed iron tablets, which did not address her actual condition. The coroner concluded that diabetic ketoacidosis caused her death. Diabetic ketoacidosis can occur when individuals with diabetes do not receive enough insulin. High blood glucose levels cause the body to break down body tissue for energy, producing poisonous chemicals called ketones. If left untreated, these can cause severe dehydration, coma, swelling of the brain, and can be fatal. It is unclear how long Nicky had undiagnosed diabetes or if it was triggered by her pregnancy. Mark Wilson, devastated by her loss, now shares Nicky's story to raise awareness of diabetes among new mothers and encourage others to request testing if they experience similar symptoms. 'Nicky was a natural mother to Lily. She loved being a mum, even though she was often exhausted,' said Mr. Wilson. He recalled that the iron tablets did not help, but Nicky simply believed her tiredness was normal for new mothers. On Mr. Wilson’s birthday in July 2012, Nicky began complaining of a stomach bug. She decided to rest at home while he went out with friends and took their daughter to his mother’s house. When he returned home, he discovered Nicky unconscious, surrounded by vomit. He immediately called emergency services and attempted CPR, but she could not be revived. Around 300,000 people in the UK have Type 1 diabetes, which differs from the more common Type 2 version. Common symptoms include excessive thirst, frequent urination (especially at night), fatigue, weight loss, and loss of muscle mass. Symptoms can develop quickly, sometimes over days or weeks. Later stages can involve vomiting and heavy breathing, which require urgent medical attention. The Cheshire inquest found that Nicky’s death could have been prevented with insulin treatment to control her blood sugar. Mr. Wilson has kept Nicky’s memory alive for their daughter Lily, displaying photos and mementoes at home. He encourages new mothers not to ignore persistent tiredness and other symptoms. For more information about diabetes, visit www.diabetes.org.uk or call the Diabetes UK Careline at 0345 123 2399.

Hon beslöt att vila hemma medan han gick ut och tog deras dotter till sin mamma. När han kom hem upptäckte han Nicky medvetslös och omgiven av kräkningar. Vid senare stadier kan kräkningar och tung andning förekomma, vilket kräver omedelbar medicinsk vård. Rättsläkaren i Cheshire konstaterade att Nickys död hade kunnat förhindras med insulinbehandling för att kontrollera blodsockret. article_content: Jeep India has expanded its retail presence by inaugurating a new dealership, SGA Jeep, in Coimbatore, Tamil Nadu, as part of its plan to increase its dealership network to 80 by the end of 2023. Currently, Jeep India operates in 64 cities across the country with over 72 touchpoints. The new SGA Jeep dealership spans 2,100 sq ft and offers the full range of Jeep vehicles—Grand Cherokee, Wrangler, Meridian, and Compass—to the region. The dealership will also serve neighboring districts, including Erode, Nilgiris, and Tirupur. Aditya Jairaj, Jeep India Operations Head and Deputy Managing Director of Stellantis India, said, "Tamil Nadu is an economic powerhouse and an important market for Jeep India. Our partnership with SGA Jeep in Coimbatore underscores the growing demand for the Jeep brand in the region, and aligns with our goal to strengthen our service footprint across India by increasing our network to 80 dealerships by the end of 2023." The dealership not only offers sales but also features a 12-bay workshop covering 25,000 sq ft, staffed by trained service personnel and equipped with modern diagnostic and repair tools to provide world-class service. Jeep is part of Stellantis’ global portfolio, and India is the first country outside North America where Jeep manufactures four models locally for both domestic sales and exports to other right-hand drive markets. In related business updates, India has approved the first 100% foreign direct investment in the defense sector, granting Sweden’s Saab permission to set up a facility to manufacture rockets. The State Bank of India reported an 8% increase in net profit for the second quarter, driven by steady loan demand and reduced provisions, and expects continued robust loan growth. article_content: Investigators in the Abigail Hernandez kidnapping case are reportedly focusing on a storage unit located on the suspect’s property. According to sources cited by New England Cable News, this is where the teenager was held captive. The rust-colored storage container, described by neighbors as an above-ground bunker, was surrounded by crime scene tape at the time of suspect Nathaniel E. Kibby’s arrest, according to CNN affiliate WMUR. The New Hampshire Attorney General’s Office declined to comment on these reports. Assistant Attorney General Jane Hall stated that arrest and search warrant information would remain sealed for now. A probable cause hearing is scheduled for August 12, when more evidence about how Hernandez was found may be revealed. “It’s remarkable how well she’s doing,” Hall said. “Just to be able to endure what she did under any circumstances.” Hernandez, 15, sat just feet away from her alleged kidnapper during Tuesday’s arraignment. Kibby, 34, was arrested Monday and charged with felony kidnapping for allegedly confining Hernandez on October 9 with the intent to commit an offense against her, according to prosecutors. He is being held on $1 million bail. His attorney, Jesse Friedman, did not enter a plea, arguing that the charge is unclear due to the sealed arrest warrant. The judge denied a motion to unseal the warrant. Hernandez returned home last week, more than nine months after she disappeared on her way from school. The case drew national attention when she went missing at age 14, and details about her disappearance remained few after her return last Sunday. Investigators said Hernandez provided sufficient information to justify Kibby’s arrest. In a statement Friday, Hernandez’s family said they were cooperating with police and focusing on “the peace and joy of the moment of Abby’s return.” They noted Abby is resting, very tired, has lost significant weight, and is working to regain her strength. “We hope soon she will be back on solid foods,” her family said. The family thanked people who shared her sketch and hoped the ordeal would soon be over. On Monday, Hernandez expressed gratitude to those who searched for her while she was missing. “I wish that I could personally thank everyone who looked for me. My gratitude is beyond words,” she said in a statement. “It’s an incredible feeling to be home, and I believe your hopes and prayers played a major role in my release. Thank you all for the welcome home.”

Enligt källor som citerats av New England Cable News var det där tonåringen hölls fången. Den rostfärgade förrådscontainern, som grannar beskrev som en ovanjordisk bunker, var avspärrad med polistejp när Nathaniel E. Kibby greps, rapporterar CNN:s samarbetspartner WMUR. New Hampshires justitiekansli har avböjt att kommentera uppgifterna. Biträdande justitiekanslern Jane Hall meddelade att häktnings- och husrannsakningsorder förblir sekretessbelagda tills vidare. En sannolikhetshandlingsförhandling är planerad till den 12 augusti, då mer bevis om hur Hernandez hittades kan presenteras. "Det är otroligt hur bra hon mår," sa Hall. "Att ens kunna uthärda det hon gjort under vilka omständigheter som helst." Hernandez, 15, satt bara några meter från sin påstådda kidnappare vid tisdagens häktningsförhandling. Kibby, 34, greps i måndags och åtalades för grov kidnappning för att ha hållit Hernandez instängd den 9 oktober med avsikt att begå ett brott mot henne, enligt åklagare. Han hålls häktad med en borgen på 1 miljon dollar. Hans advokat, Jesse Friedman, lämnade inget svar och anmärkte att åtalet är oklart eftersom häktningsordern är förseglad. Domaren avslog en begäran om att öppna ordnern. Hernandez kom hem förra veckan, mer än nio månader efter att hon försvann på väg hem från skolan. Fallet fick nationell uppmärksamhet när hon försvann som 14-åring, och få detaljer avslöjades efter hennes återkomst i söndags. Utredare sade att Hernandez gett tillräckliga uppgifter för att motivera Kibbys gripande. I ett uttalande i fredags sade Hernandez familj att de samarbetar med polisen och fokuserar på "freden och glädjen över att Abby är tillbaka." De berättar att Abby vilar, är mycket trött, har gått ner mycket i vikt och arbetar på att återfå sin styrka. "Vi hoppas hon snart äter vanlig mat igen," sade familjen. Familjen tackade alla som delat hennes skissbild och hoppades på ett snart slut på prövningen. På måndagen uttryckte Hernandez sin tacksamhet till dem som sökte efter henne medan hon var försvunnen. "Jag önskar att jag personligen kunde tacka alla som letat efter mig. Min tacksamhet är obeskrivlig," sa hon i ett uttalande. "Det är en otrolig känsla att vara hemma, och jag tror att era förhoppningar och böner spelade en stor roll för min frigivning. Tack alla för ert välkomnande."

article_content: Russian President Vladimir Putin will participate in a virtual G20 Summit hosted by India and chaired by Prime Minister Narendra Modi on November 22. This digital event will bring together world leaders to review progress made during India’s 2023 G20 presidency. The Kremlin has confirmed that topics will include reflections on the New Delhi Summit, recent developments, the global economy, finance, climate challenges, and the role of digital transformation. Amitabh Kant, the G20 Sherpa, shared that the summit is designed to advance the implementation of previous G20 outcomes. Invitations have gone to G20 members, the African Union chairperson, nine additional guest countries, and heads of eleven international bodies. Deliberations will also reference results from the latest Voice of the Global South Summit of November 17. Prime Minister Modi recently launched DAKSHIN, a global excellence centre for the Global South, promising greater unity and representation for these countries. India sees this virtual gathering as an opportunity to further the G20’s decisions at both national and international levels, underlining its commitment to multilateral cooperation.

article_content: Tyson Foods has initiated a recall for approximately 30,000 pounds of its Fun Nuggets after reports surfaced of metal shavings in the dinosaur-shaped chicken products. The company revealed 'small, flexible metal objects' were discovered in specific 29-ounce bags and chose to recall the product as a safety measure. These affected nuggets were produced on September 5, 2023, at a single plant. Consumers can identify them by product codes 2483BRV02 07, 2483BRV02 08, 2483BRV02 09, or 2483BRV02 10, with establishment code P7211 and a best-if-used-by date of September 4, 2024. The cases display the identifiers 048153-6910 or 10000048153. This recall follows similar incidents at Tyson Foods—namely, a 2019 recall of over 36,000 pounds of chicken nuggets due to rubber pieces, traced back to a broken machine part, as reported by The New York Times, and a 2014 recall of more than 75,000 pounds over small plastic fragments discovered by customers. Many Americans enjoy dino nuggets, but some fans note there are only a couple of dinosaur shapes—often sparking debates about whether one shape is an ankylosaurus or a stegosaurus.

With its sleek, interwoven curves and futuristic, spacecraft-inspired design, the new superyacht created by Dame Zaha Hadid is poised to become the latest luxury vessel for the extremely wealthy. The design, reminiscent of Beijing’s 'Bird’s Nest' Olympic stadium, is the first superyacht project undertaken by the award-winning architect, famous for landmark works such as London’s Aquatics Centre from the 2012 Olympics.

Developed for renowned German shipbuilder Blohm+Voss, Hadid’s family of yachts includes a striking 128-meter ‘mothership’ and five customizable 90-meter vessels. The first in the series, dubbed 'Jazz', has already been transformed into a fully functional design, featuring a sharp, torpedo-like prow and an open rear deck. Each yacht can be individually tailored to its owner's preferences and is engineered to provide exceptional hydrodynamics, comfort, spatial quality, and safety.

Dame Zaha Hadid, who holds both the Pritzker Architecture Prize (2004) and the RIBA Stirling Prize (2010, 2011), is acclaimed for iconic buildings such as the MAXXI National Museum of 21st Century Arts in Rome, the Riverside Museum in Glasgow, and the Evelyn Grace Academy in London. In addition to architecture, her design portfolio includes speedboats, wine bottles, vases, cars, and jewelry. She was made a Dame Commander of the Order of the British Empire (DBE) in 2012 for her services to architecture.

Hadid’s influence extends to major sports venues; following her work on London’s Aquatics Centre, she was commissioned to design plans for Tokyo’s National Olympic Stadium, set for the 2020 Olympics. Her innovative approach continues to earn global recognition and inspire admiration in both the architectural and design worlds.

South Korea has accused China of forcibly repatriating a considerable number of North Korean defectors, echoing claims from human rights organizations that up to 600 people—mainly women—have recently been sent back. South Korean officials stated on Friday that these reports appear to be accurate but did not confirm the exact figure. Human Rights Watch warned that those returned could face imprisonment, sexual violence, or even execution upon their return to North Korea. Chinese-based sources reported that on Monday evening, hundreds were transported from detention facilities across the border.

Koo Byoung-sam, spokesperson for South Korea’s Unification Ministry, reaffirmed South Korea’s strong opposition to forced repatriations, describing them as violations of the international non-refoulement principle, which prohibits returning refugees or asylum seekers to places where they may face persecution. South Korea has officially lodged a protest with China on this issue and reiterated its viewpoint, but did not provide additional details.

According to UN special rapporteur Elizabeth Salmon, about 2,000 North Koreans are believed to be held in China after crossing the border without authorization. China, however, does not recognize these individuals as refugees, instead calling them 'economic migrants', and continues to deport them despite repeated appeals from foreign governments and human rights advocates.

When asked about the reported repatriations, Chinese foreign ministry spokesperson Wang Wenbin dismissed the notion of 'North Korean defectors' and reiterated that China treats those entering for economic reasons in a responsible manner. Human Rights Watch said that concerns over such forced returns have grown since North Korea reopened its borders in August; since July 2021, nearly 170 defectors have reportedly been returned. The group warns that returnees are at high risk of detention in forced labor camps, torture, or execution. HRW is urging the global community to urge China to stop forced repatriations and to provide refugee status or safe passage to South Korea or other countries.

article_content: Neil Warnock made an unexpected return as Crystal Palace manager on Wednesday, signing a two-year contract as Tony Pulis's successor, ahead of Steve Clarke. Warnock, 65, is set to immediately pursue a season-long loan for Wilfried Zaha from Manchester United, with a reported £1.5 million fee. Having previously managed Palace from 2007 to 2010, Warnock now has four days to reinforce the squad before the transfer deadline. Crystal Palace is also targeting Southampton midfielder Jack Cork. The club was close to finalizing Cork's transfer before Warnock's appointment, but the 25-year-old is expected to make a decision within the next 48 hours. There was a public dispute earlier this year between Warnock and Palace forward Jason Puncheon after Puncheon was criticized for missing a penalty against Tottenham in January. Puncheon later apologized for his comments and was fined £15,000 by the FA. Sources indicate the two have now resolved their issues, but Warnock could still consider transferring Puncheon if a suitable offer arises. Additionally, Palace is interested in bringing Notts County manager Shaun Derry into their coaching staff. Warnock was seen in Central London after being appointed Crystal Palace manager.

article_content: The Filmfare OTT Awards ceremony was held on Sunday in Mumbai. Alia Bhatt attended with her producer sister, Shaheen Bhatt, and won Best Actor, Web Original Film (Female) for her web debut in 'Darlings'. Manoj Bajpayee won Best Actor, Web Original Film (Male) for 'Sirf Ek Bandaa Kaafi Hai'. Vijay Varma of 'Dahaad' received Best Actor Series (Male), and Rajshri Deshpande of 'Trial By Fire' won Best Actor Series (Female). The Best Actor Series (Female) Critics award was shared by Karishma Tanna for 'Scoop' and Sonakshi Sinha for 'Dahaad'. Hansal Mehta’s 'Scoop', starring Karishma Tanna, won Best Series, while 'Trial By Fire' won Best Series Critics. Vikramaditya Motwane took Best Director Series for 'Jubilee', and Randeep Jha of 'Kohrra' won Best Director Critics. Other winners included Suvinder Vicky (Best Actor, Series (Male): Drama for 'Kohrra'), Barun Sobti (Best Supporting Actor, Series (Male): Drama for 'Kohrra'), and Tillotama Shome (Best Supporting Actor, Series (Female): Drama for 'Delhi Crime Season 2'). Abhishek Banerjee ('The Great Weddings Of Munnes') and Maanvi Gagroo ('TVF Tripling') were honored in comedy categories. TVF Pitchers S2 won Best Comedy Series/Special, and 'Cinema Marte Dum Tak' took Best Non-fiction Original, Series/Special. 'Sirf Ek Bandaa Kaafi Hai' also won Best Film, Web Original and Best Director, Web Original Film (Apoorv Singh Karki). Rajkummar Rao won Best Actor, Critics’ (Male) for 'Monica O My Darling', while Sharmila Tagore ('Gulmohar') and Sanya Malhotra ('Kathal') shared Best Actor, Critics’ (Female). Suraj Sharma ('Gulmohar'), Amruta Subhash ('Lust Stories 2'), and Shefali Shah ('Darlings') received supporting actor honors. The event featured several celebrities, including Sonam Kapoor in a blue dress with black leather gloves and high-heeled boots, Manoj Bajpayee in a suit, and Shruti Haasan with her sister. Other attendees included Karishma Tanna, Dia Mirza, Manushi Chillar, Eijaz Khan, Pratik Gandhi, Nimrat Kaur, Radhika Madan, Rajkummar Rao, Bhagyashree, Avantika Dassani, and Jackie Shroff.
