article_content: Milly Caller, 22, appeared in court today charged with assisting the suicide of her best friend, 21-year-old Emma Crossman. Caller is accused of providing Crossman with the gas container she used to take her own life earlier this year. Police discovered Crossman's body at the flat in Sleaford, Lincolnshire, that she shared with her boyfriend on January 15. Emergency services responded quickly but were unable to save Crossman. Caller, wearing a black jacket and trousers, appeared at Lincoln Magistrates' Court and only confirmed her name and address during the brief five-minute hearing. Caller, from Sleaford, entered no plea and was granted unconditional bail until her next appearance at Lincoln Crown Court on October 30. She is the second youngest person to be charged with assisting suicide in Britain. A spokesperson for Lincolnshire Police stated that the charge against Caller followed advice from the Crown Prosecution Service and her arrest on January 15, 2014, in connection with Crossman's death. Last year, Kevin Howe was convicted of assisting the suicide of his friend, Stephen Walker, and received a 12-year prison sentence. Neighbours and friends paid tribute to Emma Crossman, describing her as happy and bubbly. Sue Price, a local resident, said, 'She just seemed so lovely, happy and bubbly all the time. We never expected anything like this – it’s an absolute tragedy; she was so young.' Messages on Crossman’s Facebook page included tributes such as, 'I will never forget you as I look up into the sky,' and, 'Heaven’s most beautiful angel, sleep tight Emma.' Although assisted suicide is permitted in countries like Switzerland, Luxembourg, Belgium, and the Netherlands, and in some parts of the US, it remains illegal in the UK with a maximum sentence of 14 years. In 2009, new guidelines were introduced that informed how such cases are prosecuted. Caller is only the second person to be charged with assisting suicide since the guidelines changed.

Private equity firm MBK Partners, specializing in North Asia, is said to be selling Japanese jewellery brand Tasaki in a deal that could exceed $500 million, according to people familiar with the matter. Daiwa Securities has been hired to manage the process, which has now entered a second phase of bidding. Sources report MBK has approached other private equity firms about acquiring Tasaki, but MBK, Daiwa, and Tasaki have not commented publicly.

Founded in Kobe in 1954, Tasaki is renowned for its pearl jewellery and operates over 100 stores within Japan as well as internationally in Asia and Europe. In 2017, MBK took Tasaki private through a 31.5 billion yen (approximately $209.5 million) buyout to streamline operations and drive expansion outside Japan. Years earlier, in 2009, MBK invested 7 billion yen to help rescue Tasaki during a downturn spurred by increased competition from affordable Chinese pearls, which reportedly brought considerable returns when MBK exited in 2015.

MBK also invests in Japanese companies such as Godiva Japan and care provider Tsukui Holdings. In 2021, groups like Human Rights Now and Justice for Myanmar urged Tasaki to cease its relationship with Myanmar Pearl Enterprise after U.S. sanctions were imposed on the state-owned entity. Activists claim that continuing business with Myanmar Pearl Enterprise indirectly supports the ruling junta, a factor that, according to sources, is narrowing the field of potential buyers. Tasaki did not reply to inquiries about its ties to Myanmar Pearl Enterprise. The exchange rate at the time of reporting was $1 to 150.37 yen.

article_content: When IBM's Watson system defeated the human champion on 'Jeopardy!' in February 2011, it impressed the world with its remarkable grasp of a wide range of facts, wordplay, and challenging questions. But how might this achievement shape our lives over the next decade, and what does it suggest about the future of intelligent machines? Watson built its extensive knowledge base by 'reading' the equivalent of millions of books, signaling a shift in how computers could acquire, analyze, and generate knowledge. Given the enormous volume of text available today—ranging from web pages and articles to tweets—automatic machine reading will be a vital part of technological progress. Here are five anticipated ways the Machine-Reading Revolution could transform your life in the next decade: 1. Scientific Assistant: By 2020, machine reading and understanding of scientific literature could help accelerate scientific breakthroughs, from discovering new disease treatments to addressing climate change. The Allen Institute for Artificial Intelligence's Aristo project is developing software that enables computers to learn from textbooks, ask questions, and draw preliminary conclusions. Tools like these, building on systems such as Watson, will likely become essential for scientists and researchers. 2. Answering Questions: Soon, when you ask your smartphone a specific question such as 'When is the next flight to Atlanta?' or 'What is President Obama's current approval rating?' you’ll receive clear and direct answers. Programs like Siri and Google Now already handle simple spoken questions. Over the next decade, the range of questions these systems can answer will expand, using information drawn not just from static databases but also from automatically analyzed news, web pages, and social media. As predicted, the traditional list of 'ten blue links' will gradually become obsolete. 3. Online Shopping Concierge: Automated concierges will soon make recommendations by analyzing your preferences and reading product reviews across the internet. Today, finding a quiet hotel in Manhattan might require hours reviewing feedback, but soon, computers will do this work for you. Research such as RevMiner has already shown computers can accurately process reviews, suggesting truly seamless online shopping is on the horizon. 4. Automated Medical Assistant: Imagine instantly receiving a 'second opinion' based on the latest medical research, either in your doctor’s office or at home. Doctors today face an overwhelming volume of new studies. By 2023, physicians could have a digital assistant that tracks medical literature, alerts them to potential issues like drug interactions or dangerous side effects, and provides timely insights. 5. Real-Time Statistics: Within a decade, key statistics on health, inflation, and unemployment could be available in real time, helping policymakers and the public. Outbreaks and other events are currently identified after delays, but social media updates can reveal such changes quickly. Research is ongoing to use real-time data for tracking epidemics and socioeconomic trends: Henry Kautz documents food poisoning outbreaks in New York City, University of Michigan researchers analyze unemployment, and the Billion Prices Project at MIT offers improved inflation tracking. The Allen Institute for Artificial Intelligence (AI2), recently launched in Seattle, aims to advance machine reading and understanding through foundational research. Within ten years, computer-acquired knowledge from massive text sources may become instantly accessible, potentially enabling interactive systems reminiscent of the Star Trek Communicator—and surpassing today's digital assistants. While the technological singularity remains a distant goal, a Machine-Reading Revolution is already on its way to your mobile device.

article_content: Swiss cyclist Fabian Cancellara has voluntarily withdrawn from the Tour de France during the race's first rest day, becoming the latest prominent rider to leave the event. Unlike past champions Chris Froome, Alberto Contador, Andy Schleck, and 25-time stage winner Mark Cavendish—who all crashed out—Cancellara chose to exit to focus on preparing for the Road World Championships in Spain this September. In a statement released by his Trek Factory Racing team, Cancellara said: 'I will travel home now and take a little break. The season has been long for me, starting back in Dubai (February). I have raced 59 days this season and have another big goal at the end: the World Championships. It's not a secret that I'd like to be in my best shape there, so it's important that I take some rest.' Cancellara delivered a strong performance during the cobbled fifth stage, finishing fifth and starting the day as one of the favorites. His departure, along with those of Andy Schleck and Danny van Poppel, leaves Trek Factory Racing with just six riders remaining in the Tour de France. The event continues with Wednesday's eleventh stage, covering a 187.5km route from Besançon to Oyonnax. Earlier, Mark Cavendish crashed out on stage one in Harrogate, Chris Froome abandoned during stage five from Ypres to Arenberg Porte du Hainaut, and Alberto Contador retired after a crash in stage ten.

article_content: A recent UK study suggests that people aged 50 and above may have experienced a decline in brain health as a result of the Covid-19 pandemic. Over 3,000 participants completed annual surveys and online cognitive exercises to track changes in memory and mental abilities throughout the pandemic. Interestingly, the drop in cognitive performance was found regardless of whether someone had tested positive for Covid-19. Researchers believe factors such as increased stress, feelings of isolation, and changes in drinking habits may partially explain these findings. The study, known as PROTECT and featured in The Lancet Healthy Longevity journal, showed the most rapid decline in thinking skills occurred during the first year of the pandemic, coinciding with nationwide lockdowns. Memory issues continued to worsen into the second year. Participants who already had mild memory problems before the pandemic saw the sharpest drops. PROTECT aims to improve understanding of how the aging process affects the brain and what leads to dementia, gathering data through brain games and risk factor questionnaires. The researchers hope to continue monitoring participants to identify lessons that might help others in the future. Lead researcher Professor Anne Corbett, from the University of Exeter, noted that restrictions during the pandemic appeared to have had a notably lasting effect on the brain health of those over 50. Professor Corbett emphasized the need for people, especially those noticing early memory issues, to seek medical advice since early support can help reduce the risk of dementia later in life. According to Dr Dorina Cadar of Brighton and Sussex Medical School, the pandemic's overall effect on public health has been severe, and many long-term impacts are still unknown. She stressed the importance of further study, as social isolation and other related factors likely play a negative role in brain health. Dr Susan Mitchell from Alzheimer’s Research UK pointed out the influence of both genetics and lifestyle choices on how our brains age, and noted that, while dementia cannot yet be prevented, adopting healthier habits like staying socially connected and looking after both heart and brain health could improve the odds.

article_content: Alibaba Group has cancelled its previously announced plan to spin off its cloud business, attributing the decision to uncertainty resulting from new U.S. export restrictions on advanced chips used in artificial intelligence. These U.S. measures have created challenges for several Chinese tech companies, including Tencent, which also noted an impact on its cloud operations. This update coincided with Alibaba’s release of second-quarter financial results, which matched analyst projections. In March, Alibaba unveiled a sweeping reorganization, with intentions to separate the cloud division; however, both the cloud spin-off and a planned IPO of the Freshippo grocery business are now postponed. Instead, Alibaba will seek external investment for its international digital commerce arm. Additionally, Alibaba’s logistics subsidiary Cainiao applied for a listing on the Hong Kong stock exchange in September. After the announcement, Alibaba’s U.S.-listed shares fell by over 8% in premarket trading, reflecting investor concerns. Investors reacted negatively to the delay, having anticipated that the cloud business spin-off could increase Alibaba’s market value. Analysts had estimated the cloud unit could be valued between $41 and $60 billion but warned that the spin-off might attract scrutiny from Chinese and overseas regulators. In September, company leadership shifted when former CEO Daniel Zhang resigned. Eddie Wu, a co-founder and longtime executive, became CEO of both Alibaba Group and its cloud business, while Joseph Tsai was named chairman. On a post-earnings call, Tsai said that Alibaba would not spin off its cloud arm due to the uncertain impact of U.S. export rules on AI chips, and would instead focus on a self-sustaining, AI-driven growth model for its cloud business. Wu confirmed continued strategic investment in cloud, emphasizing the unit’s ongoing independence. Regulatory filings on Thursday also revealed that a trust affiliated with founder Jack Ma plans to sell 10 million Alibaba American Depository Shares, totaling about $871 million. Explaining Alibaba’s updated strategy, Wu stated that its various business arms will operate more independently, following strategic reviews that differentiate between core and non-core pursuits. Core businesses will receive long-term investment and research focus, while non-core units may be sold, spun off, or otherwise monetized. Units such as DingTalk and Xianyu will operate as independent subsidiaries. Wu reiterated that Alibaba’s two primary strategic priorities going forward are user-centricity and AI innovation. The company’s second-quarter revenues reached 224.79 billion yuan ($31.01 billion), aligning closely with analyst expectations. International digital commerce, including Lazada and AliExpress, reported strong gains, with AliExpress becoming the top cross-border e-commerce marketplace in Europe. Alibaba faces increasing competition from domestic and global players like Temu and Pinduoduo. China’s economic rebound remains inconsistent; the property market continues to impact consumer confidence, though Alibaba experienced mild growth in its retail commission revenue. To compete during Singles Day, Alibaba encouraged vendors to adopt lower prices. The article concludes with brief references to unrelated industry developments in India (banking, corporate profits, and gaming bans).

article_content: Over the years, nearly all cartoon characters undergo changes in their appearance—and 'The Simpsons,' now in its 26th season, is no exception. The transformation from the show's earliest days, when Homer Simpson and his family debuted on 'The Tracey Ullman Show,' is dramatic. Compared to today's familiar Simpsons, the Ullman-era versions were crudely drawn, paler, misshapen, and had notably different voices. For this year’s 'Treehouse of Horror' Halloween special, the current Simpsons family will encounter their original Ullman counterparts—in a storyline that sees the two versions battle it out in gruesome fashion. 'We've implied that they were murdered and buried under the house, so this is expanding that thought,' producer Al Jean told Entertainment Weekly. 'If people want a real Halloween bloodbath, they get it.' While the old-school Simpsons have made brief, self-aware cameos before, this will be the first time both versions of the family share extended scenes. The episode will also feature the original voice performances. The cast had to recall how their characters sounded back during the Ullman days and switch between those and the current voices, sometimes even within the same conversation. 'It was really funny to get the interplay between the two versions and for the actors to see the voice evolution,' Jean said. 'The great thing is we didn’t have to ask—our cast originally did the Ullman voices too.' The Ullman Simpsons aren’t the only unexpected visitors this season. As previously announced, a mash-up between 'The Simpsons' and 'Family Guy' is also planned. Read the full story at RollingStone.com.

article_content: American tourists can stay in Palau for up to a year without needing a visa. With the rise of digital nomadism, travelers are seeking destinations where they can stay long-term without complicated visa processes. Most countries allow U.S., Canadian, and British citizens to visit for up to 90 days with an automatic tourist visa. Longer-term visas often come with fees, application processes, background checks, and proof of funds, making them less appealing to many travelers. Extended stays abroad may also carry consequences, such as potential tax residency status or additional IRS filing requirements. Certain long-stay visas require you to remain in the country, restricting your flexibility to travel. Another consideration is whether your foreign driver’s license remains valid for your entire stay—for instance, Panama permits a 180-day tourist stay, but foreign driver’s licenses are only recognized for 90 days. For commitment-free travel, only a small number of countries offer straightforward, long-term tourist entry. In rare cases, tourists can stay for up to a year or renew by leaving and re-entering. Albania allows Americans to stay visa-free for up to a year. Georgia permits most visitors to enter and remain for one year without paperwork. Palau, comprising over 500 islands, lets Americans stay for up to a year. A few countries offer easy 180-day entries. Since September 2023, Costa Rica allows 'Group One' countries (including the U.S., Canada, and the U.K.) to stay for 180 days, with possible extensions. Mexico grants six-month tourist stays, which can be renewed upon re-entry. Panama issues 180-day tourist visas, also resettable by leaving and re-entering. Some countries enable initial 3-month stays with easy extensions. Cambodia provides a 30-day visa, renewable monthly for up to a year (not a tourist visa). Chile and Colombia allow for extensions, reaching up to six months total; Colombia caps tourists at six months per calendar year. Guatemala offers a three-month stay, with a three-month extension, but travelers must exit the CA-4 region when their visa expires. Seychelles allows three-month entries, renewable up to a year with a fee, proof of funds, onward travel, and accommodation. Border runs, which involve leaving and immediately re-entering a country for a new tourist visa, remain possible in some regions but are restricted in others—for example, Thailand has placed new limits. In Uruguay, travelers receive 90 days, which can be extended for another 90 or reset by a border run. Taiwan permits 90-day stays with re-entry allowed after exit. Travelers should always check the latest entry and stay regulations for each country, as long-term stays may entail specific requirements.

En annan sak att tänka på är om ditt utländska körkort gäller hela vistelsen – till exempel tillåter Panama turister att stanna i 180 dagar, men körkort från hemlandet gäller bara i 90 dagar. För resenärer som vill ha frihet utan fasta åtaganden erbjuder endast ett fåtal länder smidiga långtidsvistelser. I vissa fall kan man stanna i upp till ett år, eller förlänga genom att lämna landet och återvända. Albanien låter amerikaner stanna visumfritt i upp till ett år. Georgien tillåter de flesta besökare att stanna i ett år utan pappersarbete. Palau, som består av över 500 öar, välkomnar amerikaner för vistelser upp till ett år. Från och med september 2023 tillåter Costa Rica 'Grupp Ett'-länder (inklusive USA, Kanada och Storbritannien) vistelse i 180 dagar med möjlighet att förlänga. Vissa länder erbjuder först tre månaders vistelse med lätt förlängning. Kambodja ger ett 30-dagars visum som kan förnyas månadsvis upp till ett år (ej turistvisum). Guatemala erbjuder tre månaders vistelse, som kan förlängas tre månader, men eftersom landet ingår i CA-4-avtalet måste man också lämna hela regionen när visumet går ut. Seychellerna erbjuder tre månaders inresa, förnybart upp till ett år mot avgift och krav på ekonomiska medel, utresa och boende. Gränsresor, där man lämnar landet och återvänder direkt för att förnya turistvisumet, fungerar fortfarande i vissa länder men har begränsats i andra – till exempel har Thailand infört nya regler. I Uruguay får man 90 dagar som kan förlängas med ytterligare 90 eller återställas genom gränsresa. Taiwan erbjuder 90 dagars vistelse med möjlighet att återvända efter utresa. Resenärer bör alltid kontrollera de senaste reglerna för inresa och uppehåll i respektive land, eftersom långtidsvistelser ofta innebär särskilda krav.

article_content: Chelsea began the football season with its poorest performance since Roman Abramovich became owner in 2003. However, following their recent FA Cup final victory—Chelsea's fourth in six years—the club is poised for one of its most successful years. This trophy marks a major step in the club's revival and brings Abramovich closer to his long-held goal: winning the Champions League. After clinching the Premier League title in 2005, helped by coach Jose Mourinho and numerous star signings, Chelsea established itself as a competitive force. Despite adding more league titles, attempts by successive managers—Avram Grant, Luiz Felipe Scolari, Carlo Ancelotti, and Andre Villas-Boas—to win the Champions League fell short. Villas-Boas, hired for his potential after a successful stint at Porto, struggled to connect with Chelsea's veteran players and left mid-season. His assistant, former Chelsea player Roberto di Matteo, gained the squad's respect and returned to the tactics that had previously brought success, elevating key players like Frank Lampard and Didier Drogba. Drogba was pivotal in Chelsea's semifinals victory over powerhouse Barcelona in the Champions League and sealed the FA Cup win against Liverpool with a crucial goal. The 34-year-old Ivorian striker made history as the first footballer to score in four separate FA Cup finals, matching Liverpool legend Ian Rush's total of five goals in such finals. Drogba may depart after the upcoming Champions League final against Bayern Munich—a match with enormous significance for both Abramovich's ambitions and Chelsea's financial planning, given new fair play regulations in European football. Each team in the Champions League final is expected to receive around $66 million, a significant boost as clubs can no longer depend on private funding as before. Chelsea is also bidding to purchase Battersea Power Station to develop a new stadium with a greater capacity than Stamford Bridge. Their $2.9 million prize from the seventh FA Cup win will aid finances and bolster Di Matteo’s candidacy for a permanent managerial position. In the FA Cup final, Ramires opened the scoring for Chelsea, followed by Drogba's second goal. Liverpool substitute Andy Carroll narrowed the gap and nearly equalized, but Chelsea goalkeeper Petr Cech's save denied him. The match's outcome angered Liverpool’s Luis Suarez, who was booked for protesting to officials. Di Matteo, who previously scored in two FA Cup finals for Chelsea, expressed pride in his players: 'We’ve been heavily criticized this season, but we have a trophy and a chance for another. This group made the club proud.' Liverpool, despite qualifying for the Europa League via a League Cup win, had an underwhelming season under Kenny Dalglish, trailing Chelsea by 12 points with two games left. Dalglish admitted, 'They were better than us for the first hour... We've just got to learn the lessons.' Chelsea’s Champions League qualification hinges on the upcoming final, as rivals Arsenal, Tottenham, and Newcastle all compete for top league positions. Manchester City reclaimed first place after defeating Manchester United, who have an easier final opposition in Swansea.

Denna trofé markerar ett viktigt steg i klubbens återhämtning och för Abramovich närmare hans långvariga mål: att vinna Champions League. Efter att ha vunnit Premier League-titeln 2005, med hjälp av tränaren Jose Mourinho och flera stjärnvärvningar, etablerade sig Chelsea som en stark konkurrent. Drogba kan lämna klubben efter den kommande Champions League-finalen mot Bayern München—en match av enorm vikt både för Abramovichs ambitioner och Chelseas ekonomiska planering, med tanke på de nya reglerna för finansiell fair play i europeisk fotboll. Nvidia expects a sharp fall in sales to China for the fourth quarter, citing newly expanded U.S. export controls that limit what chips it can send there. Despite this, the company predicts total revenue for the quarter will beat Wall Street's expectations, driven by eased supply-chain bottlenecks and soaring global demand for artificial intelligence.

Previously, about a quarter of Nvidia's datacenter revenue came from Chinese sales. The company says it cannot accurately predict the long-term hit from the new restrictions but is designing chips for China that comply with the new rules. However, these new products won't have a noticeable effect this quarter.

Nvidia’s stock, which has surged more than 240% in 2023, slipped on the news. Further uncertainty comes from Israel, where Nvidia's networking division is based. The firm warned that the Gaza conflict had brought many Israeli staff members into active military service, which could affect operations if the turmoil continues.

Despite these challenges, Nvidia projects fourth-quarter gross margins over 75%, higher than analysts estimated. Still, market watchers question if increased sales outside China can offset the losses and maintain such profitability.

On the supply side, Nvidia is prepaying chipmaking partners such as TSMC to ensure priority manufacturing slots. Shipments of AI servers are forecast to jump 40% globally this year.

The latest quarterly results showcased exceptional growth: total revenue tripled, datacenter sales grew 41%, and gaming revenue increased 15%. In response to export bans, Nvidia has introduced new chips for China, but specialists warn that these efforts might drain resources or fall under future embargoes if restrictions tighten.

Meanwhile, competitors like Google, Amazon, and Microsoft are designing custom AI chips to reduce reliance on Nvidia, and firms like AMD and Huawei are rolling out rival products. 

Ultimately, Nvidia is experiencing impressive growth and improving chip supplies but faces continued uncertainty from shifting regulations and global tensions.

Trots detta tror bolaget att den totala kvartalsomsättningen kommer att överträffa Wall Streets förväntningar, tack vare lättnader i leveranskedjan och stark, global efterfrågan på artificiell intelligens.

Nvidias aktie, som stigit med över 240 % under 2023, sjönk efter nyheten. Ytterligare osäkerhet finns i Israel, där Nvidias nätverksavdelning har sitt säte. Företaget varnar för att konflikten i Gaza gjort att många israeliska anställda kallats in till militärtjänst, vilket kan påverka verksamheten om det fortsätter.

Trots utmaningarna räknar Nvidia med bruttomarginaler på över 75 % för fjärde kvartalet, vilket är högre än analytiker väntat. Ändå tvivlar marknadsbedömare på om ökade försäljningar utanför Kina kan väga upp förlusterna och behålla dagens lönsamhet.

För att säkra tillgången på AI-chip förbetalar Nvidia tillverkningspartners som TSMC för prioriterad produktion. Globala AI-serverleveranser väntas öka med 40 % i år.

De senaste kvartalsresultaten visade på exceptionell tillväxt: den totala omsättningen tredubblades, datacenterförsäljningen steg med 41 % och spelintäkterna ökade med 15 %. För att möta exportrestriktionerna har Nvidia lanserat nya chip för den kinesiska marknaden, men experter varnar att ansträngningarna kan bli förgäves om reglerna skärps ytterligare.

Samtidigt tar konkurrenter som Google, Amazon och Microsoft fram egna AI-chip för att minska beroendet av Nvidia, och företag som AMD och Huawei lanserar konkurrerande produkter.

article_content: Climate change has been described as a fundamental threat to life on Earth by leading scientists, who issued a sobering report after a year of extreme weather and record-high temperatures. With 2023 set to become the hottest year ever recorded, many regions worldwide have endured deadly heat waves and devastating floods—sometimes in quick succession. An international group of researchers, writing in the journal BioScience, expressed alarm and surprise at the unprecedented intensity of this year’s weather events. They stated, 'We are deeply troubled by the severity of the 2023 extremes and the unknown challenges ahead.' The report declares that 'Life is under siege on planet Earth,' highlighting minimal progress in cutting climate-warming emissions. It also notes that greenhouse gases and fossil fuel subsidies reached record levels last year. This warning comes weeks before the UN COP28 climate summit, which will take place in the oil-rich United Arab Emirates. The authors urge that the climate crisis should be seen not only as an environmental challenge but as a systemic and existential threat. By reviewing data on 35 key measures of the Earth’s health, the authors found that 20 hit record extremes in 2023.

Eftersom 2023 ser ut att bli det varmaste året någonsin har många regioner världen över drabbats av dödliga värmeböljor och förödande översvämningar—ibland tätt efter varandra. En internationell grupp forskare, som skriver i tidskriften BioScience, uttrycker stor oro och förvåning över den intensitet årets väderextremer haft. De säger: 'Vi är djupt bekymrade över allvaret i 2023 års extrema väder och de okända utmaningar vi nu står inför.' Rapporten slår fast att 'livet på planeten Jorden är under belägring' och lyfter fram att det har skett minimala framsteg i att minska växthusgasutsläppen. Den noterar också att nivåerna av växthusgaser och subventioner till fossila bränslen nådde rekordnivåer förra året. In the Ukrainian city of Rivne, 97-year-old Angela Artyomova survived a terrifying ordeal after slipping while cleaning her apartment windows. She found herself hanging from her fourth-floor residence, suspended about 35 feet above the street, by clutching an air conditioning unit. Her foot, caught in the bracket of the unit, enabled her to hold on for around 30 minutes.

Her calls for help drew the attention of neighbors and passersby, who quickly notified emergency services. Firefighters, perceiving the immediate danger, decided to use a ladder instead of setting up an air cushion. They rescued Angela and safely brought her back inside.

Angela was subsequently taken to the hospital and treated for shock. Her remarkable resilience in the face of such danger left a strong impression on both rescuers and the local community.

Hennes fot fastnade i hållaren, vilket hjälpte henne att hålla sig kvar i cirka trettio minuter.

Hennes nödrop hördes av grannar och förbipasserande som snabbt kontaktade räddningstjänsten. Brandmännen insåg situationens allvar och använde en stege istället för att hinna rigga upp en luftmadrass. De lyckades rädda Angela och föra henne i säkerhet in i lägenheten igen.

Angela fördes senare till sjukhus och behandlades för chock. Hennes beundransvärda styrka och mod i denna livsfarliga situation gjorde stort intryck på både räddningspersonalen och lokalsamhället.

A 24-foot-tall Buddha statue in China’s Longmen Grottoes has captured widespread attention for its apparent ‘peace sign’ gesture, which resonates with the popular photo pose among East Asian youth. The Amita Buddha is located in the 104th cave of the famous grottoes in Henan Province, part of a collection of roughly 100,000 statues carved into more than 1,400 caves over nearly 2,000 years.

The ‘peace’ gesture, widely used by young people from South Korea to China, originated as the ‘V for Victory’ sign in WWII Europe, and was later adopted by the peace movement in the US during the 1960s. Its spread across East Asia is often attributed to the influence of Japanese culture following World War II.

Despite the Buddha statue’s newfound fame, the gesture is reportedly a coincidence—historians and media sources like Rex Features explain that the hand shape resulted from centuries of weathering and damage. The Amita Buddha was constructed during the reign of Emperor Gaozong of Tang (Li Zhi), who ruled northern China between 650 and 683 AD. Many Longmen Buddhas are depicted with ritual hand gestures, or Mudras, each with specific meanings. However, in this case, the resemblance to a peace sign is accidental and not part of the original artistic intent.

En 7 meter hög Buddhastaty i Longmen-grottorna i Kina har fått stor uppmärksamhet för sin gest som liknar ett ‘peace’-tecken, en populär pose bland östasiatiska ungdomar. Amita Buddha ligger i den 104:e grottan i de berömda grottorna i Henan-provinsen och är en av cirka 100 000 statyer uthuggna i mer än 1 400 grottor under nästan 2 000 år.

‘Peace’-gesten, som ofta används av unga från Sydkorea till Kina, har sitt ursprung som ‘V för Victory’-tecknet i Europa under andra världskriget och anammades senare av fredsrörelsen i USA på 1960-talet. Gesten spreds vidare till Östasien, mycket tack vare japansk kulturell påverkan efter andra världskriget.

Trots statyns nyvunna berömmelse menar historiker och medier som Rex Features att handgesten är en ren tillfällighet – formen uppstod av århundraden av väder och skador. Amita Buddha byggdes under kejsar Gaozong av Tang (Li Zhi), som regerade norra Kina mellan 650 och 683 e.Kr. Många Buddhastatyer i Longmen avbildas med olika mudras, rituella handgester med särskilda betydelser. Men i det här fallet är likheten med ett peace-tecken bara en slump och inte en del av den ursprungliga konstnärliga meningen.

article_content: Integrating AI tools can help project managers become more efficient, confidently handle decision-making and planning, and make creative use of resources. Project managers already manage significant responsibilities: planning for risks, distributing and organizing resources, setting annual budgets, scheduling stakeholder meetings, and coordinating daily operations. Toward the year’s end, these tasks can become overwhelming. Fortunately, rapid advances in artificial intelligence have made project management roles easier. AI tools aid in tracking project milestones and deadlines, support better planning, and enhance resource allocation and creativity. How to Choose the Right AI Tool for Project Management Selecting an AI-powered project management tool starts with identifying what processes need automation, key required features, and considering user experiences from reviews. Pricing is important too—choose a tool that fits your budget while offering strong customer support and essential features, rather than simply opting for the cheapest. The right tool should balance affordability with functionality, fitting seamlessly into your workflow. Eight AI Tools for Project Managers Ayanza: A software solution for managing projects from start to finish, helping teams coordinate and stay aligned with objectives. Features include real-time communication and a focus on team health. Plans range from $0 to $15; enterprise pricing is available on request. Stepsize: Designed for technical project managers, Stepsize integrates with GitHub, Jira, and Slack. It provides detailed sprint and Kanban summaries, with subscriptions starting at $29 per month. Zapier: With the ability to connect more than 2,000 applications, Zapier enables automated workflows, saving project managers time on repetitive tasks. Pricing starts at $0 per month, with the highest standard tier at $69 plus available enterprise plans. Trello (with Butler Power-Up): Trello supports automated task management via the AI-driven Butler Power-Up, which moves cards, assigns tasks, and sends notifications automatically based on triggers. This streamlines workflows and saves significant manual effort. Subscription plans range from $0 to $17.50 per user and higher, depending on team size. Kuki Chatbot: Kuki provides AI-powered chatbots that manage customer queries, bookings, and lead capture, ensuring prompt responses and improving efficiency. Notion: Notion serves as an all-in-one workspace for note-taking, content management, and automations for task flows and database entries. It integrates with Slack and GitHub, with pricing from $0 to $15 and additional enterprise options. Taskade: Financial advisor Howard Goldman recommends Taskade for tracking tasks, collaborative project management, and staying organized. Powered by GPT-4, it offers AI chat assistants, summarization, and workflow generation. Fellow: Fellow specializes in meeting productivity, allowing users to prepare agendas, take notes, and track meeting effectiveness. Plans range from $0 to $15 monthly, with enterprise offerings available. Embracing Artificial Intelligence in Project Management With a wide range of AI tools, project managers can reduce workplace stress, gain better insights and analyses, boost team morale, and achieve higher project success rates.

article_content: As companies increasingly encourage employees to return to the office, organizations supporting hybrid and flexible work styles are turning to enhanced employee engagement programs. The aim is to reduce feelings of disconnection and lift productivity. Executives cite that this growing 'disconnect' not only impacts collaboration and productivity, but also hampers team bonding. These engagement initiatives are especially beneficial for younger employees who began their careers remotely during the pandemic. NatWest Group, Tech Mahindra, EY, and Capgemini are among the firms rolling out a variety of initiatives: regular team meetings, in-person group sessions, 'fun-at-work' and sports events, and assigning buddies to new hires—all designed to build workplace cohesion. For example, NatWest Group has conducted more than 40 in-person group sessions for employees who joined during the pandemic. 'We realized that over 7,000 colleagues who came onboard virtually missed opportunities to build relationships and connections,' said Maneesh Menda, HR head for international hubs at NatWest Group. 'These sessions are part of our engagement strategy.' NatWest’s leadership has been actively involved in these activities to help staff network and strengthen relationships. A recent Employee Experience survey by Qualtrics found that 83% of new hires reported lower engagement, and just 24% confirmed an intention to stay, indicating a decline in the first-year experience. Other companies, like Tech Mahindra, are harnessing technology to promote engagement. 'With our broad, dispersed workforce, technology is central to our people engagement strategy, TechMHRNxt,' said Harshvendra Soin, global chief people officer at Tech Mahindra. The company has introduced an AI coach for managers and launched BeMe, an AI-driven engagement platform. EY India has improved its onboarding system by pairing each new hire with an experienced 'buddy,' a peer who helps new employees settle in and feel supported, said EY India talent leader Sandeep Kohli. Capgemini’s India Continuous Assimilation Program (I-CAP) helps newcomers feel welcomed and engaged from before they join, through their acclimatization to the company, shared chief HR officer Aarti Srivastava. Separately, India’s income tax department says it has detected nearly Rs 10,000 crore in tax evasion over three years by brands selling via platforms such as Instagram and Facebook, having sent notices to 45 brands so far. Additionally, heightened GST scrutiny is influencing M&A plans, with Indian companies now reviewing tax liabilities carefully before finalizing business deals. Meanwhile, Raymond’s managing director Gautam Singhania has been accused by estranged wife Nawaz Modi of assaulting her and one of their daughters two months ago.

Målet är att minska känslan av frånkoppling och öka produktiviteten. Företagsledare menar att denna ökande 'frånkoppling' inte bara påverkar samarbete och produktivitet, utan också hindrar laganda. article_content: Fitbit devices are no longer being officially sold in many countries such as Poland, Portugal, and Thailand, as first reported by Android Authority. Google decided to pull Fitbit from these markets to align its distribution with that of its Pixel devices, according to TechCentral. This move marks another step in Fitbit’s integration into Google, which began acquiring the company in 2019 and completed the purchase in 2021. Fitbit, once renowned for pioneering fitness trackers and fostering a small but vibrant developer community, has seen many of its unique features and third-party app support discontinued under Google’s leadership. Now, users are limited to integrating with only Google services; non-Google features like Spotify are gone, and creative elements such as step challenges tied to real-world places have been phased out. New Fitbit users must also link their accounts to Google and migrate their data, as Google is consolidating account systems. Recent updates to products like the Sense 2, Versa 4, and Charge 6 have brought little change, with ongoing issues like spotty GPS reception still unresolved. What's left is a polished but less distinctive user experience, with a focus on the Fitbit Premium subscription service, which some consider to be less technologically advanced than Apple Fitness+. Moreover, Google's Pixel Watch now serves as the primary wearable for Pixel phones, casting further doubt on the direction of higher-end Fitbit models. While affordable fitness trackers may persist, the future for devices like the Sense is increasingly uncertain. Although there was talk from Fitbit’s CEO about launching a smartwatch with Google’s Wear OS, Google later stated those comments were misunderstood. For now, Fitbit’s evolution under Google continues, but the brand’s future path remains unclear.

Det här är ytterligare ett steg i Fitbits integrering i Google, som började förvärva företaget 2019 och slutförde köpet 2021. Fitbit var tidigare känt för sina banbrytande aktivitetsband och ett litet men aktivt utvecklarsamfund, men har under Googles ledning förlorat många av sina unika funktioner och stödet för tredjepartsappar. Nya Fitbit-användare måste dessutom logga in med Google-konto och flytta över sin data, eftersom Google sammanslår kontosystemen. Uppdateringarna av modeller som Sense 2, Versa 4 och Charge 6 har varit små, och problem som opålitlig GPS kvarstår. Det som återstår är en slät men mindre unik användarupplevelse, med tonvikt på abonnemangstjänsten Fitbit Premium—som vissa anser inte kan mäta sig tekniskt med Apple Fitness+. Dessutom är Pixel Watch nu huvudalternativet för Pixel-telefoner, vilket gör framtiden för mer avancerade Fitbit-modeller än mer osäker. Fitbits utveckling under Google fortsätter alltså, men varumärkets framtid är osäker.

article_content: A midwife is facing a hearing for alleged professional misconduct after reportedly using a plastic spoon to induce labour in a pregnant woman at King’s College Hospital NHS Trust, despite the labour being without complications. The Nursing and Midwifery Council (NMC) claims that Patience Adams employed this unorthodox technique without obtaining consent from the patient, referred to as ‘Patient A.’ The woman speaks Mandarin and understands little English. Adams stated she could communicate with the patient, sometimes using sign language and assistance from the patient’s husband. Evidence presented to the panel indicates that on May 8, 2011, at around 12:30 am, Adams performed an artificial rupture of membranes, even though the labour was progressing normally and without concerns for the baby’s well-being. Medical documentation did not justify the procedure. Fellow midwife Alison Taylor reported that Adams requested a needle—which is not standard practice for this procedure—and began an internal examination. After Taylor intervened, Adams set aside the needle. Later, Taylor saw Adams with a plastic spoon, which was reported to have been used during the procedure. The use of a non-sterile object like a plastic spoon poses infection risks and potential harm to the baby. Adams admitted at the hearing that she did not offer a translator, failed to record fetal observations, and performed two internal examinations without medical reason. However, she denied using a needle to attempt the procedure and denied performing it without discussion or consent. If the allegations are upheld, Adams could be removed from the professional register. Comments on the case are not being accepted for legal reasons.

Enligt Nursing and Midwifery Council (NMC) ska Patience Adams ha använt den okonventionella metoden utan patientens samtycke. Patienten, kallad ”Patient A”, talar mandarin och förstår lite engelska. Adams uppgav att hon kunde kommunicera med patienten, ibland genom teckenspråk och med hjälp av patientens man. Panelen informerades om att Adams den 8 maj 2011 cirka kl. 00.30 utförde en artificiell hinnsprängning, trots att förlossningen fortskred normalt och utan oro för barnet. Det fanns ingen dokumentation som motiverade ingreppet. Kollegan Alison Taylor rapporterade att Adams bad om en nål – ovanligt för detta ingrepp – och började en invändig undersökning. Efter att Taylor ingripit lade Adams undan nålen. Senare såg Taylor Adams med en plastsked, som enligt uppgift användes under proceduren. Att använda ett icke-sterilt föremål som en plastsked innebär infektionsrisk och kan skada barnet. Vid utfrågningen erkände Adams att hon inte erbjöd tolk, inte dokumenterade fosterövervakning och genomförde två interna undersökningar utan medicinsk anledning. Hon nekade dock till att ha försökt använda nål och till att ha utfört proceduren utan samtal eller samtycke. Om anklagelserna fastställs kan Adams förlora sin legitimation. Kommentarer till ärendet tas inte emot av juridiska skäl.

article_content: As the biggest sporting event of the year approached, ESPN took a moment to honor veteran broadcaster Stuart Scott, who passed away from cancer on January 4 at age 49. His emotional colleagues remembered Scott’s passion and kindness during a tribute segment. Host Suzy Kolber recalled that Scott, who covered the Super Bowl for years, once held her newborn daughter, Kellyn, at her first NFL game and that she had done the same for his daughter, Taelor. Kolber shared a photo of Scott with Kellyn, calling it 'magical.' She expressed that what she will miss most about Scott were his well-known, heartfelt hugs and the love he shared with those around him. Kolber said, 'We can’t replace that, but we are grateful to have had him in our lives. His legacy lives on.' Kolber and Scott shared a 20-year professional relationship. Scott covered numerous Super Bowls, including the 2002 event, and interviewed sports legends such as Michael Jordan and Tiger Woods. He also interviewed and played basketball with Barack Obama before his 2008 presidential victory. President Obama paid tribute to Scott after his passing, acknowledging that Scott’s shows often entertained him during his campaign. ESPN hosts celebrated Scott’s 'undaunted, indomitable' spirit and reminded viewers of his involvement with the Jimmy V Foundation, which supports efforts against cancer. Scott began at ESPN in 1993 and became a figure of inspiration during his public cancer battle, although he never specified the type of cancer he was fighting. He continued to work during intense treatment and remained deeply committed to his family and career. On the day of Scott’s passing, ESPN president John Skipper described him as 'a true friend and a uniquely inspirational figure' and praised his steadfast devotion to work and family. Scott was known for training in mixed martial arts during chemotherapy and returning to TV soon after hospital procedures. He is survived by his parents, O. Ray and Jacqueline Scott; siblings Stephen Scott, Synthia Kearney, and Susan Scott; his daughters Taelor, 19, and Sydni, 15; and his girlfriend, Kristin Spodobalski.

article_content: A rural stadium is set to be constructed in Sahaspur Alinagar, the ancestral village of Indian pacer Mohammed Shami, according to Amroha District Magistrate Rajesh Kumar Tyagi. The stadium will span 1.092 hectares and is expected to cost around Rs 5 crore. Tyagi stated that efforts will be made to invite Shami to the foundation stone-laying ceremony, schedule permitting, and that Shami’s parents will also receive invitations. The exact date for the ceremony has not yet been decided. The initiative is part of a broader state government plan to construct rural stadiums across 20 districts. Mohammed Shami has drawn national attention through his outstanding performance in the ongoing Cricket World Cup, leading India as the top wicket-taker with 23 wickets in six matches at an economy rate of 5.01. Notably, he took seven wickets in the semifinal against New Zealand in Mumbai last Tuesday.

article_content: Liverpool moved closer to their first English league title since 1990 after a dramatic 3-2 victory over Manchester City at Anfield on Sunday. The match was played in an emotionally charged atmosphere, as it came on the 25th anniversary of the Hillsborough disaster. Prior to kick-off, tributes honored the 96 Liverpool fans who died in 1989. The win put Liverpool two points ahead of Chelsea, who later beat Swansea 1-0, and seven points clear of third-placed Manchester City, who have two games in hand. Philippe Coutinho scored the decisive goal in the 78th minute, capitalizing on a wayward clearance by City defender Vincent Kompany. Liverpool managed to hold their lead despite being reduced to ten men after Jordan Henderson received a red card for a late challenge on Samir Nasri in injury time. Liverpool captain Steven Gerrard showed emotion at the final whistle, gathering his teammates in a huddle. He later described the match as one of the toughest of his career, emphasizing the importance of the result. Meanwhile, Manchester City manager Manuel Pellegrini lamented his side’s missed opportunities, noting that Liverpool’s early two-goal lead made their task more difficult. Liverpool, recording their 10th consecutive Premier League win, started strongly with first-half goals from Raheem Sterling and Martin Skrtel. Manchester City fought back after the break, leveling through David Silva and a Glen Johnson own goal, but Coutinho’s late strike restored Liverpool’s advantage. Earlier in the weekend, all English football matches included tributes to the Hillsborough victims. A memorial service is set to take place at Anfield on Tuesday, exactly 25 years after the tragedy. A new inquest into the disaster recently began following the High Court’s decision to overturn the original coroner’s verdict, amid concerns over police conduct that day. Chelsea kept up the pressure in the title race with a narrow win at Swansea, secured by a Demba Ba goal in the 68th minute. Swansea were reduced to ten men following Chico Flores’ early red card. In the FA Cup, Hull City reached their first final after defeating Sheffield United 5-3 at Wembley. Hull will face Arsenal, who beat Wigan on penalties in the other semifinal. Sheffield United took the lead through Jose Baxter and Stefan Scougall, but Hull responded with goals from Matty Fryatt, Tom Huddlestone, Stephen Quinn, and David Meyler. In Spain, Atletico Madrid extended their lead at the top of La Liga with a 2-0 win at Getafe. Diego Godin and Diego Costa scored, with Costa suffering a minor injury in the process but expected to be fit for the next match. Atletico lead Real Madrid, with Barcelona a further point behind, as the season enters its final stretch.

Segern gav Liverpool ett försprång på två poäng mot Chelsea, som senare slog Swansea med 1-0, och sju poängs ledning över trean Manchester City, som dock har två matcher mindre spelade. Philippe Coutinho avgjorde matchen i den 78:e minuten efter att Manchester Citys Vincent Kompany misslyckats med en rensning. Lagkaptenen Steven Gerrard visade starka känslor efter slutsignalen när han samlade laget i en ring. Han beskrev senare matchen som en av de tuffaste i sin karriär och betonade resultatets betydelse. Manchester Citys tränare Manuel Pellegrini uttryckte besvikelse över de missade chanserna och menade att Liverpools tidiga tvåmålsledning försvårade uppgiften. Liverpool tog sin tionde raka Premier League-seger och inledde starkt med mål av Raheem Sterling och Martin Skrtel i första halvlek. Manchester City kom tillbaka efter paus och kvitterade genom David Silva och ett självmål av Glen Johnson, men Coutinhos sena mål gav Liverpool segern. Tidigare under helgen hedrades Hillsborough-offren under samtliga engelska fotbollsmatcher. En minnesceremoni hålls på Anfield på tisdag, exakt 25 år efter tragedin. En ny utredning om katastrofen har nyligen inletts efter att Högsta domstolen upphävde den ursprungliga rättsläkarens dom, med hänvisning till misstänkta brister i polisens agerande den dagen. Chelsea behöll trycket i titelracet genom att vinna knappt borta mot Swansea, med Demba Ba som målskytt i den 68:e minuten. Swansea spelade med en man mindre efter att Chico Flores fått ett rött kort tidigt i matchen. I FA-cupen gick Hull City till sin första final någonsin efter att ha besegrat Sheffield United med 5-3 på Wembley. Hull möter Arsenal, som slog ut Wigan på straffar i den andra semifinalen. Sheffield United tog ledningen genom Jose Baxter och Stefan Scougall, men Hull vände med mål av Matty Fryatt, Tom Huddlestone, Stephen Quinn och David Meyler. I Spanien utökade Atletico Madrid sin ligaledning genom att vinna med 2-0 borta mot Getafe. Diego Godin och Diego Costa gjorde målen, varav Costa fick en lättare skada i samband med sitt mål, men väntas vara spelklar till nästa match. Atletico leder före Real Madrid, medan Barcelona är ytterligare en poäng bakom, när ligasäsongen närmar sig sitt slut.

article_content: For nearly fifty years, farmer Doug Goulbourne lived without running water. Since age 21, he carried buckets to and from an old water pump at Widow Croft Farm in Hollingworth, Greater Manchester, just to bathe or collect drinking water. Now, at 72, Goulbourne has been connected to a mains water supply for the first time. He celebrated by turning on the tap, filling his kettle, and making a cup of tea. Since 1962, his daily routine included a trek to a worn-out water pump in a ditch 50 yards from his home after moving with his parents. For years, he rescued frogs from the 166-year-old pump at dawn, but now he enjoys easy access to water at any time. Goulbourne expressed delight, saying that having running water makes life much easier and it is fantastic to just turn on the tap. He moved to the farm at 21, inheriting it from his father in the late 1960s. Built in 1837, the farm used a gravity-fed tank from streams, requiring constant maintenance and early mornings. The old pump sometimes froze or failed, especially in harsh seasons, meaning Goulbourne often had to make repairs himself. He began each day at 5:30 AM, collecting water after caring for his animals, including a pet cow named Susan, 60 cattle, and four dogs. Despite these challenges, he had not considered connecting to the mains supply until United Utilities offered it as part of a £3 million scheme expanding the water network to remote properties, benefitting Goulbourne and over 30 other homes. Describing his old situation as 'like having a wooden leg,' Goulbourne said he managed with what was available, even during inconvenient breakdowns, often around Christmas. He acknowledged that mains water has made a tremendous difference, providing more time and cleaner water, since the old supply sometimes became polluted. Now, if he has issues with the water, he can simply call United Utilities for assistance. He noted that while people fetched water this way in the past, he is now grateful for the reliable, clean water in Britain. Graham Dent, project co-ordinator at United Utilities, pointed out the irony that homes so near a reservoir did not have mains water, but the new works will address this with minimal disruption to roads. In 2010, only 30,021 out of over 21 million households in England and Wales lacked mains water. Modern water supply in Britain began in the mid-19th century, replacing reliance on rivers and wells.
translated_content: I nästan femtio år levde bonden Doug Goulbourne utan rinnande vatten. Sedan han var 21 bar han hinkar till och från en gammal vattenpump på Widows Croft Farm i Hollingworth, Greater Manchester, bara för att bada eller hämta dricksvatten. Nu, vid 72 års ålder, har Goulbourne för första gången fått tillgång till vatten från vattenledningsnätet. Han firade genom att sätta på kranen, fylla vattenkokaren och göra sig en kopp te. Sedan 1962 har hans dagliga rutin varit att gå till en sliten vattenpump i ett dike 50 meter från huset efter att ha flyttat dit med sina föräldrar. I åratal räddade han grodor från den 166 år gamla pumpen tidigt på morgonen, men nu har han alltid enkelt tillgång till vatten. Goulbourne uttryckte sin glädje och sade att rinnande vatten gör livet mycket enklare och att det är fantastiskt att bara kunna vrida på kranen. Han flyttade till gården vid 21 års ålder och ärvde den från sin far i slutet av 1960-talet. Gården, byggd 1837, använde en gravitationsmatad tank fylld av vatten från bäckar, vilket krävde ständig tillsyn och tidiga morgnar. Den gamla pumpen frös ibland eller slutade fungera, särskilt under hårda årstider, vilket gjorde att Goulbourne ofta fick laga den själv. Varje dag började han klockan 05:30 med att hämta vatten efter att ha tagit hand om sina djur, bland annat en kossa som hette Susan, 60 nötkreatur och fyra hundar. Trots utmaningarna funderade han inte på att ansluta till vattenledningen förrän United Utilities erbjöd det som del av ett projekt värt 3 miljoner pund, vilket expanderade nätet till avlägsna fastigheter och gynnade Goulbourne samt över 30 andra hushåll. Han beskrev sin tidigare situation som 'som att ha ett träben' och sade att han klarade sig med det som fanns, även när pumpen ofta gick sönder, särskilt runt jul. Han erkände att rinnande vatten har gjort en enorm skillnad, gett honom mer tid och renare vatten, då den gamla källan ibland blev förorenad. Nu, om det uppstår problem med vattnet, kan han enkelt ringa United Utilities. Han noterade att även om folk förr hämtade vatten på detta sätt, är han nu tacksam för tillgången till rent, pålitligt vatten i Storbritannien. Graham Dent, projektledare på United Utilities, påpekade ironin i att hus så nära en reservoar saknade vatten från ledningsnätet, men nu åtgärdas detta med minimal påverkan på vägarna. År 2010 saknade endast 30 021 av över 21 miljoner hushåll i England och Wales vatten från ledningsnätet. Det moderna vattennätet i Storbritannien började byggas i mitten av 1800-talet och ersatte i stort sett bruket av floder och brunnar.

article_content: Jonathan Waters, the former director of Ohio State University's marching band, was fired after a university-led investigation into reports of sexual harassment and a hostile environment in the band. The university concluded Waters was aware or should have been aware of the ongoing misconduct. Waters' lawyer, David F. Axelrod, criticized the investigation as inadequate, arguing that only four current band members and a handful of alumni were interviewed among hundreds eligible, casting doubt on the report’s credibility. The university cited traditions in the band with sexually explicit elements, including the so-called 'midnight ramp' where members allegedly entered the stadium in their underwear with staff present. Axelrod refuted this, saying participation wasn’t required and some members wore more modest clothing. He supported his claims with testimonials from former band members. Complicating matters, an audio recording was released featuring Waters sternly reprimanding a band member. Axelrod admitted Waters was aware of some issues but insisted he worked to address them based on his own experience as a band member. Nevertheless, university leadership determined that Waters’ actions as director were insufficient according to Ohio State’s standards. OSU President Michael Drake stressed the importance of student safety and community standards. Following the controversy, the university appointed former Ohio Attorney General Betty Montgomery to head an independent task force investigating the band’s culture and recommending reforms. Ohio State’s marching band, which gained national attention for creative halftime shows, is recognized as one of the leading college bands.

Universitetet drog slutsatsen att Waters kände till eller borde ha känt till den pågående misskötseln. Waters advokat, David F. Axelrod, kritiserade utredningen som otillräcklig och hävdade att endast fyra nuvarande bandmedlemmar och ett fåtal alumner intervjuades, trots att det fanns hundratals möjliga, vilket ifrågasätter rapportens trovärdighet. Universitetet pekade på traditioner inom bandet med sexuellt explicit innehåll, inklusive den så kallade 'midnattsrampen', där medlemmar enligt uppgift gick in på stadion i underkläder med personal närvarande. Axelrod motsatte sig detta och hävdade att deltagandet inte var obligatoriskt och att vissa medlemmar bar mer täckande kläder. Han stödde sina påståenden med vittnesmål från tidigare bandmedlemmar. Situationen förvärrades när en ljudinspelning släpptes där Waters hörs skarpt tillrättavisa en bandmedlem. Trots detta ansåg universitetsledningen att Waters agerande som ledare inte räckte enligt Ohio States normer. OSU:s ordförande Michael Drake betonade vikten av studenternas säkerhet och gemensamma värderingar. Efter kontroversen utsåg universitetet före detta Ohios justitieminister Betty Montgomery att leda en oberoende arbetsgrupp som ska granska bandets kultur och föreslå reformer. Ohio States marschband, som fått nationell uppmärksamhet för sina kreativa halvtidsshower, är känt som en av de ledande studentorkestrarna i landet.

article_content: At the Paris Peace Forum, Microsoft President Brad Smith said Russia is actively spreading disinformation about the Middle East, especially during the conflict between Israel and Hamas. Smith explained that Microsoft and other major tech companies are using artificial intelligence tools to help detect fabricated or altered online content. He clarified (in statements translated by French radio France Inter) that technology platforms have three main options when dealing with this kind of content: ignore it, remove it, or flag it clearly as manipulated, and highlighted that there’s no agreed standard for which approach to take. Smith also referenced previous Russian disinformation campaigns, such as spreading misinformation about COVID-19 vaccinations, and suggested similar tactics are being used now regarding Middle Eastern events. The Paris Peace Forum took place against a backdrop of rising global tensions, particularly after the recent escalation between Israel and Hamas following the October 7 attacks. According to Israel, those attacks left 1,200 people dead and 239 taken hostage. Israel’s subsequent operations in Gaza, according to the Hamas-run health ministry, have caused over 11,000 deaths, many among children. Meanwhile, French President Emmanuel Macron, speaking to the BBC, condemned the Hamas attacks while urging Israel to stop bombing civilians in Gaza, arguing that such actions lead to further resentment and can’t be justified. The article also covers unrelated business topics, like Diwali gift-giving in Indian companies, potential impacts of new Indian data laws, and a recent downgrade of the US credit outlook by Moody’s, but these do not relate to the disinformation discussion.

In Lake Wales, Florida, four generations of the Shepard family celebrated Darcy Shepard’s 18th birthday by skydiving together. At the heart of the adventure was their 94-year-old matriarch, Harriett Shepard, whose example inspired relatives both young and old. For the Shepards, skydiving has become a cherished tradition, complementing their previous group adventures such as scuba diving and hang gliding.

Harriett, who had already taken a jump at age 91, returned to the skies and became the oldest person to skydive at the Florida Skydiving Center. She was joined by Darcy, her son Dave (74), her grandson Dallas (45), great-grandson Trevor Muir (23), and other family members and friends. Originally invited to watch, Harriett insisted on participating herself.

After attending training at the Lake Wales Airport and pairing with tandem instructors, eight family members took off in a DeHavilland Twin Otter and leapt from 14,000 feet, with Harriett leading the way. Fearless as ever, she floated down gently in her favorite sandals, saying she found it thrilling to share the experience with her family. Her great-grandchildren described her as always up for adventure.

One by one, each family member landed safely, greeted by excited relatives below. Darcy received a round of birthday applause and plenty of hugs—including one from her great-grandmother. Family members said the group jump was "incredible" and "unforgettable," especially with all four generations taking part. Despite a lifetime of interesting pursuits as an author, photographer, and architect, Harriett joked that she hopes the skydiving isn’t the only thing people remember her for.

An 8.0-magnitude earthquake struck off the coast of the Solomon Islands in the South Pacific on Wednesday, triggering a tsunami that claimed five lives but did not threaten the broader region. According to Augustine Bilve, director at a hospital in Lata, the main town of the affected area, four elderly people and one child died after a wave approximately one meter (three feet) high hit the Santa Cruz Islands, an eastern part of the Solomon Islands. The strong waves caused damage at the local airport and in neighboring villages. Although the hospital itself remained undamaged, some patients were relocated as a precaution.

Andrew Catford, World Vision's program director in the Solomon Islands, reported that staff in Temotu province (another name for the Santa Cruz Islands) felt the quake, and within five minutes experienced multiple surge waves that flooded the airport runway. World Vision indicated it was still assessing the full extent of the damage, but believed several villages near the airport were severely impacted.

The Pacific Tsunami Warning Center initially issued tsunami warnings for nearby countries, including Papua New Guinea and Fiji, but later canceled them after further analysis. A broader tsunami watch covering nations such as New Zealand, Australia, and Indonesia was also lifted. The US Geological Survey (USGS) reported the earthquake's epicenter was near the Santa Cruz Islands. The quake's depth was first estimated at 3.6 miles, later revised to 17.8 miles.

In response to the earthquake, regional authorities enacted precautionary measures. The New Zealand Ministry of Civil Defense and Emergency Management advised residents along parts of the west coast to avoid the water and shorelines. In Japan, authorities warned of possible minor sea level changes along the eastern coast. The New Caledonia High Commission in Noumea ordered immediate evacuations on the eastern coast and Loyalty Islands.

The main earthquake was preceded by a 6.3-magnitude tremor and followed by several aftershocks, the strongest of which registered 6.6 in magnitude. In 2007, an 8.1-magnitude earthquake struck the western Solomon Islands, causing a tsunami that killed at least 52 people and left thousands homeless.

Reporting by CNN's Sarita Harilela, Jethro Mullen, and Dave Alsup.

En jordbävning med magnituden 8,0 inträffade utanför Solomonöarna i södra Stilla havet på onsdagen, vilket utlöste en tsunami som krävde fem liv, men som inte hotade det bredare området. Enligt Augustine Bilve, chef på sjukhuset i Lata, huvudorten i det drabbade området, dog fyra äldre personer och ett barn efter att en cirka en meter hög våg nådde Santa Cruz-öarna, en östlig del av Solomonöarna. De kraftiga vågorna orsakade skador på den lokala flygplatsen och i närliggande byar. Sjukhuset klarade sig utan skador, men vissa patienter flyttades i förebyggande syfte.

Andrew Catford, programchef för World Vision i Solomonöarna, rapporterade att personal i Temotu-provinsen (ett annat namn för Santa Cruz-öarna) kände jordskalvet och inom fem minuter upplevde flera vågsvall som översvämmade landningsbanan. World Vision meddelade att de fortfarande utvärderar skadornas omfattning, men tror att flera byar nära flygplatsen drabbats hårt.

Pacific Tsunami Warning Center utfärdade inledningsvis tsunamivarningar för närliggande länder, däribland Papua Nya Guinea och Fiji, men drog senare tillbaka dessa efter ytterligare analys. En bredare tsunamivarning för länder som Nya Zeeland, Australien och Indonesien hävdes också. US Geological Survey (USGS) rapporterade att jordbävningens epicentrum låg nära Santa Cruz-öarna. Skalvets djup uppskattades först till 5,8 kilometer, men korrigerades senare till 28,6 kilometer.

Som svar på jordbävningen vidtog regionala myndigheter försiktighetsåtgärder. Nya Zeelands katastrof- och beredskapsmyndighet rådde invånare längs delar av västkusten att hålla sig borta från vattnet och strandlinjen. I Japan varnade myndigheterna för möjliga mindre förändringar i havsnivån längs östkusten. Högkommissionen i Nya Kaledonien i Nouméa beordrade omedelbar evakuering av kustinvånare på östra kusten och på Loyaltyöarna.

Det huvudsakliga skalvet föregicks av ett jordskalv med magnituden 6,3 och följdes av flera efterskalv, det kraftigaste på 6,6. År 2007 drabbades västra Solomonöarna av en jordbävning på 8,1, vilken utlöste en tsunami som dödade minst 52 personer och gjorde tusentals hemlösa.

Rapportering av Sarita Harilela, Jethro Mullen och Dave Alsup för CNN.

article_content: OpenAI is preparing to roll out significant updates to its AI developer tools, including the addition of memory storage and advanced vision features. These enhancements are designed to lower usage expenses and expand the capabilities available to developers. Reuters reports the new features will be formally introduced at OpenAI’s first developer conference, DevDay, in San Francisco on November 6. Until now, OpenAI’s voice and image features were exclusive to consumers, enabling ChatGPT to hear, see, and respond vocally. The company now plans to provide these capabilities to developers, allowing them to build AI systems capable of interpreting images and context. A key update is the launch of memory storage—expected to reduce costs for developers by as much as twenty times, addressing a major obstacle in AI development. OpenAI faces intensifying competition from tech firms like Meta, which recently unveiled AI-enabled Ray-Ban smart glasses and maintains the open-source Llama 2 model. There is also speculation about OpenAI collaborating with designer Jony Ive on hardware, though any release is likely far off. Analyst Ben Thompson has observed that while ChatGPT's conversational abilities are impressive, its vision features may still need refinement for typical consumers. Even so, these tools have enormous potential for industries such as manufacturing, quality assurance, and healthcare. At the same time, CEO Sam Altman has acknowledged lower-than-expected adoption of OpenAI’s plugins. With the developer conference approaching, OpenAI hopes to win developer interest over open-source alternatives. OpenAI did not respond to a request for comment from Gizmodo.
translated_content: OpenAI förbereder sig för att lansera betydande uppdateringar av sina AI-utvecklarverktyg, inklusive tillägget av minneslagring och avancerade synfunktioner. Dessa förbättringar är utformade för att sänka användningskostnaderna och utöka funktionaliteten för utvecklare. Reuters rapporterar att de nya funktionerna officiellt kommer att presenteras på OpenAIs första utvecklarkonferens, DevDay, i San Francisco den 6 november. Hittills har OpenAIs röst- och bildfunktioner varit exklusiva för konsumenter och gjort det möjligt för ChatGPT att höra, se och svara med röst. Företaget planerar nu att ge dessa möjligheter till utvecklare, så att de kan bygga AI-system som tolkar bilder och sammanhang. En viktig uppdatering är införandet av minneslagring – detta kan minska utvecklarnas kostnader med upp till tjugo gånger och lösa en stor utmaning inom AI-utveckling. OpenAI står inför ökad konkurrens från teknikbolag som Meta, som nyligen lanserade AI-utrustade Ray-Ban-glasögon och den öppna modellen Llama 2. Det ryktas även att OpenAI samarbetar med designern Jony Ive om hårdvara, men något släpp verkar ligga långt bort. Analytikern Ben Thompson har noterat att även om ChatGPT:s samtalsförmåga imponerar, kan synfunktionerna behöva förbättras för konsumentmarknaden. Däremot finns stor potential för dessa verktyg inom branscher som tillverkning, kvalitetskontroll och sjukvård. Samtidigt har VD Sam Altman erkänt att användningen av OpenAIs plugins inte nått de förväntade nivåerna. Inför utvecklarkonferensen hoppas OpenAI locka utvecklare från open source-alternativ. article_content: Michael Ha, 21, was born and raised in a modest East London council house by Chinese parents who spoke little English and relied on benefits. He attended an inner-city state school that was once called the ‘worst in Britain’. At just ten years old, Michael decided he wanted to go to Cambridge University, determined not to let adversity stand in his way. Now, after achieving top A-level results, Michael is a standout medical student at St John’s College, Cambridge, having recently received an award for academic excellence. Sharing his story, he hopes to inspire other young people from disadvantaged backgrounds. He explained, 'My parents couldn’t find work because their English wasn’t good enough. It was tough, but we managed. I never knew anything different.' Michael’s father, Bao Van Ha, 67, worked as a factory welder in Vietnam before moving to Britain in 1980 with his wife, Yen Thang Trinh, 58, who worked as a seamstress. The family lived in a small terraced house in Hackney, an area with issues of petty crime and gang activity. As the youngest of four siblings, Michael recalled, 'There was always trouble on the streets of Hackney—it could be scary. A couple of times people tried to mug me, but I managed to keep out of trouble by staying focused.' At age 11, Michael started at the newly-established Mossbourne Academy, which replaced Hackney Downs School, previously described by a Conservative government as 'the worst school in Britain'. The new school was led by inspirational headteacher Sir Michael Wilshaw, who is now Chief Inspector of Schools at Ofsted. In addition to excelling in his A-levels, Michael achieved an A in AS-level further maths after teaching himself from a textbook in four months, as a challenge with a friend. 'I always saw Cambridge as this mythical place for the best students,' he said. 'I was ambitious and dreamt of going there.' Michael applied to study medicine at St John’s College, one of the most competitive courses, and will continue his studies at Addenbrooke’s Hospital, Cambridge, aiming to become a reconstructive surgeon. 'I want other people to know they shouldn’t be afraid of Cambridge and Oxford,' he said. 'Tutors are simply looking for the brightest students. If you work hard, it’s within your reach.'

'Jag vill att andra ska veta att de inte ska vara rädda för Cambridge och Oxford,' sa han. 'Lärarna letar helt enkelt efter de smartaste studenterna. Om du arbetar hårt är det inom räckhåll.'

article_content: During the winter at New Hampshire's Lake Winnipesaukee, activities like ice fishing and hockey tournaments are common, and, when the ice is thick enough, airplanes can also land on the lake. After a season of poor ice and unfavorable weather, the Alton Bay Seaplane Base and its unique ice runway are now open. Dozens of pilots from the Northeast took advantage of a rare sunny, storm-free Saturday to land on the frozen lake, which is the only ice runway in the lower 48 states approved by the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA). Pilots parked their planes on the ice after flying into Alton, New Hampshire. It is the only FAA-approved ice runway in the contiguous United States. Ken Ortmann, a pilot from Rochester, New Hampshire, remarked, 'How many times can a non-amphibian plane land on water?' Angela Leedy, another pilot, flew three hours from Pittstown, New Jersey, to experience landing on the ice. Airport director Paul LaRochelle manages the 3,000-foot airstrip, keeping it plowed when the ice is safe. He directs pilots where to park and advises them not to use their brakes on the ice to avoid skidding. Although safety is stressed, occasional incidents do happen. For instance, last March, an experimental plane clipped a snowbank and made a hard landing, but the pilot was uninjured. After several weekends of snowstorms, pilots from across the Northeast finally got the chance to fly into Alton Bay's famous ice runway. Paul LaRochelle, the ice runway manager, guided pilots to parking spots. Pilots like Angela Leedy seized the opportunity to fly in from as far as New Jersey, while others, like Ken Ortmann, coordinated with air traffic control before taking off to ensure operations were conducted safely.

Governments around the world are increasingly asking Google to remove content, with Russia at the forefront of these demands. According to VPN company Surfshark, Russia made 61% of global content removal requests over the past decade, and the numbers keep rising. Last year, more than 90,000 requests were made worldwide—a 50% jump from the previous year—and Russia was responsible for 58,000 of them.

Google’s bi-annual transparency reports show that 150 countries have made removal requests in the past ten years. Still, most nations submitted fewer than 100, while just six countries accounted for more than 10,000 each, making up the vast majority of the total.

Surfshark’s lead researcher, Agneska Sablovskaja, explained, “The number of government requests to take down Google content has nearly multiplied thirteenfold in the past decade—growing from 7,000 to 91,000 a year. Protecting national security is the most frequent reason for these requests.”

Many of these government requests target multiple pieces of content at once. Over the decade, 355,000 requests accounted for 3.87 million separate items—averaging 11 items per request. The largest share is aimed at YouTube, followed by Google Search and Blogger. Some requests also focus on mapping services, given the sensitivity over national borders and military locations, as well as Google Images.

The uptick in removal requests from Russia is linked to its invasion of Ukraine, which started in February 2022. Russia’s government most commonly cites national security and copyright in its submissions.

Surfshark’s report highlights ongoing debate about whether these removals serve public safety or cross into excessive censorship.
