article_content: On November 26, 2011, Pope Benedict XVI emphasized that sexual abuse is an issue affecting all sectors of society, not just the Church. Speaking to U.S. bishops at the Vatican, he alluded to recent high-profile American cases of abuse outside of religious institutions. The Pope described child abuse as a 'scourge' impacting the whole of society, acknowledging that longstanding scandals involving clergy have deeply unsettled U.S. Catholics. Pope Benedict stressed that every institution should be held to rigorous standards in responding to child sexual abuse, not just the Church. He stated, 'It is my hope that the Church's dedicated efforts to confront this reality will help the broader community to recognize the causes, full extent, and serious consequences of sexual abuse, and to respond to this problem effectively.' Recent years have seen major abuse scandals at institutions outside the Church, such as the case involving Penn State University’s former football coach, Jerry Sandusky, who was charged with sexual abuse of eight boys. The scandal led to significant leadership changes at the university, including the dismissal of long-serving coach Joe Paterno and the resignation of university president Graham Spanier. College football is a highly prominent part of U.S. culture, and the case has significantly impacted Penn State's reputation. The Pope did not address allegations by victims and advocates that Church officials, including the Vatican office he previously led, systematically covered up cases of abuse and were rarely held accountable. Investigations have shown that offending priests were often transferred between parishes instead of being removed. Reflecting on his 2008 visit to the United States, Pope Benedict said the trip was aimed at supporting American Catholics following the crisis caused by these scandals. He personally acknowledged the suffering endured by victims and recognized the efforts made to protect children and deal transparently with abuse allegations. Some within the Church have argued that religious institutions have been unfairly singled out for criticism regarding abuse. The bishops were visiting Rome as part of their regular consultations with the Vatican, which are scheduled every five years.

article_content: Bill Maher's Real Time aired its Thanksgiving episode, which is normally the season's final show before a break. Because of the Writers Guild strikes, the show will continue into December—a reason to be thankful. On Friday's episode, Maher welcomed comic legends Rob Reiner and Albert Brooks, whose wit and storytelling allowed Maher to relax and enjoy the conversation. Reiner and Brooks appeared to promote their new HBO documentary, 'Albert Brooks: Defending My Life.' With a longstanding friendship dating back to high school, the duo shared humorous stories, including Brooks' first meeting with Reiner and entertaining moments at the Reiner home. They also reminisced about living together in Benedict Canyon, joked about visiting friends, discussed precise routines, and mentioned Brooks turning down a permanent hosting opportunity for Saturday Night Live. The week's panel featured Donna Brazile, a Georgetown University professor and acclaimed media contributor, and Adam Kinzinger, a former Republican Congressman and author. The conversation touched on politics, from Trump to young voters to TikTok. In his 'New Rules' editorial, Maher advised viewers against sharing opinions on topics they don't fully understand—an apt message for Thanksgiving gatherings.

article_content: Joanne Jackson, 43, from Dewsbury in West Yorkshire, has decorated her body with 17 tattoos, including over her mastectomy scars, each representing a chapter of her life. Diagnosed with breast cancer in June 2011, she had a mastectomy and underwent reconstructive surgery using fat from her stomach. Refusing to let cancer diminish her self-confidence, Joanne chose to express her resilience through tattoos. She calls her body art a statement and a testament to her strength through adversity. Joanne says, 'I don't drink and I don't smoke, but ink is my thing. I collect fine art—it's just on my body, not my walls.' Joanne is married to Andrew, 47, and has two sons: Evan, aged 7, and Connah, aged 22. She received her first tattoo, a small bird on her thigh, at 21. Today, she has a full sleeve on her left arm featuring strong women, Geisha girls, and Samurai warriors, crafted over 20 hours and five sessions by tattoo artist Matt Evans at Slawit Ink, Slaithwaite. Among her most striking tattoos is a colourful peacock, created by Kim Walsh from Ink Station in Heckmondwike. The blue tail feathers of the peacock sweep across Joanne’s stomach, masking the scars from reconstructive surgery. The tattoo has taken 14 hours so far and will be completed soon. Joanne shares, 'It's a stunning piece. It marks an end to what I have been through.' Joanne's other tattoos carry deep meaning, such as a cancer ribbon on her back and an image of a breastfeeding mother with four lilies, symbolizing the four miscarriages she suffered. She also features Eleanor Roosevelt quotes on her left thigh, including, 'You gain strength and courage by every experience in which you really stop to look fear in the face. You are able to say to yourself, I have lived through this horror and I can take the next thing that comes along. You must do the thing you think you cannot do.' In 2012, Joanne commissioned professional photographs of herself posing topless following her mastectomy, aiming to show that women can still feel sexy and confident after surgery. She shared these photos on Facebook, but the platform later removed them and threatened to close her account, which frustrated her. Although Joanne is running out of space for new tattoos, she has a few more designs planned for her thighs and ribs. She concludes, 'I know tattoos aren’t everyone’s cup of tea, but they’ve come a long way from being associated with yobs and thugs. Tattoos are a true art form, and I have found some amazing tattoo artists. This is my thing, and I’m growing old disgracefully!'

Joannes övriga tatueringar är också fyllda av betydelse, som ett cancerband på ryggen och en bild av en ammande mamma med fyra liljor, som symboliserar de fyra missfall hon gått igenom. Hon har även citat från Eleanor Roosevelt på sitt vänstra lår, bland annat: 'Du får styrka och mod av varje erfarenhet där du verkligen slutar upp för att möta rädslan. Du kan säga till dig själv, jag har överlevt den här fasan och jag kan ta nästa sak som kommer. Du måste göra det du tror att du inte klarar.' År 2012 tog Joanne professionella bilder där hon poserade topless efter sin mastektomi, för att visa att kvinnor kan känna sig sexiga och självsäkra även efter operationen. Hon delade bilderna på Facebook, men plattformen tog bort dem och hotade att stänga hennes konto, vilket gjorde henne frustrerad. Trots att Joanne börjar få ont om plats för fler tatueringar, har hon planer för några till på sina lår och revben. Hon avslutar: 'Jag vet att tatueringar inte är allas grej, men de har verkligen kommit långt från att förknippas med busar och ligister. Tatueringar är en konstform och jag har hittat fantastiska tatuerare. Det här är min grej och jag tänker åldras med stil!'

article_content: The U.S. Justice Department is enacting a significant policy change, reversing its long-standing resistance to recording suspect interviews. For many years, federal agents were not required to make electronic recordings of custodial interrogations, largely because of concerns that such recordings could benefit defendants. However, a new memorandum from Deputy Attorney General James Cole—first reported by the Arizona Republic—outlines that beginning July 11, most interviews with individuals held in custody after arrest but before their initial court appearance must be electronically recorded if equipment is available. This revised policy applies to several major agencies, including the FBI, ATF, DEA, and U.S. Marshals Service. The memo, which is dated May 12, was circulated without public announcement; law enforcement officials have confirmed its authenticity, though the Justice Department has declined to officially comment. There are specified exceptions: interviews related to national security or intelligence, those under the public safety exception to Miranda rights, and interviews conducted before arrest are not required to be recorded. Electronic recordings of suspect statements are already widespread among state and local police agencies, and are standard practice for the Justice Department’s inspector general. Previously, the Department discouraged such recordings, which often meant agents would need to defend hand-written notes during high-profile trials.

PM:et daterat 12 maj skickades ut utan offentlig annonsering; poliskällor har bekräftat dess äkthet, även om justitiedepartementet har avstått från officiella kommentarer. Elektronisk inspelning av misstänktas uttalanden är redan praxis bland statliga och lokala polismyndigheter och är standard för departementets egen internrevision. Prominent Chinese-Australian artist Guo Jian has been detained by Chinese authorities ahead of the 25th anniversary of the Tiananmen Square crackdown, according to friends. His arrest followed a Financial Times profile featuring his latest artwork: a diorama of Tiananmen Square covered in ground meat. In the article, Guo was highly critical of the People's Liberation Army's actions during the 1989 incident, in which he had previously served as a soldier in the late 1970s.

Guo was taken from his home in eastern Beijing Sunday night and notified friends of his arrest via text message. Artist Melanie Wang told the Sydney Morning Herald she called Guo after receiving his message; he informed her he had been taken to a detention center and was told he would be released in 15 days.

Guo actively participated in the 1989 pro-democracy demonstrations, which lasted for weeks and ended when PLA troops opened fire on mostly student protestors in the heart of Beijing. The FT article published on May 30 revealed that Guo also took part in a hunger strike during those protests. Another friend told CNN he attempted to call Guo after the FT piece was published but received a reply indicating that Guo was "with police," followed by another message instructing him not to call. Later, the friend received a text in Chinese saying Guo had gone to Tongzhou police station near the Songzhuang art colony where he lives and works.

Guo’s new artwork has been described by friends as provocative, and they speculate that both the nature of the art and the upcoming anniversary contributed to his detention. Guo was aware of the risks and asked friends to keep his project confidential until it was completed, fearing interference from authorities. He intended the work as a commemoration of the Tiananmen massacre.

The Australian government issued a statement Monday offering assistance to Guo, who is an Australian passport holder. "The Australian Embassy in Beijing has contacted Chinese authorities to seek further information regarding Mr. Guo Jian's detention and to underline our strong interest in the matter," a Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade spokesperson said. "The Australian Government stands ready to provide all possible consular assistance."

Amnesty International also condemned Guo's arrest, noting an increase in detentions of dissidents in the lead-up to the 25th anniversary, compared to previous years. Authorities across China have reportedly detained several prominent critics and activists before the anniversary on June 4. William Nee, China Researcher at Amnesty International, called Guo "the latest victim of the Chinese authorities' merciless campaign of repression ahead of the Tiananmen anniversary," urging immediate release of all those detained for speaking out peacefully about the 1989 events.

Responding to criticism of China's human rights record, Ministry of Foreign Affairs spokesperson Hua Chunying previously told CNN that human rights should not be judged by U.S. standards. "Our society is moving forward, people's living standards have improved, and levels of freedom are at their highest," she said.

In the FT article, Guo recalled the night troops opened fire on protesters, stating, "I didn't believe it, even though I had been a soldier. In the army I had never seen that sort of violence. Then I saw the tracers and people falling around me—they were just gone. I suddenly realized, this was war." No official death toll has ever been released for the 1989 crackdown, but estimates range from hundreds to thousands, with most victims killed by PLA soldiers.

Financial Times-artikeln, publicerad den 30 maj, avslöjade också att Guo deltog i en hungerstrejk under protesterna. Guos nya konstverk beskrivs av vänner som provocerande, och de tror att både verkets karaktär och den kommande årsdagen kan ha bidragit till gripandet. Guo var medveten om riskerna och bad sina vänner hålla projektet hemligt tills det var klart, av rädsla för myndigheternas ingripande. Australiens regering gjorde på måndagen ett uttalande där de erbjuder stöd till Guo, som är australisk medborgare. "Australiens ambassad i Peking har kontaktat kinesiska myndigheter för att få mer information om Mr Guo Jians gripande och understryka vårt stora intresse för ärendet," sade en talesperson för utrikesdepartementet. "Regeringen står redo att ge all möjlig konsulär hjälp."

Även Amnesty International fördömde gripandet och noterade att fler dissidenter gripits inför 25-årsdagen än tidigare år. Myndigheter i hela Kina har rapporterats gripa flera framstående kritiker och aktivister inför årsdagen den 4 juni. William Nee, Kinaforskare på Amnesty International, beskrev Guo som "det senaste offret för de kinesiska myndigheternas skoningslösa förtryck inför årsdagen" och krävde att alla som fredligt uttryckt sig om händelserna 1989 omedelbart ska friges.

Som svar på kritik mot Kinas människorättssituation har utrikesministeriets talesperson Hua Chunying tidigare sagt till CNN att mänskliga rättigheter inte bör bedömas utifrån amerikanska kriterier. article_content: Honda is set to launch a new hydrogen-powered vehicle, the FCV, in March 2016. This clean-energy car produces only water as a by-product, offers a range of 300 miles (480km), and seats up to five people. Notably, it includes an external power feeder that can supply electricity to a home during emergencies. However, widespread adoption of hydrogen vehicles faces obstacles such as limited fueling infrastructure and challenges in hydrogen production and storage. While hydrogen is touted as a potential replacement for petrol due to its zero-emission credentials, producing pure hydrogen is complex and often expensive. Beyond Honda, other major carmakers like BMW, Toyota, Hyundai, Audi, and Mercedes are working on similar hydrogen vehicles. BMW’s rumored i5 would join its electric and hybrid models, while Toyota and Hyundai already have hydrogen cars available. Rumors also suggest upcoming models from Audi and Mercedes. Scientists continue seeking solutions to hydrogen storage. Researchers at Benaras Hindu University in India, led by Professor Viney Dixit, have found that carbon derived from coconut kernels could store significant amounts of hydrogen. The process is cost-effective and the raw materials are readily available. The FCV builds on Honda’s previous fuel-cell vehicle, the FCX Clarity, with improvements in power output—delivering over 100kW and a 60% increase in power density. It can be refueled in just three to five minutes, although hydrogen fueling stations remain scarce. Honda highlights its leadership in fuel-cell technology, citing two decades of development and experience, and emphasizes advancements in vehicle operation under varied conditions while meeting safety and customer expectations. The FCV's price and top speed have yet to be announced, with releases in the US and Europe planned after the initial launch in Japan.

article_content: Two billionaire brothers from Texas, Farris (60) and Dan Wilks (56), have quietly acquired more than 177,000 acres of Montana ranch land in the past two years near the Little Snowy Mountains. Their total holdings in Montana now exceed 276,000 acres across seven eastern counties, equivalent to 431 square miles—more than half the size of Silver Bow County. This places them among Montana’s largest landowners, surpassing even Turner Enterprises, owned by Ted Turner, which holds 149,000 acres in the state. Recently, billionaire Stanley Kroenke, who is married to a Wal-Mart heir, bought the 124,000-acre Broken O Ranch near Augusta for $132 million. Kroenke also owns Cedar Creek Ranch near Ennis and the PV Ranch near Hysham. The Wilks brothers have been especially active in Fergus County, purchasing 79,000 acres from ten landowners over two years. Their largest purchase, the famed 62,000-acre N Bar Ranch, was bought for $45 million from software billionaire Tom Siebel, attracting national attention. Other notable sellers include Theodore Roosevelt IV, who had a log lodge and timber land between the forks of Flatwillow Creek, and the Sunlight Ranch Co., owned by Earl Holding of Sinclair Oil. In Forbes, Staci Wilks of Wilks Brothers LLC said the Wilks brothers use their properties for hunting, fly fishing, farming, ranching, and wildlife management, often inviting friends, family, and corporate guests. This summer, the Wilks brothers held a barbecue at the N Bar Ranch, inviting locals to dine and socialize. Tom Lowry, a neighboring landowner, described them as friendly and approachable. While the Wilks brothers declined interviews, it’s known they grew up in a working-class family, began in their father’s masonry business, and in 2002 branched into the oil industry by founding Frac Tech. Their considerable wealth came after selling their stake in Frac Tech in 2011 for about $3.2 billion, landing them on Forbes’ billionaire list. Given their experience in oil and gas, some Montanans speculate that the brothers may pursue energy projects in central Montana, while others believe they’re investing as a safeguard in turbulent market times. Despite their large land purchases, the Wilks own less than one percent of Montana’s 147,200 square miles. The Wilks have also bought properties in Wyoming, Kansas, Texas, and Idaho. In Colorado, Farris Wilks reportedly paid $16 million for a seven-bedroom ski-accessible home in Snowmass Village. When visiting Montana, they travel by an 18-passenger Bombardier Global Express corporate jet, landing at Lewistown airport before using a helicopter to reach the N Bar Ranch. Construction of a 6,000-foot airstrip near their ranch headquarters is underway for more direct access in the future. In Fergus County, the Bureau of Land Management owns about 2,500 landlocked acres within the N Bar. Local BLM field manager Stan Benes said the agency is open to land exchange ideas, but any proposals would need public consideration and proof of public benefit. The primary Wilks purchases by county: 79,000 acres in Fergus; 64,000 acres in Musselshell (Pronghorn Ranch); 34,800 acres in Golden Valley; 15,200 acres in Meagher (between the Big Belt and Little Belt mountains near the Smith River); 22,800 acres in Blaine (Bears Paw Mountains); 48,300 acres in Garfield (southeast of Jordan); and 12,000 acres in Bighorn (near the Bighorn River)—all acquired in the past two years. Dan Tiegen, who considered selling his family’s large ranch north of Grass Range to the Wilks, said they first pursued a conservation easement for public hunting and protecting the land from development, but that fell through. Tiegen expressed concern about family ranches being bought by bigger entities, while Tom Lowry, the Wilks’ neighbor, said he is comfortable with their purchases and appreciates their openness. Lowry commented, 'If they’re buying up land, they can do what they want with it.'

article_content: A new study warns that humans are increasingly moving into areas prone to dangerous flooding, with China’s rapid urban growth playing a significant role. The research, conducted by World Bank economist Jun Rentschler and published in Nature, analyzed three decades of satellite images and global flood-risk maps. The study found that since 1985, the growth of settlements in flood-prone regions has far outpaced expansion in safer areas. By 2015, roughly 20% of all human settlements were located in zones with at least medium flood risk, compared to 17.9% three decades prior. While the percentage change seems modest, it represents a vast area due to worldwide urbanization. Rentschler estimates that about 76,400 square kilometers of settlements—around 48 times the size of Greater London—are now exposed to floods exceeding half a meter. These patterns, particularly noted in East Asia and the Pacific (notably China, Vietnam, and Bangladesh), make future exposure inevitable and create a growing need for expensive flood-protection infrastructure. In Vietnam, for instance, almost a third of the coastline is already built up, leaving fewer safe and productive locations and pushing new development onto risky floodplains and riverbeds. It's important to note that the study doesn’t factor in further flood risk increases from climate change, deforestation, or changing landscapes. Rentschler emphasizes that settlement expansion—rather than the enlargement of the flood zones themselves—is the main issue for management. While differences in flood protection between countries exist, the study focuses on rare and severe floods that can challenge even countries with advanced systems such as the Netherlands. Climate change is expected to heighten the likelihood of extreme floods, since warmer air holds more moisture. Rentschler argues that tracking and managing settlement patterns is an essential first step for policymakers: to reduce risks, countries must first avoid adding new ones. He says local authorities could do much more to protect their communities and mitigate future climate impacts.
translated_content: En ny studie varnar för att människor i allt högre grad bosätter sig i områden med hög översvämningsrisk, med Kinas snabba stadsutveckling som en betydande bidragande faktor. Forskningen, ledd av Världsbanksekonomen Jun Rentschler och publicerad i Nature, bygger på analyser av tre decennier av satellitbilder samt globala kartor över översvämningsrisker. Studien visar att ökningen av bosättningar i översvämningsdrabbade regioner sedan 1985 har varit betydligt större än expansionen i säkrare områden. År 2015 låg cirka 20 procent av alla bosättningar i områden med minst medelhög översvämningsrisk, jämfört med 17,9 procent trettio år tidigare. Även om ökningen i procent kan verka liten innebär det en enorm yta på grund av världsomspännande urbanisering. Rentschler uppskattar att ungefär 76 400 kvadratkilometer av bosättningar – nästan 48 gånger större än Stor-London – nu är utsatta för översvämningar på mer än en halv meter. Trenden är tydlig i Östasien och Stilla havet, särskilt i Kina, Vietnam och Bangladesh, vilket gör framtida utsatthet och behov av kostsamma översvämningsskydd oundvikligt. Till exempel är nästan en tredjedel av Vietnams kust redan utbyggd, vilket leder till att säkrare och mer lönsamma lägen är upptagna och att ny bebyggelse istället sker på riskfyllda marker, som flodslätter och flodbäddar. Det är värt att notera att studien inte tar hänsyn till ökade risker till följd av klimatförändringar, avskogning eller förändringar i landskapet. Rentschler betonar att det främst är var människor väljer att bosätta sig – snarare än att översvämningszoner växer – som är kärnfrågan för riskhantering. Studien pekar också på att det finns stora skillnader i skydd mot översvämningar mellan länder, men fokuserar på extrema och sällsynta översvämningar som kan överväldiga även de mest avancerade skyddssystem, som i Nederländerna. Klimatförändringarna tros göra kraftiga översvämningar vanligare, eftersom varm luft kan bära mer fukt. Rentschler framhåller att kartläggning och styrning av bosättningsmönster är en avgörande första åtgärd för beslutsfattare: innan riskerna kan minskas behöver länder sluta öka dem. Han menar att lokala myndigheter har stor potential att skydda människor och förebygga framtida effekter av klimatförändringarna.

article_content: Everyone I talk to seems exhausted. Exhausted by their marriage, their divorce, their last date, their day job, their dream job, their politics, their grief, their family, their friends, their fertility—even, or especially, their emails and algorithms. Most of what I mentioned involves life’s big issues, so it’s natural these require our effort and energy. But at a time when efficiency and productivity seem central, why do so many of us feel behind and inadequate? Here’s a simple truth that I’ve discovered: Not everything can be done in a hurry. Healing, for example, cannot be rushed. The major events in life often bring emotional baggage so heavy it can overwhelm us. Our wounds need more than a fleeting moment; we have to slow down to truly heal. Easier said than done. I recently recognized the shame I carried about the slower pace that physical and mental healing demands—especially during motherhood. As a chronic 'do-er,' I had trouble slowing down during my pregnancy and postpartum. When I was six months pregnant with my first daughter, I was living in London and had just come back from a work trip in Rwanda. The same day I landed, I insisted we meet friends at the Notting Hill Carnival. Having grown up attending Mardi Gras in New Orleans, dancing to live music in the street is something I love. But instead of listening to my tired body, I chased the excitement (and FOMO). I was so rundown that I fainted on the street. Thankfully, my partner caught me. I was in denial about my physical changes and the need to move through the world differently. Similarly, I believe my postpartum depression might have been less overwhelming if I hadn’t tried to rush my recovery; if I had accepted the need for slowness, or faced my insecurities, which tied my worth to always being productive. When you move slowly, you may not feel like yourself. It’s hard to love a stranger—especially when depression makes that stranger you. Awake at night, my racing heart amplified the words 'something is wrong with you' until they echoed through me. It was a lie that felt true, and I couldn’t silence it. Postpartum healing is different for everyone. For me, it began with patience and kindness toward myself. I allowed myself more time to do things and treated myself with compassion. Therapy, friends, and my partner all helped—but above all, slowing down made a big difference. We’re always in a rush, but where are we going? If we sprint to the end and can’t catch our breath, when do we experience life or joy? Speaking of joy, it, too, cannot be rushed. When modern spirituality says 'be present,' I think it means: slow down and soak it in. Enjoy your favorite song. Let your laughter turn into the tears you need. Breathe. Snuggle. Enjoy some sunlight. This is the good stuff of life, available if we make time for it. But it’s difficult to access joy without also allowing ourselves some ease. We rarely choose ease, even when it’s within reach. During my postpartum period, ease was available, but I didn’t know how to accept it. These days, choosing ease feels almost radical; it rejects the fixation on hustle and grind. Society tells us that discomfort enhances the value of our goals or relationships. While there can be wisdom in struggle, we can also grow and thrive without destroying ourselves—without missing out on life’s good things. We see retirement as the time when we’re finally allowed to prioritize ease, but do our moments of rest only belong at the end of life? I’m not suggesting quitting everything. This is the real world—we have to work and 'do.' But we also aren’t built to only do. We are beings, not machines, no matter how much time we spend with them. Being alive requires patience, as does bringing a life into the world and recovering afterward. If something on our phones takes too long to load, we assume it’s broken. I worry this has taught us that our own slowness is a flaw rather than a necessity for intentional living. Patience is a gift that welcomes presence, reflection, and healing. The reward for patience is the good stuff of life. When a website asks us to check a box that says, 'I am not a robot,' let’s treat that as a daily mantra. Slow down. The world’s pace doesn’t have to be yours. Re-pace. We’re not meant to move at the speed of Wi-Fi.
translated_content: Alla jag pratar med verkar utmattade. Utmattade av sitt äktenskap, sin skilsmässa, senaste dejten, sitt vanliga jobb, sitt drömjobb, sin politik, sin sorg, sin familj, sina vänner, sin fertilitet – till och med, eller framför allt, sina mejl och algoritmer. Det mesta jag nämnde handlar om livets stora frågor, så det är självklart att de kräver vår ansträngning och energi. Men i en tid då effektivitet och produktivitet står i centrum, varför känner sig så många av oss otillräckliga och efter? Här är en enkel sanning jag har upptäckt: Allt kan inte göras i all hast. Till exempel kan läkning inte forceras. De stora livshändelserna innebär ofta känslomässigt bagage så tungt att det kan överväldiga oss. Våra sår behöver mer än ett ögonblick; vi måste sakta ner för att kunna läka på riktigt. Lättare sagt än gjort. Jag insåg nyligen skammen jag bar på över det långsammare tempo som fysisk och mental läkning kräver – särskilt under moderskapet. Som en kronisk 'görare' hade jag svårt att sakta ner under graviditeten och efteråt. När jag var sex månader gravid med min första dotter bodde jag i London och hade precis kommit hem från en jobbresa till Rwanda. Samma dag som jag landade skulle vi träffa vänner på Notting Hill Carnival. Jag hade vuxit upp med Mardi Gras i New Orleans, så att dansa till livemusik på gatan är något jag älskar. Men istället för att lyssna på min trötta kropp följde jag med i upplevelsen (och FOMO). Jag var så utmattad att jag svimmade på gatan. Som tur var hann min partner fånga mig. Jag förnekade mina fysiska förändringar och behovet av att röra mig annorlunda i världen. På samma sätt tror jag att min förlossningsdepression hade varit mindre överväldigande om jag inte försökt skynda på min återhämtning; om jag accepterat långsamheten och mött mina osäkerheter, som kopplade mitt värde till att alltid prestera. När man rör sig långsamt kan det kännas som att man inte är sig själv. Det är svårt att älska en främling – särskilt när depressionen gör främlingen till dig. Vaken på natten förstärkte mitt rusande hjärta orden 'det är något fel på dig' tills de ekade inom mig. Det var en lögn som kändes sann, och jag kunde inte tysta den. Postpartum-återhämtning ser olika ut för alla. För mig började den med tålamod och vänlighet mot mig själv. Jag gav mig själv mer tid och mötte mig själv med omtanke. Terapi, vänner och min partner hjälpte, men framför allt hjälpte det att sakta ner. Vi är alltid på språng, men vart är vi egentligen på väg? Om vi springer till slutet och inte kan andas ut, när finner vi då livet och glädjen? På tal om glädje – den kan heller inte forceras. När modern andlighet säger 'var närvarande' tror jag att det betyder: sakta ner och ta in det. Känn din favoritlåt. Låt ditt skratt bli till de tårar du verkligen behöver. Andas. Mys. Få lite sol på ditt solskyddade ansikte. Det här är livets goda, som vi kan få om vi ger oss tid. Men det är svårt att nå livets goda utan att tillåta oss lätthet. Vi väljer sällan lätthet, även när den är inom räckhåll. Under min postpartumperiod fanns lätthet tillgängligt, men jag visste inte hur jag skulle ta emot det. Idag känns det nästan radikalt att välja lätthet; det går emot fixeringen vid att alltid vara igång. Samhället säger att svårigheter gör våra materiella mål eller relationer mer värda. Det finns visdom i kampen, men vi kan också växa och utvecklas utan att förstöra oss själva – utan att missa livets goda saker. Vi ser pensionen som tiden då vi äntligen får prioritera lätthet, men är våra andetag reserverade för livets sista kapitel? Jag föreslår inte att vi säger upp oss från allt. Det här är verkligheten – vi måste arbeta och 'göra'. Men vi är heller inte skapta för att bara göra. Vi är människor, inte maskiner – oavsett hur mycket tid vi spenderar med dem. Att leva kräver tålamod, liksom att skapa liv och låta kroppen återhämta sig. Om något på våra mobiler tar för lång tid att ladda tror vi att det är trasigt. Jag är rädd att detta har fått oss att tro att vår egen långsamhet är ett fel snarare än något som krävs för ett eftertänksamt liv. Tålamod är en gåva som öppnar för närvaro, reflektion och läkning. Belöningen är livets goda. När en webbsida ber oss att kryssa i 'Jag är inte en robot', låt oss göra det till vårt mantra. Sakta ner. Världens tempo behöver inte vara ditt. Hitta ditt eget tempo. Vi är inte byggda för wifi-fart.
post_content: Feeling overwhelmed by life, work, and endless emails? You don't have to move at Wi-Fi speed. Take it slow, give yourself some kindness, and remember: you're not a robot. #SlowDown #SelfCare

article_content: Russia's interior ministry has placed Sergei Aleksashenko, formerly a deputy governor of the Bank of Russia and deputy finance minister, on its wanted list, according to Russian state news agencies TASS and RIA. Aleksashenko, who has criticized Russia's war in Ukraine, is living in exile in the United States after falling out with President Vladimir Putin's government and had previously been declared a 'foreign agent.' TASS reported that Aleksashenko was added to the wanted list on an unspecified criminal charge. Reuters could not immediately access the interior ministry's database, and Aleksashenko could not be reached for comment. On his Telegram channel, Aleksashenko said he had been listed in the database for five years, but added that being included on the wanted list was a new development. Earlier this week, Russian lawmaker Vasiliy Piskarev accused Aleksashenko and Sergei Guriev, an economics professor at France's Sciences Po, of participating in shaping sanctions against Russia through their involvement with Stanford University's international working group on Russian sanctions. Piskarev, who heads the committee investigating foreign interference in Russia's internal affairs, accused both economists of state treason.

Aleksashenko, som har kritiserat Rysslands krig i Ukraina, lever i exil i USA efter en konflikt med president Vladimir Putins regering och hade redan tidigare förklarats som 'utländsk agent'. TASS rapporterade att Aleksashenko lagts till på efterlysningslistan för en ospecificerad brottsåtalspunkt. Reuters kunde inte omedelbart komma åt inrikesministeriets databas, och Aleksashenko gick inte att nå för en kommentar. På sin Telegram-kanal sade Aleksashenko att han redan funnits i databasen i fem år, men att det var nytt att han nu lagts till på efterlysningslistan. Tidigare i veckan anklagade den ryske lagstiftaren Vasiliy Piskarev Aleksashenko och Sergej Guriev, ekonomiprofessor vid Sciences Po i Frankrike, för att ha deltagit i utformningen av sanktioner mot Ryssland via sitt engagemang i Stanfords internationella arbetsgrupp för Rysslandssanktioner. Piskarev, som leder utskottet för utredning av utländsk inblandning i Rysslands inre angelägenheter, anklagade båda ekonomerna för landsförräderi.

article_content: Louis van Gaal has renewed his criticism of FIFA following the Netherlands’ defeat to Argentina, this time targeting the relevance of the World Cup third-place play-off. The 62-year-old Dutch coach stated, 'This match should never be played. I’ve been saying that for ten years—it’s unfair.' Despite his criticism, Van Gaal does not consider the semifinal loss to Argentina as a true defeat since the game was tied after 120 minutes, with Argentina advancing only after penalties. He now views the upcoming play-off in Brasilia as an opportunity for the Netherlands to end the tournament undefeated—something never achieved in their history. Speaking at a press conference with Dutch player Dirk Kuyt, Van Gaal commented, ‘There is still something for us to do here—we can still make history. The Netherlands have always lost at least one match in previous World Cups, even in 1974 and 1978 when they reached the final.’ He added, ‘I hope I can prepare the team well. It will be my last match and maybe the players want to give me a parting gift with a win, so we can leave the tournament unbeaten. It’s meaningful to go seven matches without defeat.’ Van Gaal acknowledged the emotional difficulty after being eliminated on penalties, saying, 'It’s very sad. A dream has been broken and it will not return. Our goal was to become champions, so losing like this is the worst way. I would have preferred to lose 7-1 as Brazil did against Germany.' References were made during the briefing to Brazil’s shocking 7-1 defeat to Germany, and Van Gaal reiterated past criticisms of what he saw as favorable scheduling for the host nation. Nevertheless, the Dutch team prepared for the final match at the Estadio Nacional, hoping to achieve a historic, undefeated World Cup run for Van Gaal’s send-off.
translated_content: Louis van Gaal har återigen riktat kritik mot FIFA efter Nederländernas förlust mot Argentina, denna gång om värdet av VM:s bronsmatch. Den 62-årige nederländske tränaren sade: 'Den här matchen borde aldrig spelas. Jag har sagt det i tio år – det är orättvist.' Trots sin kritik tycker Van Gaal inte att semifinalförlusten mot Argentina räknas som en riktig förlust eftersom matchen stod lika efter 120 minuter och Argentina gick vidare på straffar. Han ser nu bronsmatchen i Brasília som en chans för Nederländerna att avsluta turneringen obesegrade – något som landet aldrig tidigare har gjort. På en presskonferens tillsammans med spelaren Dirk Kuyt kommenterade Van Gaal: 'Vi har fortfarande något kvar att göra här – vi kan fortfarande skapa historia. Nederländerna har alltid förlorat minst en match i tidigare VM, också 1974 och 1978 när vi gick till final.' Han tillade: 'Jag hoppas kunna förbereda laget väl. Det blir min sista match och kanske vill spelarna ge mig en avskedsgåva genom en seger så att vi kan lämna turneringen obesegrade. Det skulle verkligen vara något att gå sju matcher utan förlust.' Van Gaal erkände hur tufft det var känslomässigt efter strafförlusten och sade: 'Det är väldigt sorgligt. En dröm har krossats och kommer inte tillbaka. Vårt mål var att gå hela vägen, så att förlora så här är det värsta sättet. Jag hade hellre förlorat med 7-1 som Brasilien gjorde mot Tyskland.' På presskonferensen togs också upp Brasiliens chockförlust med 7-1 mot Tyskland, och Van Gaal upprepade sin tidigare kritik mot vad han kallat fördelaktiga spelscheman för värdnationen. Trots detta förberedde det nederländska laget sig för den sista matchen på Estadio Nacional, med hopp om att ge Van Gaal en historisk, obesegrad VM-avslutning.

article_content: The United States has pledged to supply Syrian rebels with food and medical assistance, not weapons—the first step of this kind in the two years since the conflict's start. Meanwhile, European countries are deliberating ways to increase support for Syrian rebel groups without providing direct military aid, after a European Council ruling allowed civilian-protection support. Secretary of State John Kerry announced the US aid package is intended to help rebels seeking to remove President Bashar al-Assad. The Syrian war has resulted in over 60,000 deaths, devastated regions, and triggered a severe humanitarian crisis as countless Syrians flee the violence. There are rising fears of broader regional instability and that groups like Hezbollah or Iran might increase their influence should Assad fall. After consultations with the Syrian opposition in Rome, Kerry stated the US response is fueled by the continued violence of Assad’s military forces, supported by foreign fighters including those from Iran and Hezbollah. On top of previously committed support ($385 million in humanitarian aid and $50 million in earlier aid), Kerry announced an additional $60 million for groups aligned with the opposition Syrian National Council. The goal is to improve governance and service delivery in rebel-held territories, ensuring communities have access to essentials such as food, medical care, and sanitation. US officials acknowledge that reinforcing moderate groups with such assistance could limit the spread of radical Islamist actors in areas no longer held by the government. A senior State Department official told CNN that failing to help civilians in 'liberated' areas could allow extremist groups to fill the gap in services. Syrian National Council head Sheikh Ahmed Moaz al-Khatib argued that Western concerns about the influence of Islamists are overstated and affirmed the council’s opposition to extremist ideologies threatening Syria's diverse society. US officials hope that delivering tangible assistance will showcase the opposition’s capability and encourage more regime supporters to defect. Although the opposition council will allocate the aid, the US will place technical advisors with their Cairo headquarters to help monitor the funds and their usage appropriately. The European Council has modified sanctions, allowing the transfer of nonlethal aid and technical help focused on civilian safety, but has not detailed which materials are permitted. UK Foreign Secretary William Hague reiterated via social media that Britain will increase support due to the worsening situation, while French authorities are considering sending equipment like night-vision devices or body armor. In the US, President Obama is reportedly evaluating options for providing training and protective gear to Syrian rebels. This could include equipment like body armor and vehicles and assist the opposition in both strategy and establishing security post-Assad. Kerry stopped short of confirming these new forms of support but noted ongoing consultations with allies. Officials specified that support would be distributed cautiously to thoroughly vetted individuals and groups. Violence and civilian casualties continue daily; opposition activist networks reported nearly 100 deaths in a single day across Syria, especially around Damascus. The conflict, which erupted from demands for political reform ignited by the Arab Spring, deteriorated into civil war following a government crackdown. According to UN data since March 2011, about 60,000 people have died, nearly a million have fled Syria, and over 10% of the population has been internally displaced. Relief agencies and the United Nations have warned that the refugee wave is overwhelming capacity in neighboring countries. Erika Feller, assistant high commissioner at the UNHCR, highlighted these concerns in a recent address. Reporting was provided by Jill Dougherty (Rome), Michael Pearson (Atlanta), with additional contributions from Nick Paton Walsh and Elise Labott (CNN).
translated_content: USA har lovat att skicka mat och medicinsk hjälp till syriska rebeller, men inga vapen—det första steget av detta slag på två år sedan konflikten började. Samtidigt diskuterar europeiska länder hur man kan öka stödet till de syriska rebellstyrkorna utan att ge militärt bistånd, efter att Europeiska rådet beslutat att stödja civilt skydd. USA:s utrikesminister John Kerry meddelade att stödpaketet syftar till att hjälpa rebeller som vill avsätta president Bashar al-Assad. Kriget i Syrien har lett till över 60 000 dödsfall, förstört hela regioner och orsakat en allvarlig humanitär kris när otaliga syrier flyr våldet. Oro växer för ökad regional instabilitet och att grupper som Hizbollah eller Iran kan stärka sitt inflytande om Assad faller. Efter samtal med den syriska oppositionen i Rom förklarade Kerry att USA:s svar beror på det fortsatta våldet från Assads militära styrkor, som får stöd av utländska kämpar från bland annat Iran och Hizbollah. Utöver tidigare stöd (385 miljoner dollar i humanitärt bistånd och 50 miljoner i tidigare hjälp) tillkännagav Kerry ytterligare 60 miljoner dollar till grupper anslutna till oppositionsrådet Syrian National Council. Syftet är att förbättra styrning och tjänster i områden som kontrolleras av rebeller, så att samhällen får tillgång till mat, medicinsk vård och sanitet. Amerikanska tjänstemän medger att detta stöd kan stärka moderata grupper och begränsa radikala islamisters inflytande i områden där regimen inte längre styr. En hög amerikansk UD-tjänsteman sa till CNN att om man inte hjälper civila i 'befriade' områden kan extremistgrupper fylla den tomrummet. Sheikh Ahmed Moaz al-Khatib, ledare för Syrian National Council, menar att västvärldens oro över islamisters inflytande är överdriven och bekräftade att rådet motsätter sig extremism som hotar Syriens mångfald. USA hoppas att konkret hjälp visar oppositionens kapacitet och får fler av regimens supportrar att byta sida. Oppositionsrådet bestämmer hur biståndet ska användas, men USA skickar tekniska rådgivare till deras Cairo-kontor för att följa upp hur medlen används. Europeiska rådet har anpassat sina sanktioner för att möjliggöra icke-dödande utrustning och teknisk hjälp, men har inte specificerat vilken utrustning som är tillåten. Storbritanniens utrikesminister William Hague har upprepat via sociala medier att landet ökar sitt stöd på grund av förvärrad kris, medan Frankrike överväger att skicka utrustning som mörkerkikare eller kroppsskydd. I USA överväger president Obama nu att erbjuda träning och skyddsutrustning till de syriska rebellerna. Det kan handla om kroppsskydd, fordon samt hjälp att planera och bygga upp en ny säkerhetsstyrka efter Assad. Kerry bekräftade inte dessa nya stödformer men betonade att samtalen med allierade fortsätter. Myndigheterna påpekade att stödet bara delas ut till noggrant granskade individer och grupper. Våldet och civila dödsfall fortsätter dagligen; oppositionsaktivister rapporterade nästan 100 döda på en enda dag, särskilt runt Damaskus. Konflikten började med krav på politiska reformer inspirerade av den arabiska våren, men förvandlades till inbördeskrig efter regimens hårda tillslag. Enligt FN har runt 60 000 människor dött sedan mars 2011, närmare en miljon har flytt landet och över 10 % av befolkningen har blivit internflyktingar. Hjälporganisationer och FN varnar för att flyktingströmmen överbelastar grannländerna. Erika Feller, biträdande högkommissionär vid UNHCR, tog upp detta i ett tal nyligen. article_content: Reports indicate that Ri Sol-Ju, spouse of North Korean leader Kim Jong Un, gave birth in late 2012, though this information remains unconfirmed by North Korea's government. While the baby's gender is unclear, analysts, such as Michael Madden of North Korea Leadership Watch, suggest it's probably a girl, as an official announcement would have been likely if the child had been a boy. Speculation has intensified due to Ri Sol-Ju's recent public appearances and changes in her style, moving from loose to more fitted clothing, which observers interpret as evidence of childbirth. South Korean officials and media, referencing intelligence and televised images, also believe that she recently became a mother. North Korea continues its tradition of secrecy; the leader’s marriage to Ri Sol-Ju wasn’t disclosed until after a period of speculation. Analysts observe that the Kim dynasty, which began as a Soviet-influenced communist regime, has evolved into a hereditary leadership. During this period, Kim Jong Un has drawn attention for both increased military actions and his interactions with Western guests like former NBA player Dennis Rodman, who publicly praised him. Ri Sol-Ju is seen by some as an emerging presence in North Korea’s leadership circle, though her political significance, if any, is uncertain according to outside experts. Details about Ri Sol-Ju’s family suggest her parents occupy respected roles in North Korea—her father is reportedly an academic, and her mother a doctor. Her disappearance from public events spurred theories ranging from pregnancy to image management, where she may have been kept out of sight for not conforming to the expected solemn image. Ultimately, strict control over the public image of North Korea’s leader and family remains a priority for the regime, reinforcing authority and continuity in leadership.

article_content: Delhi's Environment Minister, Gopal Rai, has announced that restrictions under Stage 3 of the Graded Response Action Plan (GRAP) will remain in place until the city's air quality improves. This decision comes as Delhi continues to experience 'very poor' air quality, with the Air Quality Index (AQI) reaching 324 on Thursday morning, according to data from SAFAR-India. Rai stressed the need for public cooperation and reminded residents that Stages 1, 2, and 3 of GRAP are still active to combat air pollution. Speaking on the issue, he noted that, except for projects of national importance, construction activities in the city are currently prohibited. 'Wind speeds are low, but scientists believe that conditions could improve. The government has decided that GRAP-3 restrictions will stay until there is notable improvement in air quality,' Rai said. After an earlier improvement in air quality this month, Stage 4 restrictions were lifted, allowing permitted trucks and buses (excluding BS-3 and BS-4 petrol and diesel vehicles) to enter the city, and resuming most construction activities. According to the Central Pollution Control Board, AQI readings on Thursday morning were as follows: Anand Vihar – 387 (very poor), ITO – 343 (very poor), Wazirpur – 422 (severe), RK Puram – 415 (severe), and Okhla Phase-2 – 406 (severe). The AQI categorizes air quality as good (0-100), moderate (100-200), poor (200-300), very poor (300-400), and severe (400-500 or above). Rai urged all citizens to adhere to the guidelines and remain cautious as authorities work to improve Delhi's air quality.

Regeringen har beslutat att GRAP-3-restriktionerna ska stanna kvar tills en tydlig förbättring av luftkvaliteten sker', sade Rai. Efter tidigare förbättringar av luftkvaliteten denna månad lyftes Steg 4-restriktionerna, vilket tillät vissa lastbilar och bussar (utom BS-3 och BS-4 bensin- och dieselfordon) att köra in i staden och återupptog de flesta byggaktiviteter. Enligt Central Pollution Control Board var AQI-mätningarna på torsdagsmorgonen: Anand Vihar – 387 (mycket dålig), ITO – 343 (mycket dålig), Wazirpur – 422 (allvarlig), RK Puram – 415 (allvarlig) och Okhla Fas-2 – 406 (allvarlig). article_content: Netflix's hit series 'Wednesday' will shift production from Romania to Ireland for its upcoming second season, as Deadline reported exclusively on Monday. At the Season 5 premiere of FX’s 'Fargo,' executive producer Steve Stark explained the reasoning behind the move. 'Romania offered a great creative environment, but we faced several challenges during filming,' Stark told Deadline. The Balkan country's logistical issues led producers to consider relocating, with rumors beginning soon after Season 1 wrapped. 'By the end of filming, we knew we would be moving,' Stark said, adding that London and Ireland were both on the table. Having filmed 113 episodes of 'Vikings' in Ireland, Stark described his fondness for the country and noted the attractive offer from the same studio used for 'Vikings.' Stark, who now executive produces 'Wednesday,' 'Fargo,' and 'Vikings: Valhalla' following nearly a decade as President of MGM Television, outlined the history of Ashford Studios in Ireland, which served as the filming home for the original 'Vikings' series and will now host 'Wednesday.' Production on Season 2 is slated to begin in late April. Details on Season 2's storyline remain scarce, but showrunners Al Gough and Miles Millar have hinted that more members of the Addams family will appear, and Wednesday's relationship with her mother will be explored further. Jenna Ortega, the series' star, will become a producer and has indicated the new season will place greater emphasis on horror elements rather than teen romance. Stark teased, 'There will be a lot of surprises in Season 2.' While attending the 'Fargo' premiere, Stark discussed the upcoming fifth season, which is set in the present day, saying, 'The show's appeal lies in how it weaves comedy and tragedy—Minnesota nice contrasted with dark situations. It acts as a morality play about power, greed, and their consequences.' Season 5 will follow a woman caught between her mother-in-law and a sheriff, testing her cleverness and resilience. Stark also hinted at the possibility of additional future 'Fargo' seasons, potentially set in the 1960s or 1990s.

article_content: Marc Emery, once known as Canada's 'prince of pot,' is now a federal inmate in the United States after being sentenced on Friday to five years in prison. The marijuana activist pleaded guilty in May at the U.S. District Court in Seattle to a charge of conspiracy to manufacture marijuana, following an 18-month investigation into his marijuana seed-selling business based in Vancouver, British Columbia. The five-year sentence, which also includes four years of supervised probation, fulfills a plea agreement Emery, 52, reached with U.S. authorities to avoid a longer term. During sentencing, U.S. District Judge Ricardo S. Martinez emphasized the illegality of Emery's actions and their consequences. Dozens of Emery’s supporters gathered outside the federal courthouse in Seattle to protest what they believe is a politically motivated end to a five-year legal battle. U.S. officials previously described Emery as one of their most wanted international drug trafficking targets from Canada. Emery founded the British Columbia Marijuana Party and the website CannabisCulture.com. In Canada, he is recognized for his consistent advocacy for marijuana legalization, having taken part in demonstrations, sit-ins, and political campaigns. He said he has been arrested at least a dozen times since 1995 for his activism, and his Vancouver store has been raided multiple times since it opened in 1994. Emery admitted in his plea agreement to operating a marijuana seed-selling business with two co-defendants, who pleaded to lesser charges and were placed on probation in Canada. He also acknowledged selling seeds to U.S. customers by mail, phone, and at his retail store. U.S. Attorney Jenny A. Durkan stated that Emery disregarded U.S. law and profited by sending marijuana seeds into the U.S., regardless of the buyers' age or activities. Durkan said Emery is now facing the consequences of his involvement in the illegal drug trade. Emery and his supporters maintain the prosecution was politically motivated, highlighting a 2005 DEA press release that called his arrest a 'significant blow' to the marijuana legalization movement. The statement said Emery had funded legalization groups in the U.S. and Canada. Emery's lawyer, Richard Troberman, argued that Emery was singled out mainly because he donated proceeds to advocacy, rather than for unique criminal actions. The U.S. Attorney's Office, however, insisted Emery's politics were not part of the prosecution, focusing solely on his criminal activity. With Emery imprisoned, his wife Jodie has taken a leading role in the movement, organizing rallies in over 70 cities worldwide to support Emery and marijuana legalization. Emery, meanwhile, remains committed to his beliefs, but in a letter to the court admitted that his actions were reckless and expressed regret for not choosing legal methods for reform.

article_content: At 39, Eva Mendes launches her first clothing collection and appears on the cover of The Edit, Net-a-Porter’s digital magazine. In an open interview, Mendes discusses the debut of her eponymous label, her personal fashion principles, and her admiration for Penelope Cruz and director Pedro Almodóvar. Mendes is photographed by David Bellemere, modeling the latest from Dolce & Gabbana, Anna Sui, Gucci, and Alexander McQueen in a striking feature. Highlighted by soft lighting and bold makeup, she is seen in elegant styles with accessories by Dolce & Gabbana and Pamela Love. Exclusively partnering with New York & Company, Mendes’s new line captures her signature retro-chic style. Before joining forces with the retailer, she consulted her mother and sisters, who were highly supportive of the venture. The collection’s prices are accessible, starting at $24.95 for a camisole and reaching $159.95 for the pale pink Milano one-button coat. The range also offers accessories like jewelry, belts, and Mendes’s must-have printed scarf, generally costing about $20. Throughout the shoot, Mendes wears designs from Moschino, Valentino, Biyan, and Simone Rocha. She emphasizes the value of personal details, cherishing pieces such as earrings from her late grandmother. When it comes to eveningwear, Mendes adheres to two rules: short outfits should avoid excess exposure, while fully covered looks can be more form-fitting. Looking back at her youth, Mendes recalls considering paths as a nun or astronaut prior to acting. She reflects on early career challenges but appreciates the opportunities and connections she’s found. Speaking about her role in 'The Place Beyond the Pines,' Mendes says it was her first experience portraying a truly nuanced character—a film that also led her to meet Ryan Gosling. They recently worked together on Gosling’s directorial debut, 'How to Catch a Monster,' a project Mendes describes as incredible. While Mendes keeps her relationship with Gosling private, she occasionally shares moments from their life, including their two dogs, Hugo and George. The complete interview is available at net-a-porter.com.

Wigan Athletic chairman Dave Whelan has accepted a charge of misconduct from the Football Association after making remarks about Jewish and Chinese people. These statements, made while defending his decision to hire Malky Mackay as the club's new manager, have been criticized for being racist and anti-Semitic. At that time, Mackay was under investigation for alleged discriminatory text messages sent during his previous role at Cardiff City. Whelan was quoted as minimizing derogatory language aimed at Chinese individuals and promoting stereotypes about Jewish people.

Whelan has requested a non-personal FA hearing and has said he will resign as chairman if found guilty of racism. The FA alleges that Whelan’s comments were abusive and discriminatory, amounting to an aggravated breach relating to race and religion. The FA also continues to investigate Mackay and former Cardiff recruitment head Iain Moody regarding inappropriate messages exchanged between them. Cardiff owner Vincent Tan criticized Whelan’s move to appoint Mackay, describing it as a case of a 'racist chairman hiring a racist manager.' Both Whelan and Mackay deny being racist.

article_content: Hydrogen stands as one of the universe's most common elements, but pure hydrogen is scarce on Earth. As the fight against climate change intensifies, interest in green hydrogen—produced with renewable energy—has surged due to its promise as a clean way to store and supply energy. Despite hydrogen's massive cosmic presence, its practical application as a large-scale clean fuel is a relatively recent development. The serious exploration of hydrogen's energy potential began after its use in fuel cells for NASA's Apollo missions. Since then, hydrogen has increasingly been recognized as a potential replacement for fossil fuels, especially when produced through renewable sources. According to McKinsey, hydrogen could account for over 20% of global emissions reductions by 2050. Momentum is growing worldwide: by May 2023, more than 1,000 major hydrogen projects were announced, totaling $320 billion in investment. In India, hydrogen demand sits at about 6 million tonnes per year and is on track to double by 2030. In response, the Indian government launched the National Green Hydrogen Mission, targeting 5 million metric tonnes of green hydrogen by 2030, supported by over ₹8 lakh crore in investment and aiming to create more than 600,000 jobs. India currently imports 40% of its energy, spending about $90 billion each year. Building a domestic green hydrogen industry could turn India into an energy exporter and cut fuel import bills. However, numerous technical and economic challenges remain, particularly in the manufacturing and deployment of green hydrogen. Central to this effort is the electrolyser, a device that splits water into hydrogen and oxygen. Advancing domestic production of high-quality electrolysers would give India an edge globally. Worldwide, electrolyser sales more than doubled between 2020 and 2021, and this growth is expected to continue. India has a timely chance to capture part of this expanding market. Strong partnerships between government and industry—such as public-private collaborations and pilot projects—are necessary to accelerate progress. The European Commission’s Clean Hydrogen alliance provides a model for multi-stakeholder cooperation. India is encouraged to pursue similar alliances through its business and government institutions. Substantial challenges persist, however. Large volumes of freshwater and renewable electricity are required for hydrogen production. Producing 1 kilogram of hydrogen calls for about 10 litres of water and 50 kWh of power, resulting in a cost of $4.10 to $7 per kilogram. Achieving the government’s green hydrogen target would require about 50 billion litres of freshwater, a significant challenge in a country already facing water shortages. There is a need to innovate by using alternatives to freshwater, such as treated wastewater, for hydrogen production. Additionally, expanding renewable power generation and modernizing the electricity grid are critical to ensuring stable, continuous electricity for hydrogen facilities. Transporting hydrogen presents further obstacles: its highly flammable nature means it must be moved in special cryogenic containers, raising costs. Alternative solutions—like producing hydrogen onsite from transported feedstocks—are being considered, though these require technological maturity and investment. Overcoming regulatory and logistical issues, harmonizing national and state energy policies, and creating special industrial zones for green hydrogen production could help speed progress. A robust green hydrogen sector could generate large numbers of jobs, lower greenhouse emissions, and make India more energy self-reliant. The Indian government has already taken steps towards this vision, and if innovation and investment continue, green hydrogen could become a cornerstone in solving energy and climate challenges. Nations that become net exporters of green hydrogen may shape the future of the global energy market.
translated_content: Väte är ett av universums vanligaste grundämnen, men rent väte är sällsynt på jorden. I takt med att kampen mot klimatförändringar intensifieras har intresset för grönt väte – som produceras med förnybar energi – ökat tack vare dess potential som ett rent sätt att lagra och leverera energi. Trots vätets enorma kosmiska förekomst är dess praktiska användning som storskaligt rent bränsle en relativt ny utveckling. En mer seriös utforskning av vätets energipotential tog fart efter dess användning i bränsleceller under NASAs Apollo-uppdrag. Sedan dess har väte i allt större utsträckning betraktats som en möjlig ersättare för fossila bränslen, särskilt när det produceras via förnybara energikällor. Enligt McKinsey kan väte bidra till över 20 % av de globala utsläppsminskningarna till 2050. Det händer mycket internationellt: i maj 2023 hade över 1 000 stora väteprojekt annonserats, med investeringar på totalt 320 miljarder dollar. I Indien ligger efterfrågan på väte på cirka 6 miljoner ton per år och väntas fördubblas till 2030. För att möta den ökande efterfrågan har den indiska regeringen lanserat National Green Hydrogen Mission, med målet att producera 5 miljoner ton grönt väte till 2030, stödd av över 8 lakh crore rupier i investeringar och med en ambition att skapa mer än 600 000 arbetstillfällen. Indien importerar för närvarande 40 % av sin energi och spenderar cirka 90 miljarder dollar årligen. Att bygga upp en inhemsk industri för grönt väte kan förvandla Indien till en energiexportör och minska landets utgifter för bränsleimport. Men det kvarstår många tekniska och ekonomiska utmaningar, särskilt inom tillverkning och implementering av grönt väte. I centrum för detta står elektrolysören – en enhet som spjälkar vatten till väte och syre. Att utveckla inhemsk produktion av högkvalitativa elektrolysörer skulle ge Indien ett försprång globalt. På världsmarknaden fördubblades försäljningen av elektrolysörer mellan 2020 och 2021, och denna tillväxt väntas fortsätta. Indien har ett gyllene tillfälle att ta del av denna växande marknad. Starka samarbeten mellan stat och industri – till exempel offentligt-privata partnerskap och pilotprojekt – är nödvändiga för att driva utvecklingen framåt. EU-kommissionens Clean Hydrogen Alliance är ett exempel på ett brett samarbete. Indien uppmanas att efterlikna sådana modeller via sina näringslivs- och myndighetsorganisationer. Det kvarstår dock betydande utmaningar. Stora mängder färskvatten och förnybar el krävs för väteproduktionen. För att tillverka 1 kg väte behövs ungefär 10 liter vatten och 50 kWh el, vilket ger en produktionskostnad mellan $4,10 och $7 per kilo. Om man ska nå regeringens mål krävs cirka 50 miljarder liter färskvatten – ett problem i ett land som redan har vattenbrist. Det behövs innovation för att använda alternativ till färskvatten, såsom renat avloppsvatten, i produktionen. Dessutom är det avgörande att bygga ut den förnybara elproduktionen och modernisera elnätet för att säkerställa en stabil energi för hydrogenanläggningar. Att transportera väte är också en utmaning – gasen är mycket brandfarlig och måste fraktas i speciella kryogena behållare, vilket ökar kostnaderna. Alternativ, till exempel produktion av väte på plats från transporterade råvaror, övervägs, men dessa tekniker är ännu inte mogna och kräver investeringar. För att påskynda utvecklingen krävs också bättre samordning av energipolitiken nationellt och inom delstaterna, samt framväxten av särskilda industrizoner för grönt väte. En stark sektor för grönt väte kan skapa många jobb, minska växthusgasutsläppen och göra Indien mer självförsörjande på energi. Regeringen har redan tagit initiativ, och om investeringar och innovation fortsätter kan grönt väte bli en viktig lösning på våra energi- och klimatutmaningar. Länder som kan exportera grönt väte riskerar att få en ledande roll på framtidens globala energimarknad.

article_content: A month after devastating floods swept through eastern Libya, especially Derna, evidence has emerged pointing to critical failures by local authorities that worsened the catastrophe. BBC Arabic’s investigation highlights three key areas where better management could have saved lives. Firstly, many Derna residents were advised by officials to remain at home as Storm Daniel approached. Clear evacuation orders were not consistently issued; only certain neighborhoods near the sea or river were told to leave, while most were simply told to stay indoors. Some evacuees were relocated to areas that later became even more hazardous, resulting in further casualties. Secondly, authorities neglected clear warnings about the precarious condition of Derna’s two river dams. On September 11, both dams failed after heavy rainfall, flooding the city. Previous research by Dr. Abdulwanis Ashour and others had highlighted these structural issues, warning they could not withstand severe storms. Despite this, no significant maintenance was undertaken. Thirdly, after the disaster, strict controls by eastern authorities under General Khalifa Haftar delayed the delivery of emergency aid. Only select organizations like the Red Crescent were initially allowed access, and even they were overwhelmed. Aid convoys from the west and other areas faced blockades, with officials insisting on inspecting all supplies and managing distribution themselves. Essential food, water, and medical aid frequently arrived days late. The true death toll remains uncertain—at least 4,000 people have been confirmed dead, with around 10,000 still missing and many swept away to sea. The mishandling led to public outrage, culminating in protests on September 18 and the burning of the mayor’s house. The mayor resigned soon after. In the following days, journalists and aid workers experienced communications blackouts, obstructing both rescue efforts and protest organization—believed by many to be intentional. These failings occurred in a country already deeply divided between rival governments in the east and west since the 2011 fall of Muammar Gaddafi. General Haftar’s eastern forces have controlled Derna for years. Following the tragedy, prosecutors from the west issued arrest warrants for 16 dam officials on charges of negligence, though it’s unclear if these arrests occurred. Aid workers and residents are united in their anger, accusing leaders of putting security measures and political rivalries ahead of urgent humanitarian needs. The BBC’s findings highlight the dire consequences of ignored infrastructure warnings, incomplete evacuation plans, and politicized disaster response in Libya.

BBC Arabic visar i sin granskning tre centrala områden där bättre ledarskap kunde ha räddat liv. För det första uppmanades många invånare i Derna av myndigheterna att stanna hemma när stormen Daniel närmade sig. Tydliga evakueringsorder utfärdades inte konsekvent; endast vissa områden nära havet eller floden blev ombedda att lämna sina hem, medan de flesta ombads hålla sig inomhus. Vissa som evakuerades hamnade i områden som senare blev ännu farligare och drabbades av fler dödsfall. För det andra ignorerade myndigheterna upprepade varningar om det farliga skicket på Darnas två flod-dammar. Den 11 september kollapsade båda dammarna efter kraftigt regn och staden översvämmades. Forskning av Dr Abdulwanis Ashour och andra hade tidigare påtalat allvarliga brister och varnat för att dammarna inte skulle klara extrema väder. Trots detta gjordes inga större underhållsåtgärder. För det tredje försenades nödinsatser av strikta kontroller från östra myndigheter under ledning av general Khalifa Haftar. Endast vissa organisationer, till exempel Röda halvmånen, fick tidig tillgång men blev snabbt överväldigade. Hjälpkonvojer från västra Libyen och andra områden stoppades och alla förnödenheter inspekterades innan distribution – vilket ledde till att mat, vatten och medicin ofta anlände flera dagar för sent. Det verkliga dödstalet är okänt – minst 4 000 människor har bekräftats döda, omkring 10 000 saknas och många tros ha svepts ut till havs. Myndigheternas misskötsel ledde till stor upprördhet, massprotester den 18 september och att borgmästarens hus brändes ner; borgmästaren avgick därefter. Under de följande dagarna stördes kommunikationerna i staden, vilket försvårade räddningsarbete och protester – något många anser var avsiktligt. Dessa misslyckanden skedde i ett land redan djupt splittrat mellan rivaliserande regeringar i öst och väst sedan Gaddafis fall 2011. General Haftars styrkor har kontrollerat Derna i flera år. Efter katastrofen utfärdade västliga åklagare arresteringsorder mot 16 dammansvariga för försumlighet, men det är oklart om någon faktiskt gripits. Hjälparbetare och lokalbefolkning uttrycker ilska över att säkerhetsåtgärder och politiska motsättningar gått före humanitära behov. BBC:s granskning belyser de allvarliga konsekvenserna av ignorerade varningar om infrastrukturen, ofullständiga evakueringsplaner och en politiserad krishantering i Libyen.

article_content: Minister of Sports Development, Senator John Enoh, has urged football fans across Nigeria to support the Super Eagles as they aim to reclaim the Africa Cup of Nations (AFCON) title at the 2023 tournament in Ivory Coast. Enoh made this appeal during the launch of the #Letsdoitagain campaign, organized by the Nigeria Football Federation (NFF) to mark Nigeria’s quest for a fourth continental title. The tournament will take place from January 13 to February 11, 2024. Nigeria qualified for their 21st AFCON appearance by topping Group A in the qualifiers with 15 points, ahead of Guinea-Bissau, Sierra Leone, and Sao Tome and Principe. The Super Eagles won five games, lost one (at home to Guinea-Bissau), and scored 22 goals—the highest in their group. It has been ten years since Nigeria last won the AFCON, and the #Letsdoitagain campaign aims to motivate the three-time champions for another triumph. "I want to thank the NFF for organizing this. It is greatly needed. Let’s do it again—we can and we will. It is very important," Enoh said at the event. The campaign seeks to unite all 200 million Nigerians behind the Super Eagles as they compete in Ivory Coast. Nigeria has a rich football history, and there are opportunities to share inspiring stories about the players. Enoh also stressed the importance of carrying this enthusiasm into other sports, especially during challenging economic times, with the hope of inspiring the nation. "We can make this campaign impactful and ensure it reaches every Nigerian. The hope is that it will not only fuel our AFCON ambition but also encourage growth in other sports," he added. Nigeria’s first AFCON title was in 1980 on home soil, followed by victories in Tunisia in 1994 and South Africa in 2013. Senator Enoh concluded by expressing confidence that renewed success in football could help revitalize Nigerian sports and reignite national pride during economic difficulties.

Enoh vädjade om detta under lanseringen av #Letsdoitagain-kampanjen, organiserad av Nigerias fotbollsförbund (NFF) för att markera Nigerias strävan efter en fjärde kontinentaltitel. Turneringen hålls från 13 januari till 11 februari 2024. Nigeria kvalificerade sig till sitt 21:a deltagande i AFCON genom att toppa grupp A i kvalet med 15 poäng, före Guinea-Bissau, Sierra Leone och Sao Tomé och Príncipe. Super Eagles vann fem matcher, förlorade en (på hemmaplan mot Guinea-Bissau) och gjorde 22 mål – flest i sin grupp. Det har gått tio år sedan Nigeria senast vann AFCON, och #Letsdoitagain-kampanjen syftar till att motivera de trefaldiga mästarna till nya framgångar. "Jag vill tacka NFF för att de ordnat detta. Det behövs verkligen. Låt oss göra det igen – vi kan och vi kommer. Det är mycket viktigt," sade Enoh vid evenemanget. Nigeria har en rik fotbollshistoria och det finns möjligheter att lyfta fram inspirerande berättelser om spelarna. "Vi kan göra kampanjen betydelsefull och se till att den når varje nigerian. Förhoppningen är att den inte bara ska stötta vår AFCON-satsning, utan också stimulera utveckling inom andra sporter," tillade han. article_content: Authorities in Selah, Washington, are investigating after a hidden camera was found under a female student's desk in a ninth-grade science class at Selah Junior High School. The device’s discovery led police to seize both the camera and computers from the home of 51-year-old science teacher Dave McMillen. Investigators suspect the camera was used for inappropriate recordings, prompting a probe into possible acts of voyeurism. Shortly after the inquiry began, McMillen resigned from his position. Although no official reason was provided for his resignation, it followed his placement on administrative leave earlier this month when students reported the camera. The device, about two inches wide, was found accidentally when a student knocked it loose. According to Police Chief Stacy Dwarshuis, authorities are currently reviewing the device’s contents and have confiscated computers from McMillen’s home. Dwarshuis commented that McMillen’s resignation was appropriate under the circumstances, though his ability to work elsewhere would depend on any further state certification action. The school notified parents that the board had reached a settlement with McMillen, officially ending his employment. In the meantime, a temporary substitute has been teaching the class, with a certified science teacher scheduled to take over for the rest of the school year. As of now, McMillen has not been charged with any crime.

article_content: Afghan President Hamid Karzai intervened on behalf of Gulnaz, a rape survivor, leading to her release from prison. Gulnaz had been sentenced to 12 years after reporting that she was raped by her cousin's husband. Following Karzai's action, she was freed, and her case received international attention as she had considered marrying her attacker to gain her release and legitimize her daughter, conceived during the assault. Karzai explained to CNN's Fareed Zakaria that he viewed the situation as a misjudgment that was resolved by granting her a pardon. Now staying in a women’s shelter in Kabul with her daughter, Gulnaz initially kept the assault secret out of fear. Eventually, the courts found her guilty of adultery—sex outside of marriage—and imprisoned her, as Afghan law does not clearly distinguish between rape and adultery, both considered crimes under Sharia law. In the interview, Karzai emphasized that it is Gulnaz's decision whether to marry her attacker, stating, 'It's up to her to decide who to marry or not to marry. Islam gives her that right.' He also expressed confidence in Afghanistan's judicial system after international forces withdraw, reassuring that there would be no internal strife or miscarriages of justice. Although she has been pardoned, Gulnaz faces an uncertain future in a conservative society where her ordeal is seen as bringing shame to her family. Karzai also addressed Afghanistan’s relationship with the United States and efforts regarding the Taliban in the interview, set to air Sunday on Fareed Zakaria GPS.

Efter Karzais ingripande frigavs hon, och hennes fall fick internationell uppmärksamhet när det framkom att hon övervägde att gifta sig med sin förövare för att få sin frihet och legitimera sin dotter, som blev till under övergreppet. Karzai förklarade för CNN:s Fareed Zakaria att han såg situationen som ett felbeslut som löstes genom att benåda henne. I intervjun betonade Karzai att det är Gulnaz eget val om hon vill gifta sig med sin förövare och sa, 'Det är upp till henne att bestämma vem hon ska gifta sig med eller inte. Islam ger henne den rätten.' Han uttryckte också förtroende för Afghanistans rättssystem efter att de internationella styrkorna lämnar och försäkrade att det inte skulle uppstå interna konflikter eller rättsövergrepp. Trots benådningen står Gulnaz inför en osäker framtid i ett konservativt samhälle där hennes upplevelser betraktas som skam för familjen. Karzai tog också upp Afghanistans relation till USA och ansträngningarna kring talibanerna i intervjun, som sänds på söndag i Fareed Zakaria GPS.
