article_content: New Delhi, India (CNN) – The Indian government issued an ultimatum Thursday to the maker of BlackBerry smartphones: Provide access to highly encrypted communications by August 31, or face the blockade of two popular messaging services. Indian authorities have been scrutinizing real-time BlackBerry messaging because strong encryption prevents intelligence agencies from monitoring communications, which, according to officials, could pose a national security risk. The government wants law enforcement agencies to gain access to the BlackBerry Enterprise Service and BlackBerry Messenger Service. "If a technical solution is not provided by 31st August, 2010, the government will review the situation and take steps to block these two services from the network," the official announcement stated. This standoff impacts millions in India’s booming wireless market, where more than 600 million people use mobile phones and about one million are BlackBerry users, according to the Telecom Regulatory Authority of India. Calls to Research in Motion (RIM), the Canadian manufacturer of BlackBerry devices, were not immediately returned. Indian officials have expressed serious security concerns around encrypted communications. Some are surprised about the stringent stance from the world’s largest democracy, but India’s position reflects profound security anxieties. The country has faced multiple attacks, including the November 2008 Mumbai attacks by suspected Pakistani militants, which killed over 160. During that incident, authorities accessed satellite phone calls between the attackers and their handlers, but only after violence had begun. Vikram Sood, a retired Indian intelligence official, warned that if terrorists used BlackBerry devices for planning and the government could not access their communications, the country would be left blind. "So what do you do? React after the fact? If you do, a terrorist act has already occurred and lives are lost. Who is responsible for that? Is BlackBerry liable if it withholds information?" Sood asked. He stressed the importance of sharing information for national security. This situation spotlights an ongoing debate about the government’s right to access information versus individuals’ rights to privacy and the free flow of information. The outcome will have significant implications in rapidly growing telecom markets like India. RIM stands to lose a sizable market share if some BlackBerry services are blocked. While telecom operators in India are preparing contingency plans, they do not widely expect BlackBerry services to be suspended, noting that RIM made concessions with Saudi Arabia to avoid a ban. The United Arab Emirates has issued similar threats to RIM about service shutdowns if access is not granted. “We think it will all be worked out,” said Sanjay Warke, Vodafone India’s chief executive officer. CNN’s Sara Sidner contributed to this report.

Indiska myndigheter har granskat BlackBerrys realtidsmeddelanden eftersom den starka krypteringen hindrar säkerhetstjänster från att övervaka kommunikationen, vilket enligt myndigheterna kan utgöra en nationell säkerhetsrisk. "Om en teknisk lösning inte presenteras före den 31 augusti 2010 kommer regeringen att utvärdera situationen och vidta åtgärder för att blockera dessa två tjänster från nätverket," stod det i det officiella uttalandet. Vikram Sood, en pensionerad indisk underrättelsetjänsteman, varnade för att om terrorister använder BlackBerry för att planera och regeringen inte kan få åtkomst till deras kommunikation skulle landet vara oförberett. Även om teleoperatörer förbereder reservplaner förväntar de sig inte i stor utsträckning att BlackBerrys tjänster verkligen stängs ner, bland annat eftersom RIM lyckades undvika ett förbud genom att kompromissa med Saudiarabien. Förenade Arabemiraten har också hotat med liknande blockad om åtkomst inte ges. "Vi tror att det löser sig," sade Sanjay Warke, VD för Vodafone Indien. article_content: Jailed Nobel Peace Prize laureate Narges Mohammadi has been a leading figure in Iran’s women’s movement. When Berit Reiss-Andersen, chair of the Norwegian Nobel Committee, announced Mohammadi’s win, she recited the slogan, “Women, life, freedom”—a key phrase for women’s rights in Iran. Mohammadi is an Iranian human rights activist and physicist who has long fought against the oppression of women. At 51, she serves as a writer and deputy director of the Defenders of Human Rights Center (DHRC). Her activism spans many causes, including campaigning against the death penalty and corruption. According to the Norwegian Nobel Committee, Mohammadi received the prize 'for her fight against the oppression of women in Iran and her efforts to promote human rights and freedom for all.' Henrik Urdal, director of the Peace Research Institute Oslo, said the award is a significant boost to both Mohammadi and the DHRC. Over the past 30 years, Mohammadi has empowered women in Iran through education, advocacy, and grassroots organizing, including protests, sit-ins, and essays. Mohammadi is currently serving a 12-year sentence in Tehran’s Evin Prison for charges that include spreading propaganda against the state. She was first arrested in 2011, then detained again in 2015 following accusations of national security offenses and forming the group 'Step by Step to Stop the Death Penalty.' She was held in Zanjan Central Prison and released in 2020 after her sentence was reduced. Reiss-Andersen shared that, in total, Mohammadi has been arrested 13 times, convicted five times, and sentenced to 31 years in prison and 154 lashes. In September 2022, Mahsa Amini, 22, was arrested by Iran’s morality police for allegedly violating dress codes. She died after collapsing in custody, sparking protests across Iran. From prison, Mohammadi called Amini’s death a symbol of the regime’s oppression of women. Mohammadi has continued to share her experiences of abuse in Evin Prison, writing in The New York Times: 'The more of us they lock up, the stronger we become.' Mohammadi is the second Iranian woman to win the Nobel Peace Prize, following Shirin Ebadi in 2003 for her work promoting democracy and human rights. Ebadi, also a human rights activist and lawyer, was the first female judge in Iranian history and the first Muslim woman to receive the Nobel Prize. She has advocated for reforms in Iranian family law, including divorce, inheritance, and child protection. Mohammadi, who works closely with Ebadi at DHRC, has suffered health issues in prison, including a lung condition and neurological disorder. She has not been able to see her husband and two children due to her incarceration. Her husband and fellow activist, Taghi Ramahi, said, 'This Nobel Prize will strengthen Narges’s fight for human rights, but more importantly, it is a prize for the women, life, and freedom movement.'

article_content: Amazon has cut its monthly subscription fee for Indian exporters newly joining its global selling program from $39.99 to just $1 per month for the first three months. This offer is available until March 2024 to support festive season sales such as Thanksgiving, Black Friday, and Christmas. Ahead of these major shopping events, Indian exporters have added over 50,000 new products to Amazon’s international sites, with promotional sales set between November 17 and 27, covering Thanksgiving (Nov 23), Black Friday (Nov 24), and Cyber Monday (Nov 27). Indian sellers list a variety of items ranging from home and kitchen products, toys, apparel, health and personal care, office supplies, jewelry, beauty, to furniture. Since 2015, Amazon’s global selling program in India has expanded to more than 120,000 sellers across 200-plus cities and towns. The United States, Canada, and Germany are leading destinations for Indian exporters using the program, while Japan and Australia are rising markets. According to Bhupen Wakankar, director of Global Trade at Amazon India, the initiative is designed so sellers can benefit from multiple sales peaks throughout the year, beyond just major Indian festivals. Amazon aims to achieve $8 billion in exports from India by the end of 2023, with $3 billion generated in the last 15 months, and has reiterated its $20 billion export goal for 2025. The company’s cross-border logistics platform, SEND (Seller Exports and Delivery), has recently expanded to include ocean freight for Indian exporters, supplementing earlier air-only shipment options. Wakankar noted that Indian exporters are charged commissions similar to local sellers in the international markets they access.

Inför dessa stora shoppinghändelser har indiska exportörer lagt till över 50 000 nya produkter på Amazons internationella webbplatser, med kampanjförsäljning mellan 17 och 27 november, inklusive Thanksgiving (23 nov), Black Friday (24 nov) och Cyber Monday (27 nov). Indiska säljare erbjuder allt från hem- och köksprodukter, leksaker, kläder, hälsa och personlig vård, kontorsmaterial, smycken, skönhetsartiklar till möbler. Sedan 2015 har Amazons globala säljprogram i Indien vuxit till över 120 000 säljare från mer än 200 städer och orter. USA, Kanada och Tyskland är de största exportmarknaderna för indiska säljare inom programmet, medan Japan och Australien är nya tillväxtmarknader. Enligt Bhupen Wakankar, chef för Global Trade på Amazon Indien, är målet att säljare ska kunna dra nytta av flera försäljningstoppar under året, och inte bara vid större indiska högtider. Amazon siktar på att nå $8 miljarder i export från Indien till slutet av 2023, varav $3 miljarder kom de senaste 15 månaderna, och har bekräftat sitt exportmål om $20 miljarder till 2025. Företagets logistikprogram SEND (Seller Exports and Delivery) har nyligen utökats så att indiska exportörer nu kan skicka sjöfrakt utöver tidigare enbart flygfrakt. Wakankar tillade att indiska exportörer betalar provision liknande lokala säljare på de internationella marknaderna de når.

article_content: A few weeks ago, a senior citizen sent me a video featuring Dr. Chidi Ngwaba, a physician specializing in lifestyle medicine. His insights were so compelling that I immediately searched for his social media profiles. In doing so, I found a colleague’s introduction from a previous health talk: “Why would a surgeon put down his scalpel to talk to his patients about diet and lifestyle? Tune in for my live conversation with Dr. Chidi Ngwaba.” This sentiment echoes Thomas Edison’s 1903 prediction that “the doctor of the future will give no medicine but will instruct his patient in the care of the human frame in diet and the cause and prevention of disease.” At the Seventh Day Adventist Hospital in Ile-Ife, Osun State, there’s a section where patients are treated with food and plants—showing Edison's vision has arrived. Let’s take a closer look at nutrition and how it can positively or negatively influence our health. By the end, you might be inspired to commit to a healthier lifestyle. Nutrition is the process by which living things obtain the nutrients necessary for life. It’s a cornerstone of a healthy lifestyle. Making conscious food choices and balancing your diet can boost well-being, reduce chronic disease risk, and extend both life and vitality. Nutrition is an investment in your long-term health. There are philosophical and even religious perspectives on our ideal diets. For example, after creation, humanity was placed in a garden—filled with fruits and vegetables, not processed foods like cakes and sodas. Yet, processed food consumption has become common, despite warnings from experts like anthropologist Margaret Mead, who said, “It is easier to change a man’s religion than to change his diet.” Choosing the right diet is more than a joke—it is life or death. The foods we eat can nourish or harm us. As Benjamin Franklin remarked, “Few die of hunger, many die of eating.” Dr. Mark Hyman agrees: “Food is the cause and food is the cure of most diseases.” Our ancestors often enjoyed better health, living as hunter-gatherers and eating natural diets. Their immune systems were strong, often enabling them to avoid diseases. In my own childhood, community members drank from rivers or wells and remained healthy—a testament, perhaps, to the benefits of natural diets. Today, modern life is more sedentary, and unhealthy diets are widespread, contributing to non-communicable diseases. Historically and today, many experts—like Hippocrates—emphasized treating illness with food. In health-conscious social media groups, people report positive changes by adopting better nutritional habits, such as giving up soda or reducing carbohydrates. One remarkable story is that of Chris Wark, who, at 26, was diagnosed with stage 3 colon cancer. He had surgery but chose nutrition and natural therapies over chemotherapy, and is now cancer-free. Not all health challenges are hereditary; many are diet-related. Even if you have a family history of disease, a healthy diet can improve outcomes. Scientific studies, like 'The Role of Nutrition in Maintaining Optimal Health' by Martin Clarke, confirm that nutrition profoundly influences physical, mental, and emotional well-being. Optimizing nutrition fosters immunity and reduces chronic disease risk. Eating plenty of fruits and vegetables provides essential nutrients—such as selenium, iron, zinc, protein, and vitamins C and D—which support immune function. Combining good nutrition with exercise and avoiding smoking or excessive alcohol can further decrease disease risk. Making informed choices today can lead to a healthier, longer life.

Under sökandet hittade jag en kollegas introduktion från ett tidigare hälsoseminarium: “Varför skulle en kirurg lägga ner skalpellen för att prata med sina patienter om kost och livsstil? Låt oss titta närmare på hur näring kan påverka vår hälsa – både positivt och negativt. Kanske blir du inspirerad att satsa på en hälsosammare livsstil. Medvetna matval och en balanserad kost kan förbättra välmåendet, minska risken för kroniska sjukdomar och förlänga livet. Näring är en investering i din framtida hälsa. Det finns filosofiska och till och med religiösa perspektiv på hur vår ideala kost bör se ut. Till exempel placerades människan – enligt berättelser – först i en trädgård med frukt och grönsaker, inte kakor och läsk. Trots det har konsumtionen av processad mat blivit vanlig, vilket antropologen Margaret Mead varnade om: “Det är lättare att ändra en människas religion än hennes kost.” Att välja rätt kost är mer än bara ett skämt – det handlar faktiskt om liv och död. Den mat vi äter kan både stärka och skada oss. Benjamin Franklin sa: “Få dör av hunger, många dör av att äta.” Dr. Mark Hyman håller med: “Mat är orsaken och botemedlet till de flesta sjukdomar.” Våra förfäder hade ofta bättre hälsa, levde som jägare och samlare och åt naturlig kost. Deras immunförsvar var starkt, vilket hjälpte dem att undvika sjukdomar. Jag minns från min barndom hur folk i min by drack vatten från floder eller brunnar och ändå förblev friska – kanske tack vare kosten. Idag är livet mer stillasittande och dåliga matvanor är vanliga, vilket bidrar till icke-smittsamma sjukdomar. Historiskt och även idag har många experter – som Hippokrates – betonat att hälsosam mat kan användas för att behandla sjukdomar. I hälsofokuserade grupper på sociala medier berättar folk om positiva förändringar efter bättre kostvanor, som att sluta med läsk eller att dra ner på kolhydrater. Ett anmärkningsvärt exempel är Chris Wark, som vid 26 års ålder diagnosticerades med tjocktarmscancer i stadium 3. Han opererades men valde kost och naturliga terapier framför cellgifter och är nu frisk från cancer. Alla hälsoproblem är inte ärftliga – många har med kosten att göra. Även om du har ärftliga risker kan en sund kost förbättra dina förutsättningar. Vetenskapliga studier, som 'The Role of Nutrition in Maintaining Optimal Health' av Martin Clarke, visar att näring starkt påverkar fysisk, psykisk och emotionell hälsa. Att optimera kosten stärker immunförsvaret och minskar risken för kroniska sjukdomar. Rikligt med frukt och grönsaker ger viktiga näringsämnen såsom selen, järn, zink, protein samt vitaminerna C och D – vilket stöttar immunförsvaret. Att kombinera rätt matvanor med motion och undvika rökning eller överdriven alkoholkonsumtion minskar risken för sjukdomar ytterligare. Kloka val idag leder till bättre och längre liv.

article_content: Nubia is preparing to make a statement in the gaming smartphone market with the upcoming RedMagic 9 Pro, set to be unveiled later this month. On Weibo, the company teased key features of the device’s design. The RedMagic 9 Pro maintains a clean, rectangular look, but now sports a completely flat back—including the camera array. Unlike previous models, where the triple-lens setup protruded from the rear panel, the new cameras are flush with the back. Early details suggest the phone features a trio of lenses: the main 50MP ISOCELL GN5 sensor with OIS, an ISOCELL GN1 ultra-wide lens, and an as-yet unspecified third sensor. The camera sensors are positioned under the LED flash. RGB lighting remains central to the RedMagic identity. Teaser videos show colorful lights highlighting the ‘09’ (signifying the ninth generation), the built-in cooling fan under the camera array, and the side-mounted shoulder buttons. While complete specifications have not been shared, the phone’s design confirms the presence of Qualcomm’s latest Snapdragon 8 Gen 3 processor. Nubia says the device’s thickness has been reduced to 8.3mm, and an under-display camera is in place for an uninterrupted screen. The RedMagic 9 Pro will launch in three colorways: Dark Knight, Deuterium Front Transparent Dark Night, and Deuterium Front Transparent Silver Wing (translated names). The device will be officially revealed in China on November 23. Specification details remain scarce, but based on the RedMagic 8 Pro’s features—a 6.8-inch display, 8MP ultra-wide lens, 2MP macro sensor, and a 6,000mAh battery with 65W fast charging—some features may carry over. Nubia previously launched the global model a few months after the China release, a trend that may continue.

article_content: Singapore's Ministry of Health (MOH) has increased healthcare capacity by adding almost 500 new beds across the country so far this year. This includes 30 beds in acute hospitals, 90 in community hospitals, more than 350 in nursing homes, and 20 in home-based inpatient care. MOH also plans to add about 800 more beds by year-end, with a goal of 1,300 new beds in 2023. Health Minister Ong Ye Kung delivered this update during the opening ceremony for the rehabilitation and recovery wards at Tan Tock Seng Hospital's Integrated Care Hub on Monday (Oct 2). He noted that this increased capacity is equivalent to one and a half regional hospitals and is intended to relieve the ongoing bed shortage in hospitals. Minister Ong highlighted that additional beds mean more healthcare staff will be needed. He said the Ministry is monitoring infrastructure and staff increases carefully. Ong pointed out that the healthcare sector has faced significant challenges since COVID-19, and he expects demand to grow as Singapore's population ages. In April, MOH also revealed that median waiting times for hospital admissions had risen from about five to 7.2 hours. The main reason is that more patients, often elderly with complex medical conditions, require longer stays in hospital.

MOH planerar dessutom att lägga till cirka 800 fler sängar innan årets slut, med målet att totalt öka antalet sängar med 1 300 under 2023. Hälsominister Ong Ye Kung presenterade detta under invigningen av rehabiliterings- och återhämtningsavdelningarna på Tan Tock Seng Hospitals Integrated Care Hub på måndagen (2 okt). Han påpekade att kapacitetsökningen motsvarar en och en halv regionsjukhus och är tänkt att lindra den pågående sängbristen. Minister Ong betonade att fler sängar kräver mer sjukvårdspersonal, och berättade att ministeriet noga övervakar både utbyggnaden av vårdinfrastruktur och rekrytering av personal. Ong framhöll att sjukvården stått inför stora utmaningar sedan covid-19 och att efterfrågan sannolikt kommer att öka i takt med att befolkningen åldras. I april informerade MOH också om att mediantiden för att få sjukhusplats hade ökat från ungefär fem till 7,2 timmar. Detta beror framför allt på att fler, ofta äldre patienter med mer komplexa vårdbehov, nu behöver längre vårdtider.

England rugby legend Jonny Wilkinson has opened up about how he faced significant self-doubt in his relentless pursuit of perfection on the field. Speaking with Rob Burrow, Wilkinson revealed that his struggles came to a head during his final year playing for Toulon in France—when his normally reliable kicking deserted him at critical moments. “Five times, just before the final whistle, I had a chance to draw or win the game—I missed all five,” Wilkinson recalled. “I felt all those old scars coming up.”

At 44, Wilkinson appears as a guest on the new BBC podcast series 'Seven: Rob Burrow', where Leeds Rhinos legend Rob Burrow and his wife Lindsey interview seven sports stars, asking each seven questions. The series is available on BBC Sounds.

Wilkinson, who made his England debut in 1998 and played for Newcastle Falcons, scored 1,179 points for England—a record surpassed only recently by Owen Farrell. His iconic drop goal in the closing moments of the 2003 Rugby World Cup final against Australia secured one of England's most memorable sporting victories. However, Wilkinson describes how, during his last professional matches, these earlier triumphs felt increasingly distant. “As a kid, I dreamt of being carried off on shoulders. In my final year—after all the hard work—I missed all five kicks,” he said.

He added: “Instead of being carried off on their shoulders and looking down on my teammates, feeling their love, I saw heartbreak in their eyes. I felt all those old scars coming up—‘you weren’t enough for this,’ ‘they’ll never respect you’—all those things I’d always chased.” When asked what advice he’d give his seven-year-old self, Wilkinson replied: “You’re enough, you’re safe, there is nothing missing.”

Among other topics, Wilkinson shared that he once had the opportunity to spend a summer playing rugby league with Wigan Warriors while recovering from injury, but ultimately decided against it, fearing further injury could end his career. Responding to a joke from Burrow, who called rugby league the “faster, tougher version of the sport,” Wilkinson admitted: “I probably watch more rugby league than rugby union; it’s been that way for a long time.”

Podcast host Rob Burrow, a patron of the Motor Neurone Disease Association, uses AI technology and recordings of his own voice—along with eye-gaze assistance—to communicate during the series. Upcoming guests on the podcast include double Olympic gold medallist Dame Kelly Holmes and seven-time Paralympic gold medallist Hannah Cockroft.

article_content: Actor Sean Penn chose to attend a Senate hearing on Haiti's earthquake recovery in Washington D.C. instead of appearing at the Cannes Film Festival. His latest movie, 'Fair Game,' was set to premiere at Cannes, but Penn prioritized addressing the Senate Foreign Relations Committee, highlighting the urgent need for transparency in aid for Haiti. He emphasized that donations must directly benefit the people affected by the disaster. Penn, who leads the J/P Haitian Relief Organization, has been actively involved in Haiti—living in Port-au-Prince and helping oversee a major camp for earthquake survivors. He joined experts and officials, including Senator John Kerry, to push for efficient and accountable recovery efforts. Senator Kerry, supporting a bill allocating $3.5 billion for Haiti’s reconstruction over five years, reiterated that nations who pledged a total of $10 billion at a conference in March need to deliver these funds and ensure they are used wisely. He also stressed the importance of Haiti improving its ability to manage aid. Andrew Natsios, former USAID Administrator, described the formidable obstacles ahead, calling Haiti a 'failed state.' By comparing Haiti’s catastrophe to Chile’s more powerful but less devastating earthquake, he underlined the role of poor governance in Haiti’s struggles. Natsios argued that aid programs should concentrate on strengthening institutions and fostering economic growth, cautioning against oversimplified solutions.

article_content: Google is reportedly close to investing about $4 million in Corover.ai, an Indian conversational artificial intelligence startup, according to sources familiar with the matter. This move reflects the rapidly growing interest in the Indian AI startup ecosystem. Last week, it was reported that Adobe acquired Bengaluru-based AI video creation platform Rephrase.ai. Corover is one of the few Indian startups developing an indigenous large language model (LLM) named BharatGPT, which supports more than a dozen Indian languages. Google previously made a non-equity funding of $500,000 to Corover after signing an agreement in March, and is now in talks to invest $4 million in equity following the upcoming launch of BharatGPT, sources said. The startup has already received much of the $500,000 with the remainder expected by December. As a strategic partner, Google also provides cloud computing credits to Corover. The new funds are expected to help scale up BharatGPT in the coming weeks. Corover, founded in 2016, has investors such as CanBank Venture Capital Fund, Lead Angels, Cognify, Karekeba Ventures, and IIIT-Delhi. According to Tracxn, the startup was valued at $8.5 million as of December 2022. Corover's clients and partners, as listed on its website, include IRCTC, NPCI, ICICI Prudential, ITC, Max Life Insurance, Bosch, Karnataka Tourism, Israel Tourism, Chandigarh Smart City, and Car and Bike. Industry experts believe that many Indian companies focusing on AI for Indian languages are attracting the attention of global tech firms seeking to enhance their AI capabilities, particularly in regional languages. In a separate development, Adobe's recent acquisition of Rephrase.ai marks its first deal in the Generative AI and video-tooling sector, and its first acquisition of an Indian startup for such technology. Corover offers text, audio, and video chatbots in Indian and foreign languages, which can be integrated across platforms such as WhatsApp, Signal, Zoom, Salesforce, and SAP. The company serves clients in banking, finance, healthcare, manufacturing, travel, and e-commerce. Google and Corover did not respond to requests for comment before press time.

article_content:
Rachel Motte, a writer who grew up listening to Rush Limbaugh, examines the enduring impact of the prominent conservative radio host. Motte reminisces about discovering Limbaugh’s program as a child in the late 1980s; his sharp wit and commentary resonated with her family and made political satire a memorable part of her upbringing. Though she once dreamed of convincing Limbaugh to run for president, she now believes he’s most influential behind the microphone.

Motte discusses ongoing conversations among conservatives about Limbaugh’s place in modern politics. While many liberals are quick to label him as the Republican Party’s unofficial figurehead—often to make him an easier target—Motte argues that Limbaugh has never been the party’s leader. Instead, she sees him as an essential force in energizing the conservative support base, especially after political setbacks. She references Republican National Committee Chairman Michael Steele, who called Limbaugh just "an entertainer" before retracting, illustrating the complexities of Limbaugh’s status.

Critics, including Motte’s colleague John Mark Reynolds, have described Limbaugh’s tone and jargon as potentially alienating to young voters—a concern echoed by the fact that the majority of voters under 30 supported President Obama, whose campaign was known for its dynamic messaging. Motte acknowledges that the generational shift in political communication could lessen Limbaugh’s resonance, but maintains that his impact lingers among those shaped by his broadcasts.

Motte concludes that while conservatives will need new voices to connect with changing audiences, Limbaugh remains a notable figure for now. She predicts that future conservative leaders will often trace some of their inspiration back to him.

Även om hon en gång drömde om att övertala Limbaugh att kandidera till president, tycker hon idag att han gör störst intryck bakom mikrofonen.

article_content: On Australia’s Gold Coast, a woman unwittingly ate part of a dead mouse that was inside a handmade rice paper roll she’d bought for $5.50 at Woolworths. She only discovered the rodent when she noticed fur after a couple of bites, missing the tail that protruded from one end. Her daughter Emilie Petrusic expressed shock, saying it seemed impossible for a whole animal to end up in a hand-prepared roll. Woolworths suggested in a statement that the mouse was likely introduced after the product left the store. Local authorities have launched an investigation, and the affected woman is undergoing medical tests. Public health official Dr. Paul Van Buynder stated that it’s too early to determine the full story but confirmed that inquiries are ongoing. A nearly identical event occurred in Russia the previous week, where 28-year-old Anatol Voronkov found a dead mouse inside a sausage he’d already started eating. He initially thought the object was a piece of pepper, only to realize it was a rodent’s foot. The animal is being tested for disease in that case.

Hennes dotter, Emilie Petrusic, uttryckte chock och sa att det verkade omöjligt att ett helt djur skulle hamna i en handgjord rulle. Woolworths uppgav i ett uttalande att musen troligen hamnat i produkten efter att den lämnat butiken. Lokala myndigheter har inlett en utredning och kvinnan genomgår medicinska tester. Hälsochefen Dr. Paul Van Buynder sade att det är för tidigt att säga exakt vad som hänt men att utredning pågår. En nästan identisk händelse inträffade i Ryssland veckan innan, då 28-årige Anatol Voronkov hittade en död mus i en korv han redan börjat äta. Först trodde han att det var en pepparbit men insåg sedan att det var en gnagares fot. Djuret testas för sjukdomar där.

article_content:
Chevron has announced it will acquire Hess Corp. in a stock transaction valued at $53 billion. This is one of the largest deals in the energy sector this month, coming soon after Exxon Mobil’s $60 billion agreement to buy Pioneer Natural Resources. The rise in crude oil prices, currently around $90 per barrel, has made major oil producers cash-rich and eager to invest. Ongoing geopolitical tensions—including the war in Ukraine and conflict in the Middle East—along with output cuts from Saudi Arabia and Russia, have contributed to rising prices.

Chevron’s purchase of Hess will give it substantial assets, including a significant offshore oil field in Guyana and shale holdings in North Dakota’s Bakken Formation. Guyana, with a population of approximately 791,000, is on course to become the world’s fourth-largest offshore oil producer, surpassing countries like Qatar, the U.S., Mexico, and Norway. Competition for Guyana’s lucrative oil fields has intensified among global players such as Exxon Mobil, China’s CNOOC, and Hess.

According to Chevron CEO Mike Wirth, this acquisition aligns with the company’s goal to deliver higher returns and lower carbon emissions. Chevron expects the deal to boost its production and cash flow growth rates in the next five years, extending its growth profile into the next decade. The acquisition will be completed through an all-stock transaction, with Hess shareholders receiving 1.0250 Chevron shares for every Hess share they own. Including assumed debt, the total deal value reaches $60 billion.

Despite growing climate concerns after a summer of record-setting temperatures, higher energy prices have led to increased exploration and drilling, benefiting investors. Recent years have seen a wave of mergers focused on U.S. shale fields. During the pandemic in 2020, Chevron acquired Noble Energy for $5 billion, and ConocoPhillips bought Concho Resources for $9.7 billion in stock.

Last month, the UK approved a significant oil and gas project in the North Sea, overlooking advice from scientists and the United Nations warning that the development of new fossil fuel resources should pause to prevent extreme climate change.

Chevron anticipates the Hess acquisition will enable it to return more cash to shareholders, including a projected 8% increase in its first-quarter dividend to $1.63 per share (pending board approval) and a $2.5 billion boost in annual stock buybacks, potentially reaching $20 billion.

The deal has been approved by the boards of both Chevron and Hess, following six months of negotiations. It is expected to close in the first half of next year, pending approval from Hess shareholders. Hess CEO John Hess is set to join Chevron’s board upon completion, and his family retains significant ownership in Hess. On Monday, Chevron shares dropped 3.7%, while Hess shares fell by 1%.

article_content: Following Armistice Day, London saw significant demonstrations from both far-right activists and pro-Palestinian groups. The protests, which took place near the Cenotaph and throughout central London, led to clashes with police, resulting in 126 arrests and nine officers injured. Coverage in national newspapers emphasized concerns over disruptions on this day of remembrance. The Sunday Express and The Sun On Sunday criticized the actions of extremist groups, observing that moments of silence were interrupted by unrest and highlighting the involvement of both pro-Palestinian marchers and the English Defence League. Michael Gove, the levelling up secretary, was escorted by police after reportedly encountering pro-Palestinian protesters at London Victoria station. News outlets called for legal action against those responsible for violence. Prime Minister Rishi Sunak condemned the disorder and stated that lawbreakers should be swiftly prosecuted. He reiterated his criticism of Met Police Commissioner Sir Mark Rowley’s approval of the pro-Palestinian march. The Sunday Telegraph highlighted Sunak’s condemnation of perceived disrespect by both far-right and pro-Palestinian demonstrators. Labour leader Keir Starmer wrote that, while violent incitement must be addressed, peaceful advocacy for Gaza should not be silenced. He also reproached Sunak and Home Secretary Suella Braverman for their rhetoric before the protests, accusing Braverman of contradicting British values. Other papers, including The Sunday People and the Sunday Mirror, featured calls for Braverman's dismissal because of her handling of recent events. The Observer reported that mass demonstrations have intensified pressure on political leaders to support a ceasefire in Gaza.

article_content: With thousands of anti-abortion activists in Washington, D.C. for the annual March for Life, House Republicans prepared to advance legislation to ban most abortions after 20 weeks of pregnancy, despite a veto threat from the White House. GOP leaders had scheduled a vote on the legislation for Thursday but abruptly postponed it late Wednesday, citing insufficient support within their caucus. Several Republican women objected to a provision requiring victims of rape or incest seeking an abortion after 20 weeks to first report the crime to police. Instead, the House planned to vote on a separate bill to bar taxpayer funding of abortions, a restriction already largely in place. Republicans said the measure would further tighten current regulations, ensuring no federal funds support abortions under the Affordable Care Act. Anti-abortion activists staged a demonstration in front of the White House on Wednesday, as the day marked the 42nd anniversary of the Roe v. Wade Supreme Court decision that legalized abortion nationwide. Each year, anti-abortion advocates march from the National Mall to the Supreme Court in protest. The postponed bill would have included exemptions for rape, incest, and when a woman's life is at risk. GOP leaders faced criticism when some lawmakers, notably Rep. Rene Ellmers (NC) and Rep. Jackie Walorski (IN), argued the reporting requirement placed undue pressure on survivors of assault. A 2013 Justice Department report found only 35% of rapes and sexual assaults are reported to police, a statistic cited by the White House in its veto threat. Political considerations were complex for Republicans. Party leaders hesitated to postpone a prominent abortion vote during the annual anti-abortion march but also did not want to alienate GOP women as the party seeks to attract more female voters ahead of the 2016 election. Attempts to remove the reporting requirement met resistance from anti-abortion groups, who are a key Republican constituency, according to party aides. The episode highlighted the challenge GOP leaders face in unifying their caucus as they strive to govern effectively. Some lawmakers criticized the situation as a 'debacle,' while Rep. Marsha Blackburn (TN), a sponsor of the postponed bill, described it as part of the process to craft effective legislation. Tony Perkins, president of the Family Research Council, expressed disappointment over the delay but praised leaders for their commitment to pro-life policies, noting misconceptions about the bill, which would restrict abortions after five months. He pointed out that the U.S. is one of the few countries that allow abortions throughout an entire pregnancy. On Wednesday, Sen. Barbara Boxer (CA) and Sen. Patty Murray (WA), along with women's health advocates, held a press conference criticizing what they called 'Republican attacks on women's health' and the proposed abortion ban. Democratic lawmakers and advocates for abortion rights welcomed the GOP's decision to postpone the vote. Rep. Jim McGovern (MA) described the GOP's difficulties as a 'meltdown.' Cecile Richards, president of Planned Parenthood Action Fund, argued the bill was out of touch, saying, 'These attacks are so dangerous, extreme, and unpopular that House Republicans can't even get their membership lined up behind them.' The National Organization for Women called the delay a victory, saying it showed the bill was too extreme for some in the GOP. NOW added that the alternative legislation was still an attempt to undermine women's rights. House Minority Leader Nancy Pelosi (CA) criticized the new bill, saying it was 'much worse' because it could affect millions rather than thousands by banning health insurance funds from covering abortions. She argued the bill would restrict a woman's ability to use her insurance for reproductive services, calling it a setback for women's health. The 20-week abortion ban had little chance of passing, facing both White House opposition and an uncertain outlook in the Senate where anti-abortion sentiment is less prevalent. The White House stated that the bill would 'unacceptably restrict women's health and reproductive rights' and noted that requiring survivors of rape or incest to report to law enforcement shows a disregard for the challenges these women face. Research shows most sexual assault survivors do not report the crime. House Republicans maintained that the Pain-Capable Unborn Child Protection Act demonstrated their support for a key conservative issue. Supporters argued it would protect fetuses purportedly able to feel pain, while opponents cited medical groups like the American Congress of Obstetricians and Gynecologists, which say fetuses are unlikely to experience pain before the third trimester (around 28 weeks). A recent Congressional Budget Office report estimated about 10,000 abortions each year occur at or after 20 weeks of pregnancy. If the bill became law, most of these abortions would likely occur earlier, according to the CBO.

Han påpekade även att USA är ett av få länder där abort tillåts genom hela graviditeten. På onsdagen höll Barbara Boxer (Kalifornien) och Patty Murray (Washington) samt kvinnors hälsoförespråkare en presskonferens där de kritiserade det de kallade 'republikanska attacker på kvinnors hälsa' och det föreslagna abortförbudet. Demokratiska ledamöter och abortförespråkare välkomnade GOP:s beslut att skjuta upp omröstningen. Jim McGovern (Massachusetts) beskrev republikanernas problem som 'en kollaps'. National Organization for Women kallade förseningen för en seger och sa att lagförslaget till och med sågs som för extremt för vissa inom GOP. Minoritetsledaren Nancy Pelosi (Kalifornien) kritiserade det nya förslaget och sa att det var 'mycket värre' eftersom det skulle påverka miljoner istället för tusentals kvinnor genom att förbjuda sjukförsäkringspengar till aborter. Hon hävdade att förslaget skulle begränsa en kvinnas möjlighet att använda sin försäkring för reproduktiva tjänster, och kallade det ett bakslag för kvinnors hälsa. Abortförbudet efter 20 veckor hade liten chans att gå igenom, både på grund av Vita husets motstånd och osäkerheten i senaten där motstånd mot abort är mindre utbrett. Vita huset menade att lagförslaget skulle 'oacceptabelt begränsa kvinnors hälsa och reproduktiva rättigheter' och att kravet att offer för våldtäkt eller incest måste anmäla till myndigheter visar brist på förståelse för deras situation. Forskning visar att de flesta offer för sexuella övergrepp inte anmäler brottet. Republikanerna i Representanthuset höll fast vid att Pain-Capable Unborn Child Protection Act visade deras stöd för en viktig konservativ fråga. Förespråkarna hävdade att förslaget skulle skydda foster som påstods kunna känna smärta, medan motståndare hänvisade till läkarorganisationer som American Congress of Obstetricians and Gynecologists, vilka säger att foster förmodligen inte kan känna smärta före tredje trimestern (ungefär vecka 28). article_content: It comes as no surprise that Joe Simpson appears wise beyond his years. The 26-year-old Wasps scrum-half speaks with maturity after experiencing a year of emotional turmoil following the tragic passing of his 58-year-old mother, Brigid, who died last January after a six-month battle with skin cancer. Simpson has emerged as a calm and reflective individual and is currently playing the best rugby of his career—a testament to both himself and his club. 'Last season was tough,' Simpson said. 'It was emotionally draining. My mother sacrificed so much, driving me across the country from the age of 10 to club games and England camps. Some places were far from glamorous, and I remember her standing in the rain, all wrapped up. My family has always been incredibly supportive.' On the field, Simpson has been in superb form for a rejuvenated Wasps team this season. After his mother's death, he found solace in rugby. 'Rugby was a brilliant distraction for me,' he said. 'The coaches, the owner, and every staff member were fantastic. They offered me as much time off as I needed after Mum died, but I wanted to keep playing. It’s what I do.' 'Being around the team let me temporarily forget things on the training pitch. The support I received meant a lot to me when I was feeling low. I’ve come back feeling fresh and I’m loving rugby and being part of the club’s renewal. I’m thrilled with how things are going.' Simpson, who is part of a core group of Wasps players who stayed loyal during the club’s financial difficulties two seasons ago, feels a strong connection to the side he supported as a boy growing up near their training ground in Acton, West London. With major investment, a move to Coventry’s Ricoh Arena, and ambitious recruitment, Simpson’s form at scrum-half reflects the club’s improved health. 'The players brought in by (director of rugby) Dai Young have integrated well with the squad, and you can see it in the results,' Simpson added. 'We’re not the finished article yet, but it’s a great place to play, train, and be part of. I’m playing the best rugby of my career.' 'I’m leading matches more effectively and still maintaining my edge with the ability to score tries and use my pace. It’s something that makes me distinctive among No. 9s.' On Saturday night at The Stoop, Simpson faces England scrum-half Danny Care, whom he replaced in the 2011 World Cup squad after Care was injured. Simpson’s single international cap came in the pool win over Georgia. It’s possible that Simpson’s club form could earn him a call-up for this year’s World Cup. A strong performance against Care in a crucial European match—taking place just days before Stuart Lancaster announces his Six Nations squad—would help his chances. 'Playing for England is why you play rugby,' said Simpson, who recently made his 150th appearance for Wasps. 'I’ve been involved with the England squad in autumn and Six Nations before. I’ve been capped and gone to a World Cup, and that’s where I want to be. There’s no bigger stage.' 'I haven’t spoken to the England coaches. I’m just keeping my head down and working hard here. My all-round game is at its peak and I want to keep improving into my mid-30s. I believe I can offer England something and I’d love to have the opportunity. It’s about maintaining my form and the club’s form.' 'I always set my goals high but try to stay realistic. My ambition is to break into the England squad, and I would love to be selected for the World Cup. First and foremost, I’d love to be part of the squad this summer. That would give me a chance—and then it’s up to me to take it.' Given the personal tragedy Simpson endured last season, few would begrudge him some good fortune.

Hon gick bort i januari förra året efter ett halvårs kamp mot hudcancer. Simpson har blivit en lugn och eftertänksam person och spelar nu sin livs bästa rugby – ett bevis på både hans egen och klubbens styrka. 'Förra säsongen var tuff,' säger Simpson. 'Det var känslomässigt dränerande. Min mamma offrade så mycket, körde mig runt hela landet från att jag var tio år till klubbmatcher och Englands campar. På planen har Simpson varit i strålande form för ett förnyat Wasps den här säsongen. Efter sin mammas död fann han tröst i rugby. 'Rugby var ett fantastiskt avbrott för mig,' säger han. Simpson, som tillhör en kärngrupp spelare i Wasps som var lojala under klubbens ekonomiska svårigheter för två säsonger sedan, känner en stark koppling till laget han hejade på som liten nära deras träningsanläggning i Acton, västra London. 'Jag leder matcherna mer effektivt och behåller ändå min känsla för att skapa chanser och utnyttja min snabbhet. Det gör mig speciell bland nummer 9.' På lördag kväll på The Stoop ställs Simpson mot Englands scrumhalf Danny Care, som han ersatte i VM-truppen 2011 efter att Care blivit skadad. Simpsons enda landskamp kom i gruppsegern mot Georgien. Det är möjligt att Simpsons klubbform kan göra att han blir inkallad till årets VM. En stark insats mot Care i en avgörande europamatch – bara dagar innan Stuart Lancaster tar ut sin Six Nations-trupp – skulle stärka hans chanser. 'Att spela för England är varför man spelar rugby,' säger Simpson, som nyligen gjorde sin 150:e match för Wasps. 'Jag har varit med i Englands trupp under hösten och Six Nations förut. Jag har blivit uttagen tidigare och varit med på ett VM, och det är där jag vill vara. Det finns ingen större scen.' 'Jag har inte pratat med Englands tränare. Jag försöker bara jobba hårt här och hålla låg profil. Mitt spel är på topp och jag vill fortsätta utvecklas in i 30-årsåldern. Jag tror jag kan erbjuda något till England och skulle älska att få möjligheten. Det handlar om att jag och klubben håller formen.' 'Jag sätter alltid mina mål högt men försöker vara realistisk. Min ambition är att slå mig in i Englands trupp, och jag skulle älska att bli uttagen till VM. Först och främst vill jag vara med i sommarens trupp. Då får jag en chans – och då gäller det att ta den.' Med tanke på den personliga tragedi Simpson gick igenom förra säsongen, är det få som inte skulle unna honom lite medgång.

article_content: Sidney Powell, who previously served as an attorney for Donald Trump, has pleaded guilty to six charges in the Georgia 2020 presidential election interference case. Through a plea deal, Powell agreed to six years of probation, payment of a fine, a recorded statement about her actions, and an apology letter to Georgia’s citizens. She will also testify against co-defendants in upcoming trials. Powell was among 19 individuals, including Trump, accused in the case. Most maintain their innocence. Prosecutors assert she coordinated efforts to disrupt official election processes, including enlisting a forensic team to unlawfully access and analyze voting machines and voter data in Coffee County, Georgia. Legal experts say Powell’s choice reflects a common strategy to avoid jail, particularly for first-time offenders. Former federal prosecutor Neama Rahmani noted that such deals can prompt others to reconsider their positions to avoid harsher penalties. Allegations include conspiring to tamper with voting equipment and obstruct poll workers. Powell became well-known for promoting unfounded claims of widespread election fraud, including allegations—without evidence—against Dominion Voting Systems, who have sued her for $1.3 billion for defamation. Powell is the second defendant to cooperate with prosecutors. Recently, Scott Hall, a bail bondsman, accepted similar probation terms and agreed to testify. Trump has pleaded not guilty and faces 13 felony counts related to efforts to overturn the election, calling the case politically motivated.

Genom en överenskommelse med åklagaren har Powell gått med på sex års villkorlig dom, att betala böter, spela in ett uttalande om sina handlingar och skriva ett ursäktsbrev till invånarna i Georgia. Hon kommer även att vittna mot de övriga åtalade i kommande rättegångar. Powell var en av 19 personer, däribland Trump, som åtalats i ärendet. De flesta hävdar fortfarande sin oskuld. Åklagare menar att hon organiserade insatser för att störa de officiella valprocesserna, bland annat genom att anlita ett forensiskt team för att olagligt komma åt och analysera röstningsmaskiner och väljarinformation i Coffee County, Georgia. Juridiska experter menar att Powells val är en vanlig strategi för att undgå fängelse, särskilt för förstagångsförbrytare. Den före detta federala åklagaren Neama Rahmani påpekar att sådana överenskommelser kan få andra åtalade att ompröva sina val för att slippa hårdare straff. Anklagelserna mot Powell inkluderar sammansvärjning för att manipulera valsystem och hindra valarbetare från att genomföra sitt jobb. Powell blev känd för att sprida obekräftade påståenden om omfattande valfusk, inklusive anklagelser – utan bevis – mot Dominion Voting Systems, som nu har stämt henne på 1,3 miljarder dollar för förtal. Powell är den andra åtalade som samarbetar med åklagarna. Nyligen antog borgenären Scott Hall ett liknande avtal och kommer också att vittna. Trump har förnekat brott och står åtalad för 13 grova brott relaterade till försöken att omvända valresultatet, och han beskriver åtalet som politiskt motiverat.

article_content: An illicit market for delivery app accounts is making it possible for minors to work as food delivery riders, as revealed by a BBC investigation. The family of a 17-year-old named Leo, who lost his life while riding for Deliveroo—despite the company requiring employees to be at least 18—has called Deliveroo 'unaccountable.' The UK Home Office is now pressing delivery giants including Deliveroo, Just Eat, and Uber Eats to tighten their rules on 'substitution,' which allows account holders to let someone else use their account. Although riders are supposed to undergo background checks and verify their eligibility, once approved they are allowed to substitute someone else without the company's direct oversight. This loophole has led to an underground trade in delivery app accounts, some of which are being rented or sold to children. Leo began working as a Deliveroo rider at just 15, renting an account from an older man in his town. Two years later, at 17, he died in a crash while using a borrowed motorbike and still working through the app. Deliveroo's policy states all riders must be over 18, but the company had no record of Leo's employment because he used someone else's account. Leo's family, wishing to withhold their surname for privacy, is speaking out in hopes of preventing similar tragedies. His stepfather Patrick describes Deliveroo and other companies as taking no responsibility, while his mother Preta notes the appeal of high earnings for teens. Despite the rules, platforms rely on original account holders to verify the legality of substitutes instead of conducting their own checks. The BBC investigation uncovered numerous online ads offering delivery app accounts for sale or rent. Reporters were able to find sellers willing to lease Deliveroo, Just Eat, and Uber Eats accounts to users as young as 16, often for significant weekly fees, and with the sellers assuring that age or identity checks are easily bypassed. Responding to inquiries, Deliveroo said it enforces a 'zero tolerance approach' to ineligible riders and stops working with them immediately. Just Eat and Uber Eats also stressed that couriers must meet legal requirements, but noted that self-employed riders have the right to use substitutes, with the account holder responsible for ensuring compliance. Concerned by the situation, the Home Office has summoned major delivery platforms for a roundtable and published an open letter demanding stricter controls on account substitution. Minister Robert Jenrick emphasized that failing to check substitutes can have deadly consequences, citing Leo's case as a tragic example. This year alone, the Home Office reported arresting 381 riders in the UK found working without proper authorization. All three companies say they are cooperating with authorities and reviewing their procedures to prevent further abuse.

article_content: On Halloween 2023, instead of ghostly costumes, scientists have revealed a hand-shaped structure in space using two X-ray telescopes. This remarkable formation is caused by a collapsed star—now a neutron star—that emits energized matter and antimatter. About 1,500 years ago, a massive star within our galaxy used up its nuclear fuel and collapsed inward, forming a dense neutron star. This neutron star is a pulsar—not to be confused with the motorcycle. In astronomy, pulsars are rotating neutron stars with powerful magnetic fields. Pulsars serve as cosmic laboratories for studying extreme physics because their conditions cannot be reproduced on Earth. Young pulsars can generate jets of matter and antimatter from their poles, along with an intense wind, resulting in what is known as a pulsar wind nebula. NASA’s Chandra X-ray Observatory first observed this 'hand-shaped' pulsar wind nebula, designated PSR B1509-58, in 2001. The pulsar sits at the base of the nebula’s 'palm.' The nebula, called MSH 15-52, is about 16,000 light-years from Earth. Scientists recently used NASA’s Imaging X-ray Polarimetry Explorer (IXPE) to observe MSH 15-52 continuously for approximately 17 days—its longest observation of a single object since its launch in December 2021. IXPE data revealed a bright X-ray jet stretching from the nebula’s 'wrist.' The polarization increases along the jet, likely influenced by tangled magnetic fields and turbulence at its origin.

För ungefär 1 500 år sedan förbrukade en massiv stjärna i vår galax sitt kärnbränsle och kollapsade och bildade en tät neutronstjärna. Denna neutronstjärna är en pulsar—inte att förväxla med motorcykeln. Inom astronomi är pulsarer roterande neutronstjärnor med kraftfulla magnetfält. Unga pulsarer kan skapa jetstrålar av materia och antimateria från sina poler, tillsammans med en kraftig vind, vilket leder till det som kallas en pulsarvindnebulosa. article_content: Victims of burglaries and domestic incidents are waiting over 13 hours for police to respond in some areas, according to figures obtained by the Liberal Democrats. Party leader Sir Ed Davey stated that insufficient police resourcing is causing excessive delays, leading to missed opportunities for gathering vital evidence and witnesses. Last year, a policing watchdog described low charge rates for burglary, theft, and robbery as 'unacceptable.' The National Police Chiefs’ Council (NPCC) has said that improving response times is now a priority. A spokesperson for the NPCC explained that efficient response times help protect the public, support investigations, collect evidence, and bring offenders to justice. Police forces determine incident response targets based on factors like size, geography, and local area needs. Most aim to respond to Grade 2 calls — serious incidents requiring urgent police action but not posing life-threatening risks — within one hour. However, of the 29 police forces that responded to Freedom of Information requests by the Lib Dems, only 10 met this one-hour target. On average, Grade 2 response times almost doubled from 1 hour 48 minutes in 2020 to 3 hours 12 minutes in 2022. In Birmingham West, people reporting burglaries, missing persons, or domestic incidents waited an average of 13 and a half hours for police attendance — the longest among forces providing data. In Birmingham East, also policed by West Midlands Police, the average wait was 11 and a half hours. Areas like Aylesbury Vale and Reading, covered by Thames Valley Police, had average waits exceeding 10 hours. In Surrey, average response times reached nearly seven and a half hours. West Midlands Police stated that a new policing model is leading to monthly improvements in response to incidents. A spokesperson said they prioritize crimes that cause the most harm — such as burglary, robbery, vehicle crime, and domestic abuse — and have recently achieved record-high arrests and positive outcomes. Thames Valley Police said it is working to reduce overall response times. Their spokesperson added that response times depend on many factors, including officer numbers, current workloads, and where officers are based. The Liberal Democrats, who are calling for a return to community policing, argue that years of underfunding have stretched police resources thin, decreasing attention to local crime. Since 2015, more than 4,500 community officers have been lost, with only 12% now working in neighborhood teams. The Lib Dems also criticize the cost and effectiveness of Police and Crime Commissioners, describing a 'postcode lottery' in response times based on location. Sir Ed Davey said, 'People deserve a swift police response when they’ve been victims of crime, regardless of where they live. These delays force victims to endure agonizing waits and risk denying them justice. Crucial evidence and witnesses can be lost during extended waiting times, which is unacceptable. The Home Secretary must focus on effective basics rather than ineffective initiatives.' A recent government recruitment campaign has restored police officer levels above 2010 figures, but there are concerns this hasn't kept up with population growth and that many experienced officers have left. Home Secretary Suella Braverman claimed the increase in officers will help prevent violence, solve burglaries, and address anti-social behavior. Under Ms Braverman, new policing guidelines require officers to pursue all reasonable lines of enquiry in investigations, amid concerns that burglary and theft have been de-prioritized. The Home Office emphasized that all police forces are expected to respond promptly to emergency calls and that the Home Secretary wants forces to take a zero-tolerance approach to crime. In 2022, the NPCC committed to ensuring police attend all home burglaries to improve detection. Nevertheless, 74.2% of burglary cases and 73.7% of theft cases were closed last year without a suspect identified. About half of domestic abuse-related cases were closed due to evidential difficulties, often because victims did not support further action. The Labour Party has pledged to recruit an additional 13,000 neighborhood police officers if elected in the next general election.

Partiledaren Sir Ed Davey menar att otillräckliga resurser inom polisen leder till stora förseningar och missade möjligheter att samla in viktig bevisning och vittnesmål. Förra året kallade en tillsynsmyndighet de låga åtalsfrekvenserna för inbrott, stöld och rån för 'oacceptabla'. Nationella Polisrådet (NPCC) har nu som prioritet att förbättra insatstiderna. En talesperson för NPCC förklarade att effektiva insatstider skyddar allmänheten, stödjer utredningar, samlar bevis och ställer gärningsmän inför rätta. Polisdistrikten fastställer sina mål för insatstider utifrån faktorer som storlek, geografi och lokala förhållanden. De flesta siktar på att åka på så kallade Grad 2-larm – allvarliga händelser som kräver polisiärt ingripande men inte innebär omedelbar livsfara – inom en timme. Av de 29 polisdistrikt som svarade på Liberaldemokraternas informationsförfrågan uppnådde dock bara 10 en timmesmålet. I genomsnitt har insatstiderna för Grad 2-ärenden nästan fördubblats från 1 timme och 48 minuter år 2020 till 3 timmar och 12 minuter år 2022. I Birmingham West fick de som anmälde inbrott, försvunna personer eller våldsärenden i hemmet vänta i snitt 13 och en halv timme på polis – det längsta bland de distrikt som lämnat siffror. I Birmingham East, också inom West Midlands Police, var snittet elva och en halv timme. Områden som Aylesbury Vale och Reading, som täcks av Thames Valley Police, hade väntetider över tio timmar. I Surrey blev snittet nästan sju och en halv timme. West Midlands Police uppger att en ny polisiär modell leder till fortlöpande förbättringar av insatstiderna varje månad. En talesperson säger att man prioriterar brott som orsakar störst skada – som inbrott, rån, bilbrott och våld i hemmet – och att man nyligen har nått rekordhöga nivåer av gripanden och lyckade utredningar. Thames Valley Police arbetar på att minska insatstiderna totalt sett. En talesperson säger att insatstider påverkas av flera faktorer, till exempel antal patrullerande poliser, arbetsbelastning och var personalen är placerad. Liberaldemokraterna, som vill återinföra närpolisverksamhet, hävdar att flera års underfinansiering har tömt resurserna och lett till mindre fokus på lokala brott. Sedan 2015 har över 4 500 närpoliser försvunnit och bara 12 % arbetar nu inom närpolisteam. Liberaldemokraterna kritiserar också kostnaden och effektiviteten hos polischeferna och beskriver situationen som ett 'postnummerlotteri' där väntetiderna varierar beroende på var man bor. Sir Ed Davey säger: 'Folk förtjänar en snabb polisiär insats när de blivit utsatta, oavsett var de bor. De här förseningarna tvingar brottsoffer till plågsamt långa väntetider och riskerar att de går miste om rättvisa. Viktiga bevis och vittnen kan förloras när det dröjer för länge – det är oacceptabelt. Inrikesministern måste fokusera på att göra basjobbet rätt, istället för ineffektiva initiativ.' En färsk regeringskampanj har återställt antalet poliser till över 2010 års nivå, men det finns oro för att det inte matchar befolkningsökningen och att många erfarna poliser har lämnat. Inrikesminister Suella Braverman säger att fler poliser ska förebygga våld, lösa inbrott och bekämpa antisocialt beteende. Braverman har infört nya riktlinjer som kräver att polisen följer alla rimliga spår i utredningar, eftersom det funnits oro för att inbrott och stölder prioriterats ner. Inrikesdepartementet understryker att alla polisdistrikt förväntas svara snabbt på 112-samtal och att ministern vill att polisen tillämpar nolltolerans mot brott. NPCC har 2022 lovat att poliser ska alltid åka ut vid inbrott, för att förbättra uppklarandet. Ändå lades 74,2 % av inbrottsärendena och 73,7 % av stölderna ner i fjol utan misstänkt. Omkring hälften av ärendena om våld i hemmet avskrevs på grund av bevisproblem, ofta då offret inte ville gå vidare. Labourpartiet har lovat att rekrytera ytterligare 13 000 närpoliser om de vinner nästa val.

article_content: For the third consecutive year, inflation-adjusted college tuition has declined. According to the newly released College Board report, 'Trends in College Pricing and Student Aid 2023,' average undergraduate tuition and fees rose by less than the rate of inflation (4.5%) for the 2023-24 academic year. In fact, after adjusting for inflation, average published tuition and fees decreased across all three major higher education sectors, marking the third year in a row of such declines.  Published Tuition Prices Before adjusting for inflation, average 2023-24 published tuition and fees for full-time college students increased. Over the past decade (2013-14 to 2023-24), however, inflation-adjusted tuition and fees decreased by 6% at public two-year colleges and 4% at public four-year institutions, while increasing by 5% at private nonprofit four-year schools.  State-by-State Tuition Differences The national average for in-state students at four-year public institutions was $11,260. Florida had the lowest average tuition and fees ($6,360), followed by Wyoming, North Carolina, Utah, and Montana. Vermont was the most expensive at $17,180, followed by New Hampshire, Connecticut, New Jersey, and Pennsylvania.  Compared to last year, average published four-year in-state tuition and fees didn’t increase in seven states and the District of Columbia and rose by less than 1% in six states (before inflation adjustment). For public two-year colleges, the national average was $3,990; California had the lowest in-district rate at $1,400, followed by New Mexico, North Carolina, Arizona, and Texas. Vermont had the highest average two-year college tuition at $8,660, with South Dakota, New Hampshire, Massachusetts, and Oregon following. From 2022-23 to 2023-24, published in-district tuition and fees at two-year colleges remained the same in 10 states and increased by less than 1% in five states (pre-inflation adjustment).  Net Tuition and Student Aid Although headline tuition prices are often high, most students pay a reduced—or net—price after grants and institutional aid. In 2022-23, full-time undergraduates received an average of $15,480 in financial aid: $10,680 in grants, $3,860 in federal loans, $850 in education tax credits and deductions, and $90 from Federal Work-Study programs.  Total Cost of College Tuition and fees are only part of the cost: students also pay for room, board, books, transportation, and personal expenses, making college overall an expensive undertaking.  Why Are Increases Small? Several factors have kept tuition increases minimal. Many colleges have frozen tuition to maintain accessibility, and some public colleges have been mandated not to raise tuition as part of state funding agreements. Additionally, declining undergraduate enrollment—accelerated by the Covid-19 pandemic—has prompted institutions to keep prices competitive.  Student Loans and Debt While student loan debt is still a concern, borrowing has declined for the 12th consecutive year. Students and parents took out $98.2 billion in loans in 2022-23, down from a peak of $152.8 billion (adjusted to 2022 dollars) in 2010-11. Federal loans per full-time equivalent (FTE) undergraduate dropped to $3,860 in 2022-23 from $6,970 in 2010-11. As of March 2023, 32% of borrowers owed less than $10,000; 21% owed between $10,000 and $20,000. Increased financial aid and fewer students enrolling have contributed to the decline in overall borrowing.  The Future Although inflation is still present, it has started to ease. With ongoing enrollment challenges and skepticism regarding the value of a college degree, most colleges are unlikely to raise tuition significantly in the near future. The increase in alternative educational providers has also intensified competition for students, making it probable that college will continue to be a buyer’s market.
translated_content: För tredje året i rad har den inflationsjusterade collegeavgiften minskat. Enligt College Boards nya rapport, 'Trender i collegepriser och studentstöd 2023', ökade den genomsnittliga grundutbildningsavgiften mindre än inflationen (4,5 %) under läsåret 2023-24. Faktum är att när inflationen räknas in har den genomsnittliga annonserade studieavgiften minskat inom alla tre huvudsakliga högskolesektorer, för tredje året i rad.  Publicerade studieavgifter Innan inflationen justeras, ökade de genomsnittliga publicerade studieavgifterna för heltidsstudenter under 2023-24. Över det senaste decenniet (2013-14 till 2023-24) har dock inflationsjusterade avgifter minskat med 6 % på offentliga tvååriga skolor och 4 % på offentliga fyraåriga institutioner, medan de ökat med 5 % på privata ideella fyraåriga skolor.  Skillnader i studieavgifter mellan delstater Det nationella genomsnittet för in-state-studenter vid offentliga fyraåriga skolor var $11,260. Florida hade de lägsta genomsnittliga avgifterna ($6,360), följt av Wyoming, North Carolina, Utah och Montana. Vermont var dyrast med $17,180, följt av New Hampshire, Connecticut, New Jersey och Pennsylvania.  Jämfört med förra året ökade de genomsnittliga publicerade fyraåriga in-state-avgifterna inte i sju delstater och District of Columbia och steg med mindre än 1 % i sex stater (före inflationsjustering). För offentliga tvååriga skolor var nationella genomsnittet $3,990; Kalifornien hade lägsta avgiften för lokalboende på $1,400, följt av New Mexico, North Carolina, Arizona och Texas. Vermont hade de högsta genomsnittliga tvååriga collegeavgifterna på $8,660, följt av South Dakota, New Hampshire, Massachusetts och Oregon. Mellan 2022-23 och 2023-24 låg de publicerade lokala studieavgifterna stilla i tio delstater och ökade med mindre än 1 % i fem stater (före inflationsjustering).  Nettoavgifter och studentstöd Även om rubrikens studieavgifter ofta är höga, betalar de flesta studenter ett reducerat nettobelopp efter bidrag och institutionellt stöd. Under 2022-23 fick heltidsstudenter i genomsnitt $15,480 i ekonomiskt stöd: $10,680 i bidrag, $3,860 i federala lån, $850 i utbildningsskatteavdrag och avdrag, samt $90 från Federal Work-Study-program.  Totalkostnad för college Studieavgifter är bara en del av kostnaden: studenter betalar även för boende, mat, böcker, transporter och personliga utgifter, vilket gör college sammantaget dyrt.  Varför är ökningen liten? Flera faktorer har hållit avgiftsökningarna små. Många skolor har fryst avgifterna för att behålla tillgängligheten, och vissa offentliga skolor har varit tvungna att inte höja avgifter som ett villkor för statligt stöd. Dessutom har minskad grundutbildningsinskrivning – påskyndad av covid-19 – drivit institutionerna att behålla konkurrenskraftiga priser.  Studielån och skulder Även om studieskulder fortfarande är ett bekymmer har utlåningen minskat för tolfte året i rad. Studenter och föräldrar tog ut $98,2 miljarder i lån under 2022-23, ned från en topp på $152,8 miljarder (i 2022 års dollar) 2010-11. Federala lån per heltidsstudent sjönk till $3,860 år 2022-23 från $6,970 år 2010-11. I mars 2023 hade 32 % av låntagarna mindre än $10,000 i skuld; 21 % hade mellan $10,000 och $20,000. Ökat ekonomiskt stöd och minskad inskrivning har bidragit till nedgången i det totala lånet.  Framtiden Även om inflationen består har den börjat avta. Med fortsatta inskrivningsutmaningar och en växande skepsis kring värdet av en högskoleexamen är det osannolikt att skolor höjer avgifterna nämnvärt på kort sikt. article_content: Technology continues to revolutionize wearable fashion, with products like smartwatches, augmented reality glasses, and electronic t-shirts. Now, a new innovation focuses on the fingertips: the fingernail.  Tokyo-based toy company Takara Tomy has unveiled LumiDecoNail, special LED stickers designed for fingernails. These stickers light up when they come close to NFC-enabled devices, such as compatible Android smartphones or electronic payment cards. The technology relies on Near Field Communication (NFC), wherein small amounts of power are transferred over short distances, making the LED blink when near a supported device.  Currently available exclusively in Japan, LumiDecoNail consists of a set of 16 nail stickers, with one containing the LED, retailing for 1,200 yen (approximately £7 or $12). The product is primarily targeted at young consumers and builds upon the trend of decorative manicure art, which features intricate nail designs and embellishments.  Company spokeswoman Misayo Aruga shared her experience, 'I am now wearing it on the middle finger of my right hand. It blinks whenever I pass through train gates, which lifts my heart a bit.'  While LumiDecoNail is only compatible with Android devices for now—leaving Apple users unable to use the product—the company has plans to consider international distribution if the product is well received in Japan.  Meanwhile, London-based CuteCircuit offers wearable technology in clothing, featuring LED lights woven into nylon ribbon to create outfits that light up, change color, or shimmer with an iPhone app. Their batteries are hidden as buttons or clasps, allowing the designs to remain fashionable and functional.

Nu har en ny innovation riktat sig till fingertopparna: nageln.  Det Tokyobaserade leksaksföretaget Takara Tomy har lanserat LumiDecoNail, speciella LED-klistermärken för naglar. Dessa lyser upp när de kommer nära NFC-aktiverade enheter, som kompatibla Android-smartphones eller elektroniska betalkort. Tekniken bygger på Near Field Communication (NFC), där små mängder energi överförs på korta avstånd och gör att LED-lampan blinkar i närheten av en stödd enhet.  LumiDecoNail finns för närvarande endast i Japan och består av ett set med 16 nagelklistermärken, varav ett innehåller LED-lampan, till ett pris av 1 200 yen (cirka 7 pund eller 12 dollar). Produkten riktar sig främst till unga konsumenter och bygger på trenden med dekorativ nagelkonst med intrikata designer och utsmyckningar.  Företagets talesperson Misayo Aruga berättar: 'Jag har den nu på mitt högra långfinger. Den blinkar varje gång jag passerar genom spärrarna på tågstationen, och det piggar upp mig lite.'  LumiDecoNail fungerar än så länge bara med Android-enheter—vilket innebär att Apple-användare inte kan använda produkten just nu—men företaget planerar att överväga internationell lansering om produkten blir populär i Japan.  Samtidigt erbjuder Londonbaserade CuteCircuit bärbar teknik i kläder, med LED-lampor invävda i nylonband. Plaggen kan lysa, byta färg eller glittra via en iPhone-app. Batterierna är dolda som knappar eller spännen, vilket gör att designen förblir både snygg och funktionell.

article_content: The UK's Serious Organised Crime Agency (Soca), often called 'Britain's FBI,' has refused to reveal which major companies hired corrupt private investigators, despite demands from Members of Parliament. Soca stated that releasing this information could harm the financial viability of these organisations by associating them with criminal activity. This decision to protect corporate reputations stands in stark contrast to law enforcement actions against newspapers for similar misconduct. A confidential and now leaked Soca report outlined illegal activities such as live telephone interceptions, computer hacking, police corruption, and obtaining itemized phone bills. Last month, Home Secretary Theresa May expressed concern after revelations implicated law firms and blue-chip companies in phone hacking, surveillance, and data theft through private investigators. According to the leaked report, those involved allegedly include a celebrity broadcaster, a corporate giant, and a wealthy businessman. Soca's chairman, Ian Andrews, informed MPs that the information had been formally classified, explaining that disclosure could jeopardize ongoing criminal investigations and breach the human rights of the businesses concerned. In response, Labour MP and home affairs select committee chair Keith Vaz said he would contact every FTSE 100 company and the top 100 legal firms to ask if they had employed private investigators and why. Mr. Vaz expressed disappointment that the committee once again had to receive a confidential document from Soca, emphasizing that transparency is key to public trust that no one is above the law and that Soca is actively addressing the issue. He also suggested that evidence may have been withheld from Parliament in an earlier investigation into private investigators.

Soca uppgav att ett avslöjande av denna information skulle kunna skada organisationernas ekonomiska ställning genom att koppla dem till kriminell verksamhet. Detta beslut att skydda företagens rykte står i stark kontrast till de rättsliga åtgärder som vidtagits mot tidningar för motsvarande överträdelser. En konfidentiell och nu läckt Soca-rapport beskrev olagliga aktiviteter såsom avlyssning av telefonsamtal, dataintrång, poliskorruption och att komma över specificerade telefonräkningar. Förra månaden uttryckte inrikesminister Theresa May oro efter avslöjanden där advokatbyråer och storföretag kopplats till telefonavlyssning, övervakning och dataintrång via privata utredare. Enligt den läckta rapporten är de inblandade bland annat en känd TV-profil, en storbolagsjätte och en förmögen affärsman. Soca:s ordförande Ian Andrews informerade parlamentsledamöterna om att informationen blivit formellt hemligstämplad och förklarade att ett avslöjande kan äventyra pågående brottsutredningar och bryta mot de berörda företagens mänskliga rättigheter. Som svar sade Labour-ledamoten Keith Vaz, ordförande i inrikesutskottet, att han kommer kontakta alla FTSE 100-bolag och de 100 största advokatbyråerna för att fråga om de anlitat privata utredare och varför. Vaz uttryckte besvikelse över att utskottet återigen fått ta emot ett hemligt dokument från Soca, och underströk att öppenhet är avgörande för att allmänheten ska kunna lita på att ingen står över lagen och att Soca verkligen hanterar problemet. Han antydde även att bevis kan ha undanhållits parlamentet vid en tidigare granskning av privata utredare.
